items.t: Tom Houck, civil rights activist and aide to Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., dies at 79
items.x: Tom Houck, a longtime civil rights activist who worked alongside Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. and spent more than six decades shaping Atlanta's political landscape and preserving its civil rights history, has died at 79. Houck died Thursday, October 22, from pneumonia, according to a close friend who spoke with The Atlanta Journal-Constitution. His passing marks the loss of another firsthand witness to the civil rights movement and a familiar voice in Atlanta politics. Born in Cambridge, Massachusetts, Houck became involved in the struggle for racial equality as a teenager. In 1965, he participated in the historic Selma-to-Montgomery voting rights march, an experience that helped define his lifelong commitment to activism. items.t: 2026 Brings Historic Opportunity For Eight Black Senators
items.x: By Kevin Harris, Guest Contributor For more than 150 years, the United States Senate has been one of the most powerful institutions in American democracy and one of the least representative of Black America. But the 2026 elections could bring a remarkable change. If Angie Nixon of Florida, Julianna Stratton of Illinois and Scott Colom of Mississippi win their competitive races for the United States Senate, they would join Cory Booker of New Jersey, Raphael Warnock of Georgia, Angela Alsobrooks of Maryland, Lisa Blunt Rochester of Delaware and Tim Scott of South Carolina for a historic total of eight African Americans simultaneously serving in the Senate. The Senate that once included lawmakers who defended slavery and segregation could welcome the largest contingent of Black senators in American history. However, she delayed its implementation until Friday (October 23) to give the administration an opportunity to appeal. items.t: Justice Department Plans Unprecedented Election Monitoring Operation Ahead of Midterms
items.x: The U.S. Department of Justice is preparing to deploy approximately 1,000 federal election monitors across all 50 states for the November 3 midterm elections, an unprecedented expansion of a longstanding federal oversight program that has raised concerns among civil rights organizations and state election officials. According to Reuters, the planned deployment would be the largest election monitoring operation in Justice Department history, involving roughly three times as many personnel as the previous midterm election. The department says its monitors will help ensure compliance with federal election laws, protect voter access and document potential violations. items.t: Georgia Surpasses One Million Early Votes as Midterm Election Approaches
items.x: More than one million Georgia voters have already cast their ballots in person ahead of the November 3 midterm election, putting the state ahead of its early voting pace four years ago and underscoring the importance of turnout in another consequential election cycle. items.x: A federal judge in Mississippi has rejected an effort by the Trump administration to shut down a lawsuit brought by the NAACP against Elon Musk’s artificial intelligence company, xAI, allowing a closely watched environmental justice case to continue. The lawsuit, filed by the national NAACP and its Mississippi State Conference, accuses xAI and its subsidiary, MZX Tech, of operating a gas-fired power plant in Southaven, Mississippi, without the environmental permits required under the Clean Air Act. The plant supplies power to xAI’s massive Colossus 2 data center, which supports the company’s artificial intelligence operations. The case has drawn attention because of the plant’s location near predominantly Black communities in North Mississippi and South Memphis. items.t: Federal Trial Begins For Buffalo Shooter Who Killed 10 Black People
items.x: Jury selection began Tuesday (October 13) in the federal hate crimes trial of Payton Gendron , who killed 10 Black people in a 2022 shooting at a Buffalo supermarket. He could face the death penalty if convicted. According to the Associated Press , Gendron, now 23, is already serving life in prison without the possibility of parole after pleading guilty to state murder charges in 2023. He has pleaded not guilty to federal hate crime and firearms charges, though his defense team does not dispute his guilt. The Justice Department decided in January 2024 to seek the death penalty. Prosecutors also rejected Gendron’s offer to plead guilty in the federal case in exchange for a life sentence. items.x: Former Dallas police officer Amber Guyger was released from a Texas prison Friday (October 16) after serving seven years of her 10-year sentence for murdering Botham Jean in his apartment in 2018. NBC News reported that Guyger was scheduled to leave prison Friday, nearly three years before her sentence was set to expire. The Texas Board of Pardons and Paroles approved her release after she served seven years of her sentence. The parole board cited Guyger’s prison conduct, lack of a documented pattern of violent criminal behavior, and completion of rehabilitation programs designed to help her find and maintain employment, according to NBC Dallas-Fort Worth . The board denied her first parole request in 2024. Guyger, 38, was convicted of murder in October 2019 for fatally shooting Jean, a 26-year-old Black accountant. items.t: Black Household Wealth Plummeted 25% In Three Years, New Data Shows
items.x: Median wealth among Black households fell 25% between 2022 and 2025, widening the racial wealth gap even as White, Hispanic, and Asian households saw their median net worth increase, according to a new analysis of Federal Reserve data. Center for Economic and Policy Research (CEPR) director of race and economic justice, Algernon Austin, shared in an analysis published Tuesday (October 13) that median wealth among Black households fell from $49,100 in 2022 to $36,800 in 2025, a 25% decline. In comparison, median wealth reached $332,100 for White households, $79,600 for Hispanic households, and $677,600 for Asian households in 2025, according to CEPR. While Black households lost wealth, these groups saw their median wealth increase between 2022 and 2025. items.t: Marilyn Mosby’s Mortgage Fraud Conviction Dismissed, Perjury Convictions Stand
items.x: Former Baltimore City State’s Attorney Marilyn Mosby ’s mortgage fraud conviction has been dismissed after federal prosecutors decided not to retry her, allowing her to keep the Florida vacation home at the center of the case. Her two federal perjury convictions, however, remain in place. According to WBAL-TV , prosecutors decided not to retry Mosby after the Fourth U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals overturned her mortgage fraud conviction in July 2025. The appeals court found that the trial judge gave jurors incorrect instructions about where the alleged crime occurred. Mosby was convicted of mortgage fraud in February 2024 after prosecutors accused her of misrepresenting the source of $5,000 used toward the purchase of a Florida condo to obtain a more favorable mortgage rate. She maintained that the money was a gift from her then-husband, former Baltimore City Council President Nick Mosby.

The allegations center on whether Omar was listed as 17 rather than 18 when her father applied for citizenship, potentially allowing her to obtain citizenship through him. Omar arrived in the United States in 1995 after fleeing Somalia’s civil war and spending four years in a refugee camp in Kenya. She became a U.S. citizen in 2000 and has denied committing immigration fraud. The investigation follows a Monday (October 12) search of Omar’s Washington, D.C., home by federal agents. items.x: More than half a dozen Charlotte-Mecklenburg Police Department officers have been recommended for termination or have resigned after an investigation uncovered alleged racist text messages, including discussions about a competition to see who could pull over the most Black drivers, according to WBTV . The messages surfaced during a North Carolina State Bureau of Investigation probe into Officer Seth Elliott ’s alleged misuse of Flock Safety, a network of license plate-reading cameras. Investigators downloaded text messages and other data from Elliott’s phone and turned the material over to CMPD, which launched its own internal investigation. items.t: Breast Cancer Awareness Month: What Black Women Need to Know
items.x: October is Breast Cancer Awareness Month, an annual campaign dedicated to honoring those we've lost, encouraging breast cancer screenings, raising awareness about the disease and supporting research. In support of this mission, the Black Information Network is taking a closer look at how breast cancer affects our communities and sharing resources that center our unique experiences. Breast cancer is the second-leading cause of cancer-related deaths among women in the United States and the leading cause of cancer deaths among Black women, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention . While Black women are diagnosed with breast cancer slightly less often than white women, they are 38% more likely to die from the disease, according to the American Cancer Society. These disparities highlight ongoing differences in access to early detection, quality treatment and medical care.

Mari Richardson told Cleveland CBS affiliate WOIO that her daughter, Tiyonna, arrived home in a stranger’s car about 20 minutes before she had expected the school bus to bring her back. Richardson said she was still at home when the woman arrived with the child. The woman, identified as Tiyonna Betts, told WOIO she noticed the girl alone and visibly distressed near the road and decided to intervene. items.t: Black unemployment is nearing twice the white rate. Economists say America should pay attention
items.x: Black workers are once again feeling economic instability first as Trump administration job cuts and a stagnant labor market add pressure. Black unemployment under the second Trump administration has been bumpy, to say the least. While the jobless rate among Black Americans has seen a low of 6%, it has also seen highs not seen since the COVID-19 pandemic at 8.2% Last month, the Black unemployment rate jumped back to 7% , a full percentage point higher than the prior month. That is highest increase since the start of the pandemic in 2020. The steadily increasing rate of Black people who can't find work is both historically familiar and a potential warning for the broader economy. "The adage goes, when the economy gets the cold, Black America gets the flu. items.x: In this interview, the multidisciplinary artist on the rise opens up about the themes in her work, her virality, motherhood, and more. Smith does not shy away from sharing his opinion, and most recently, the ESPN host brought his concerns directly to President Donald Trump. items.t: Russell Wilson and Ciara join QALO as co-owners in health tech investment

Russell Wilson and Ciara are adding wearable health technology to their growing business portfolio after joining QALO as co-owners and investors. Announced October 20, 2026, the partnership will see the couple work with company executives on product development, marketing and future growth. QALO launched in 2013 with silicone wedding rings designed for people with active lifestyles. According to press release via Business Wire , both devices track sleep, physical activity, stress and recovery without requiring a monthly subscription. Users can also switch between the ring and wristband while keeping their information connected through one platform.

For Black people, protest isn’t a tactic borrowed from abroad, but rather an inheritance. items.t: What We Need to Know: Historic Senate Bids, NASCAR Deal & Birmingham Crime Drop
items.x: Across politics, business, and community safety, Black Americans are making history on multiple fronts. items.t: 3 men extradited to Milwaukee over $17 million in cocaine
items.x: Three Mexican nationals who served as crew on a U.S.-flagged vessel have been extradited from Costa Rica to Wisconsin to face federal drug charges. Prosecutors say Costa Rican authorities seized about 840 kilograms of cocaine from the boat in April 2025 and valued it at more than $17 million. The men made their first court appearance in Milwaukee on Oct. 19, 2026, and a judge ordered them held without bail pending trial. What authorities say happened Costa Rican authorities intercepted the vessel, the My Lisa Too, near Quepos on the country’s Pacific coast on April 15, 2025. Officials said the cocaine was hidden inside the boat, and they arrested the three crew members. A federal indictment filed in May 2025 charges the men with conspiring to possess cocaine with intent to distribute while aboard a U.S. vessel. A second count alleges the same possession on the day of the seizure. googlet

items.x: Walonza Lee is the Executive Director of the South Side Heroin Opioid Task Force in Chicago. She has worked in the substance use and mental health field for 39 years, and her husband, Benny Lee, is a longtime Chicago activist. Lee developed the first program of its kind for women coming home from the penitentiary who were still serving time with their babies. What is the South Side Heroin Opioid Task Force? The South Side Heroin Opioid Task Force focuses on reducing the number of opioid fatalities and overdoses on the South Side of Chicago. We have been in existence since 2020, and since we first started, we have reduced overdose fatalities by 11%. The "Act 1: Kokura Story Trailer" arrived Friday, October 16. It shows the bond between Snoop's character, Orpheus, and the game's young lead, Makoto Daito, through a music lesson. items.x: D’Angelo left behind a vault of unreleased music and his family is now preparing a posthumous album that could extend the late soul legend's musical legacy well beyond his death. The announcement comes from his older brother Luther Archer, who confirmed during an interview with Kiss Richmond that a new project is being assembled with six tracks identified so far. The family is also considering additional releases that could include rare recordings, B-sides and an entire collection of cover songs. "We've got an album coming out," Archer said. "There are six tracks [so far]. But then we have a whole vault of music that's never been released." Perhaps the most tantalizing revelation involves a previously unreleased recording featuring D’Angelo, Michael Jackson and Mary J. Blige. items.x: Two reports of stabbings near Los Angeles’ Taste of Soul drew a police response on Saturday (October 17). The free Crenshaw festival stayed open and ended on time, its team said. The festival’s team told ABC7 that police activity took place outside the grounds. “Police activity happened on the outskirts of the event,” they said. The first call came in around 2:45 p.m. near Crenshaw and Martin Luther King Jr. boulevards. LAPD Officer Charles Miller told City News Service that a group had been in a fight. At least one person reportedly had a stab wound. Those involved had left by the time police reached the scene. Police checked hospitals to try to find a victim. LAPD’s press team later said police found two people at a hospital. They spoke with them and took assault-with-a-deadly-weapon reports over cuts. Their condition was not known. Speaking at a New York Comic Con panel for "NCIS: New York," the 58-year-old rapper put his share at 80 to 90 percent, People reported . “I do 80 or 90 percent of my stunts,” he said. LL praised Lee's drive to make screen action convincing. He also credited stunt performer Brennan Dyson, joking that some especially punishing hits called for a double. The same commitment had shaped his work on "NCIS: Los Angeles" years earlier. In a 2011 interview, LL said doing the physical work showed his investment in Sam and gave viewers a more direct experience. items.t: 50 Cent’s "Street Fighter" Tops Box Office With $31 Million Debut
items.x: 50 Cent landed at the top of the box office with “Street Fighter,” which opened to an estimated $31 million in the United States and Canada. The Paramount release took first place across 3,575 theaters, according to Sunday studio estimates reported by The Associated Press. International ticket sales added about $20 million, bringing its worldwide opening to roughly $51 million. Box-office tracker The Numbers listed $13 million for Friday and $10.8 million for Saturday, with Sunday estimated at $7.2 million. AP said men made up 69% of the audience. The film arrived in U.S. theaters on October 16 with 50 playing Balrog, the boxer from Capcom’s fighting games. Director Kitao Sakurai’s take put the characters in 1993, with Ryu and Ken drawn back into combat after Chun-Li recruited them for the World Warrior Tournament. The two will serve as team captains alongside birthFUND founder Elaine Welteroth at the November 28 event, People reported . Both already support the nonprofit as family funders. The new role brings them to a community walk in the neighborhood where Knowles ran Headliners, the hair salon tied to Destiny’s Child’s beginnings. “Every mother deserves to feel safe, supported and seen when she brings life into the world,” Rowland told People. Knowles added, “Third Ward helped me raise my girls.” birthFUND’s program helps families pay for birth care. Its need-based grants cover perinatal care and midwifery support. items.x: Katt Williams said Black films face tight limits in Hollywood, and he wants his own studio to help change that. In a new USA TODAY interview , the comic laid out the thinking behind Kemet Movie Works, his film venture in Alabama. “Nobody needs a complainer, even if they're correct,” Williams said. “So I can talk blue in the face about what I don't like about Hollywood.” He said those complaints should lead him to act once he has a chance to do so. He also said Black films face tighter bounds on the stories they can tell than other films do. His memoir recounts two times he turned down deals worth millions on principle, USA TODAY reported. He said the business too often loses sight of the people who pay to watch. The studio effort has a home at Fort McClellan in Anniston, Alabama. Celebrity manicurist Dawn Sterling connected the producer with someone at the home brand, he revealed in a Wallpaper interview about the collection's origins . That introduction led to trips to Chicago to study fabrics and help shape Casa Dean. "That took being open-minded and not just coming in with the fake celebrity energy. Method Man still questioned how his work became part of the project. He said he had not known the plan when he recorded his songs and might have contributed more had he understood it. The rapper revisited son Riot's Copenhagen stage appearance in a new Rolling Stone interview . items.x: Snoop Dogg taught Phonixthecool how to earn from music he owned while Death Row Records developed the Durban rapper, the artist said. He said the goal was to keep an audience and build a catalog that could earn more once the label's releases drew new listeners. The rapper, born Lunga Khumalo, also described the work behind a signing: trying out producers and recording to find the right fit for his voice. Alicia Keys still holds the overall lead with 14 No. 1s. Wilson had reached 11 with "Keep Me In Love" in October 2025. She again credited a county commissioner with making the video and said her campaign shared it because she thought it was fun. She also denied that she had played down his part in its success. "I have never once understated his importance in the genesis of Power,'" she said. Their roles were clear when Starz first picked up the show in 2013. Kemp created the crime drama and took on the job of showrunner, while 50 joined as an executive producer. items.x: Mercury retrograde begins today, Oct. 24, 2026, and runs through Nov. 13. Astrologers say the planet stations retrograde at about 21 degrees Scorpio and turns direct at 5 degrees Scorpio. Mercury doesn’t actually move backward. It only appears to from Earth as the two planets’ orbits line up, but astrologers treat the period as a time to slow down and review communication, technology, travel and contracts. This one doesn’t arrive alone. Venus has been retrograde since Oct. 3 and stays that way until Nov. 13. items.t: Philly Flannel Fest returns with a bigger bash this Sunday
items.x: Flannel season is in full swing in Philadelphia, and one of the city’s favorite autumn gatherings is ready for its latest round. items.t: Stroke warning signs, how BE FAST could save a life
items.x: The main stroke warning signs come on suddenly. They include loss of balance, vision changes, a drooping face, weakness in an arm or leg, slurred speech, numbness, confusion, trouble understanding words and a sudden, severe headache. Doctors use the acronym BE FAST to remember the most urgent ones. If you notice any of them, call 911 right away. For Black Americans, knowing these signs is not optional. items.t: Bully Lifestyle creator Demetrius A. Matthews on what makes a bulldog’s bloodline valuable
items.x: Demetrius A. Matthews has bred and shown bulldogs for two decades. items.t: Trump Sues Alaska To Stop A Senate Election If His Guy Loses
items.x: Source: In what can only be called one of the greatest trolls in American history, a man named Dan Sullivan entered Alaska’s Senate race knowing he shared the name of Republican incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan. The confusion is brilliant. The only problem is that the Trump administration has preemptively filed a lawsuit to block certification of Alaska’s Senate election if Sen. Dan Sullivan loses, because apparently the Senate balance of power is so precarious that a man with the wrong Dan Sullivan on his ballot might accidentally turn the whole thing blue. The Justice Department lawsuit argues that including Daniel J. Sullivan on the ballot could confuse voters and undermine the election’s legitimacy. items.t: What Is The History Of Soul Food? How Black People Shaped Southern Cuisine
items.x: Source: Carmen K Sisson / Getty Few cuisines tell a story as powerful as soul food. From crispy fried chicken and smoky collard greens to buttery cornbread and sweet potato pie, these beloved dishes represent far more than what lands on the dinner table. They tell a story of African heritage, survival, creativity, resistance, family and the generations of Black Americans who transformed limited resources into a rich culinary tradition. Understanding the history of soul food means looking beyond the recipes to the people who created them, the circumstances that shaped them and the communities that continue to keep them alive. The origins of soul food are rooted in hardship, but its legacy is one of cultural pride, innovation and joy. items.t: Protecting The Family Home Takes More Than A Promise
items.x: By Jehan Crump-Gibson, Esq. “Grandma always said we would get the house.” Families often share some version of that statement with me after a loved one dies. They say it with conviction. But often, that promise is not reflected in the legal documents needed to carry it out. A promise made at the kitchen table does not transfer ownership of a home. When a homeowner dies without valid legal documents directing how the property will pass, state law determines who inherits . Especially in larger families, several relatives may inherit shares of the same home. That shared ownership can complicate decisions about selling, refinancing, or paying for major repairs. items.x: Intraoperative radiation therapy (IORT) costs cancer patients less time and money in treatment and is less invasive compared to traditional radiation treatments for breast cancer. Access, however, is limited in the United States. The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved IORT in 1999. It’s a treatment that involves just a single dose of radiation to a patient’s breast tissue after surgery, compared to whole or partial breast radiation treatments that often require multiple sessions and more money. IORT is not recommended for every breast cancer patient. It’s an excellent option for candidates who are postmenopausal with an early-stage diagnosis, very small tumors, and no evidence of lymph node involvement. items.x: A new study shows that consuming ultraprocessed foods (UPFs) could be detrimental for Black breast cancer survivors. The study, published in the January issue of eClinicalMedicine , reveals that high consumption could adversely affect breast cancer prognosis. Their teams had merged and while each of them had previously owned a piece of work on their old team, no one had mapped who would own what after the teams combined. items.t: Corporate Board Diversity Just Hit A Decade Low

The Gender Diversity Index™ published by 50/50 Women on Boards found that women held 29.2% of Russell 3000 board seats in the second quarter of 2026, down from 30.1% a year earlier. It marks the first annual decline in women’s representation on those boards in more than a decade , even as new board appointments rose 4.1% to 2,440. In other words, the talent pool did not disappear. The allocation of opportunities changed. items.t: Global Breast Cancer Cases To Impact Over 3.5 Million Women By 2050
items.x: New research has determined that breast cancer rates are on the rise for women globally. CNN reported that breast cancer rates are expected to hit a new peak, estimated to reach more than 3.5 million cases by 2050. However, this is mainly due to gaps in medical equity between high- and low-earning countries. What does the research say? While high-earning countries have seen a decline in breast cancer mortality, mainly due to investment in screening, prevention, and treatment, those in the global south have seen the opposite impact. Residents of high-income countries saw a 30% decline in deaths from breast cancer from 1990 to 2023. For those living in the lowest-income countries, breast cancer-induced deaths have increased by 99% within the same 30-year timeframe. items.t: Happy 65th Birthday To SEEN The "Godfather of Graffiti"
items.x: Happy birthday to Richard “SEEN” Mirando, widely regarded as the godfather of graffiti, who turns 64 years old today. Born October 17, 1961 in the Bronx, SEEN was one of the earliest artists to bring aerosol art out of the shadows of subway tunnels and freight yards and into the global spotlight. His work helped elevate graffiti from misunderstood vandalism to a respected art movement that now lives in galleries, museums, fashion, film, and mainstream culture. SEEN began tagging New York City trains in 1973 and quickly gained a reputation as one of the most fearless and skilled writers of his era. His full-car masterpieces, wild style lettering, and bold cartoon imagery defined the golden era of subway art in the late 70s and early 80s. Back For The First Time arrived during a transitional era in rap, a moment when Southern artists were still fighting for industry respect. Ludacris kicked the door off the hinges with his animated delivery, sharp comedic timing, and rowdy charisma that made him stand out from his peers immediately. items.t: Avi Hirschfield Sues Drake and UMG Over Alleged Copyright Infringement on “Janice STFU”
items.x: Grammy-winning songwriter Avi Hirschfield has filed a copyright infringement lawsuit against Drake and Universal Music Group (UMG), alleging that the rapper’s hit “ Janice STFU ” uses his original chorus without credit or compensation. Hirschfield, known for co-writing Drake’s “Heated” on Beyoncé’s Renaissance , claims he created and recorded vocals, lyrics, and a melody in early January 2026 over instrumental tracks from producers FnZ, consisting of Michael Mulé and Isaac De Boni. He says he shared the completed recording with the producers and other Drake collaborators but received no response. According to the allegations, Hirschfield heard “ Janice STFU ” on Apple Music around May 15 and recognized his chorus, which he says matched his work word-for-word and note-for-note. Hirschfield alleges that metadata-backed stems support his claim that he composed and recorded the chorus first.

items.t: Joony Returns With New 15-Track Album STILL HERE'
items.x: Grammy-nominated rapper, songwriter, and producer Joony has released STILL HERE, a 15-track, genre-bending project showcasing his growth as an independent artist. The DMV-bred musician’s latest full-length release follows MEMENTO and his Jordan Ward-assisted EP, JRNY. Opening with “YES MA’AM,” the album balances upbeat moments with introspective songs addressing loss, fame, finances, drugs, relationships, and the challenges of navigating the music industry. Tracks including “FTD,” “THANOS,” and the title track “STILL HERE” highlight Joony’s evolution, while “CAN’T GO BACK” closes the project. Since his previous album, Joony earned an RIAA Gold plaque for “Paper Soldiers” with Brent Faiyaz and received a Grammy nomination for his contributions as a writer on Destin Conrad’s Love On Digital. He has also performed on COLORS and toured alongside Blxst, Leon Thomas, Lil Tjay, and Lancey Foux.

items.t: Today In Hip Hop History: Nas Released His Debut Single "Halftime" 34 Years Ago
items.x: On this date in 1992, a young Queensbridge lyricist named Nasir Jones, known then as Nasty Nas, released his debut single "Halftime", marking the beginning of one of the most celebrated careers in Hip Hop history. Today marks the 33rd anniversary of that release, a moment that quietly changed the direction of rap in the 1990s. Halftime first appeared on the soundtrack of the independent film Zebrahead , long before Illmatic was even announced. At the time, Nas was still an underground phenomenon known for his guest verse on Main Source’s "Live at the Barbeque". But once Halftime dropped, it became clear to anyone paying attention that a new elite voice in Hip Hop had arrived. His flow was razor-sharp, his rhyme patterns unmatched, and his confident delivery revealed a teenager already rhyming on a master level. items.x: On this date in 2025, the music world lost one of its most gifted and influential artists when Michael Eugene Archer, better known to millions as D'Angelo, passed away at the age of 51 following a battle with pancreatic cancer. His death marked the loss of a musical visionary whose contributions to R&B, Hip Hop and soul music helped redefine the sound of Black music for an entire generation. Born February 11, 1974, in Richmond, Virginia, D'Angelo was much more than a singer. He was a pianist, songwriter, producer, arranger and multi-instrumentalist whose musical foundation was deeply rooted in the Black church. His ability to blend gospel, funk, jazz, classic soul and Hip Hop production techniques helped usher in the neo-soul movement of the 1990s, placing him alongside artists such as Erykah Badu, Maxwell, Lauryn Hill and Jill Scott as architects of a new musical era. items.t: The Baby On The Ready To Die' Album Was Not Notorious B.I.G., Was Only Paid $150 For 2-Hour Photo Shoot
items.x: One of the most recognizable album covers in Hip Hop history features a baby sitting against a plain white background, sporting an unmistakable Afro and staring directly into the camera. For more than three decades, the artwork for The Notorious B.I.G.'s 1994 debut album, Ready to Die , has remained synonymous with the Brooklyn MC's legacy. However, contrary to what some fans have believed over the years, the child pictured on the cover wasn't a young Christopher Wallace. His name is Keithroy Yearwood, and his contribution to the legendary album reportedly earned him just $150. Yearwood, who was born in the Bronx to Jamaican parents, was reportedly discovered through a modeling agency when he was an infant. items.x: Finding a job in 2026 is tougher than the headlines suggest. Employers added 162,000 jobs in August, but the gains were uneven, and Black unemployment still sat at 6%, well above the 4.1% national rate. Candidates are actively looking for an edge. In this article, we’ll discern how to know which ones actually deliver. items.x: Source: Prince Williams / ATLPics.Net Offset is spreading the love, one Walmart bouquet at a time. The Atlanta rapper stopped by a Walmart on Wednesday, Oct. 21, and surprised unsuspecting women and employees with flowers and uplifting messages. Apparently, somebody decided it was time to give the ladies their flowers — literally. items.t: Two Unglamorous Decisions That Shape a Music Business in LA
items.x: A vintage analog synth can survive thirty years of touring and still die in one August afternoon inside a Van Nuys garage. Heat warps cases, humidity gets into pots and faders, and a single voice-card repair can eat what a month of session work paid. Plenty of LA producers, engineers, and gigging players learn this the expensive way. The ones who build lasting businesses usually sort out two dull things early: where the equipment lives, and how the money comes in. Your Apartment Is Not a Warehouse Space here is priced like a luxury, and musicians feel it first. A one-bedroom in Highland Park might fit a modest home studio, but not the PA you rent out on weekends, the road cases, and the drum kit you keep meaning to sell. So the gear spreads. Into the car. Three years later, the Bronx-born beatmaker's contributions to the culture remain undeniable, with a catalog that helped shape the sound of Hip Hop's Golden Era and produced some of the most recognizable records in rap history. Born Mark Howard James on October 16, 1961, in the Bronx, New York, The 45 King passed away on October 19, 2023, just three days after celebrating his 62nd birthday. His passing was announced by fellow legendary producer DJ Premier, who paid tribute to the man whose musical contributions helped open doors for countless artists and producers throughout the industry. items.t: Hip-Hop Heavyweights Fabolous, Maino, Dave East, and Jim Jones Toast to One Year of Let’s Rap About It in NYC

Held at Queens restaurant and lounge Partake NYC, the celebration brought together fans, industry tastemakers, and fellow hip-hop veterans for a night filled with classic New York energy and undeniable culture. Curated as an extension of the show itself, the evening delivered a family-style atmosphere that showcased the four hosts' natural chemistry. The milestone event featured live on-stage commentary, an exclusive merchandise drop, and a fan meet-and-greet. Guests turned out in statement footwear—ranging from fresh kicks and stilettos to the now-infamous "kitten heels," a nod to one of the podcast's most viral debates regarding whether low heels belong in the club. items.t: NBA and Sportsbooks Restrict High-Risk Betting Markets Ahead of 2026-27 Season
items.x: The NBA and major sportsbooks are tightening restrictions on high-risk betting markets ahead of the 2026-27 season, targeting wagers that could offer significant payouts on specific in-game outcomes. The updated rules restrict bets on individual plays, opening-tip results, and player statistical unders. Additional limitations apply to unders on players expected to play fewer than 12 minutes, as well as parlays combining these types of wagers. The restrictions will also extend to the 2027 WNBA season, expanding the measures across both professional basketball leagues. The move comes amid several gambling investigations involving NBA players, including Jontay Porter, Terry Rozier, and Malik Beasley. items.t: Surveillance pricing comes into focus in some midterm campaigns
items.x: WASHINGTON, D.C. (NEXSTAR) A stalled effort to block companies from using AI to set prices is gaining new attention on the campaign trail. As Democrats put affordability front and center in their campaigns, there's one issue some candidates are focused on: personalized prices. Personalized pricing, which is also called surveillance pricing, is when companies use your personal data to determine how much you pay for their products or services. That means you could pay more than someone else for the same item. "The number of people who come up to me and say, Gosh, Mark, I saw your ad, and that's crazy,'" said Sen. Mark Warner (D-Virginia), who is running for reelection this year. Warner has proposed a federal ban on surveillance pricing. "This is the kind of part where technology gets creepy," Warner said. items.t: Police say 2 teen girls arrested in Southern California school shooting plot may have been seeking revenge
items.x: Two 15-year-old girls arrested in connection with an alleged mass shooting plot at Corona High School in Riverside County may have been seeking revenge, police revealed in an interview with KTLA Wednesday. The teenagers allegedly spent months researching previous school shootings, investigating how to obtain firearms and discussing how they would enter the campus to carry out the attack. "They were trying to make specific plans as to how they were going to carry out this revenge-based attack," Corona Police Department Lt. Robert Montanez told KTLA. "This was not joking around. This was not a one-off conversation," Montanez said. He said the girls had moved beyond simply discussing the possibility of an attack and were working through specific details of how they would carry it out. "The level and timeline of communication, which spanned several months, is very concerning," Montanez said.

items.t: Major Los Angeles thoroughfare to get 12-mile dedicated bus lane
items.x: One of the L.A.’s busiest streets is getting a dedicated lane to speed up service. Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass and other officials unveiled the Vermont Bus Rapid Transit Corridor project on Wednesday, which will create a 12.4-mile dedicated bus lane connecting South Los Angeles and Los Feliz via Vermont Avenue. “[It] will provide residents with a faster, safer, more affordable option,” city officials said in a media statement. Over 38,000 people use the Metro routes that run along Vermont Avenue every day: local service Metro Line 204 and Metro Rapid 754 – both of which run from Sunset Boulevard in Hollywood to 120 th Street in South L.A. That daily figure equates to about 11 million riders per year, Metro CEO Stephanie Wiggins said. items.t: Long Beach fortifies battered coastline as city braces for incoming storm
items.x: Wet weather has returned to Southern California as coastal communities brace for another round of potential flooding and beach erosion from an incoming El Niño-driven storm . Crews preparing the already-battered coastline in Long Beach said they hope it's in a better position Wednesday than it was several weeks ago, with all of the damage that has occurred in the region. With another round of powerful surf around the corner, crews are dredging 415,000 cubic yards of sand from the ocean floor, pushing it back onto areas along the heavily-eroded Peninsula. A series of recent powerful storms broke up sections of the boardwalk, damaged the sea wall and destroyed several beachfront homes. VATICAN CITY (AP) — Pope Leo XIV needs no further treatment for lung cancer after follow-up tests confirmed the disease was localized, the Vatican said in a statement Wednesday. Leo, 71, had the lower lobe of his right lung removed last week in the first major health event of his 17-month pontificate. The surgery confirmed he had adenocarcinoma , the most common type of lung cancer. He left the hospital on Saturday, four days after surgery and well ahead of the week-long hospital stay the Vatican had initially anticipated. items.t: Here’s the upside of a potentially historic El Niño in California
items.x: A potentially historic El Niño could bring some much-needed benefits to California this winter, including increased rainfall, improved reservoir levels, and a healthier mountain snowpack after years of drought concerns. A “super” El Niño continues to gain strength, according to The Hill. If the climate phenomenon continues to build at this pace, it could become the strongest El Niño we’ve seen in more than 75 years. Forecasters predict much of California could see above-average precipitation and temperatures this winter. It’s unclear how the weather things will pan out this fall and winter, but similar events in past El Niño years have brought torrential downpours, coastal flooding, mudslides, power outages, and giant waves. items.t: Judge orders Meta to pay New Mexico $25B in Cambridge Analytica case
items.x: ( The Hill ) – A judge in New Mexico ordered the technology giant Meta to pay $25 billion after a jury found the company liable for misleading users about its privacy and content policies. New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez (D) announced the judge's order Wednesday, calling it "one of the single largest, if not the largest, single state verdict against the company in American history." "Today's judgement from a state, which admittedly is not very big in terms of population, should be a clear warning to everyone in Big Tech, Mr. [Mark] Zuckerberg, Meta, social media companies, indeed AI companies," Torrez said at a press conference. items.t: Frelick and Pratt lift Brewers to 5-4 comeback win over Rays and 2-0 World Series lead

Tampa Bay, which won the AL pennant by forcing opponents into mistakes, committed one error, made two other misplays that could have been charged as errors and had a runner thrown out at the plate. Down 4-0 in the first inning, Milwaukee rallied for its seventh comeback win of this postseason. The Brewers also rebounded from a 4-0 deficit to beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 6-4 in Game 4 of the NL Championship Series, completing a four-game sweep. items.x: The chief executive of Six Flags says the company will install seat belts on the Georgia roller coaster from which a rider fell to his death earlier this month. The company's rides with similar restraints will also get the safety upgrade. The theme park operator announced the extra safeguard less than two weeks after 42-year-old Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem of Atlanta died after being ejected from his seat on the Goliath coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia. “We are reinforcing safety precautions at our parks and taking additional measures, including adding seat belts on Goliath and other coasters with a similar restraint,” John Reilly, president and CEO of Six Flags Entertainment Corporation, said in a statement Friday. items.x: WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. (AP) — President Donald Trump cast his ballot in the midterm elections Saturday, saying he voted for all Republicans in Florida before speaking at a Georgia rally. Trump and first lady Melania Trump arrived at their West Palm Beach polling location at the Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections office together after the president spent the morning at his nearby golf course. items.x: RIVERVIEW, Fla. (WFLA) — A young man was arrested Thursday afternoon after deputies said they spotted him driving a stolen car in Riverview. According to the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office, detectives found a suspected stolen car near Bloomingdale Avenue and Watson Road just after 1:30 p.m. Detectives tracked the vehicle to Duncan Road, where the driver, Anthoni Williams, 19, parked and walked toward an apartment complex on Zackary Circle. Video released by the sheriff's office on Saturday showed Williams attempting to run as deputies approached him, but he was quickly detained. The suspect was arrested on the following charges: Grand theft motor vehicle, Criminal mischief ($1,000 or more), Failure to obey written promise to appear (FTA – Loitering or Prowling), Felony fleeing to elude, No valid driver’s license, Reckless driving.

items.t: Understanding CPO cars: What does certified pre-owned mean?
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) With new-car prices near record highs, certified pre-owned vehicles (CPOs) offer buyers an affordable alternative to buying new, along with additional inspections and warranty protection. What Does Certified Pre-Owned Mean? If you’re shopping for a car, you’ve likely come across CPO vehicles. But what does that mean exactly, and how do they differ from traditional used cars? A certified pre-owned car is a used vehicle that meets the age, mileage, and condition requirements of a manufacturer or dealer certification program. CPO cars undergo a multipoint inspection and generally include additional warranty coverage, though the coverage and certification standards vary by program. Many CPO vehicles also include benefits such as roadside assistance, access to a loaner vehicle, and trip interruption coverage. items.t: Early voting surges in battleground states as Democrats outpace GOP gains
items.x: Early voting is surging in several key battleground states, giving Democrats hope that their strength in midterm polling could translate into a turnout advantage in November. In North Carolina, more than 1.2 million early ballots have been accepted, a 37 percent increase from the same point leading up to the 2022 midterms, according to an analysis released Friday by Catawba College political scientist Michael Bitzer. That growth — which includes both in-person and mail-in ballots — has been driven by a 47 percent increase among registered Democrats and a 60 percent increase in participation among unaffiliated voters. Early voting among Republicans is up 2.6 percent. Similar patterns are emerging elsewhere, with high turnout especially pronounced in historically Republican-leaning states with competitive Senate races this cycle. DeLuca's strikeout came after Tampa Bay's Liam Hicks had hit into an apparent game-ending double play that was overturned after a replay review. The review determined that Brewers shortstop Cooper Pratt's right foot was slightly off the bag when he caught a throw from second baseman Brice Turang. Jacob Misiorowski allowed one run over five innings to earn the win. Christian Yelich hit an RBI triple to spark a two-run rally in the first inning that put the Brewers ahead for good and delighted a sellout crowd reveling in Milwaukee’s first World Series game since 1982. items.t: Brewers’ Jacob Misiorowski sets World Series velocity record on his first pitch
items.x: MILWAUKEE (AP) — Jacob Misiorowski broke the record for fastest World Series pitch with the very first offering of this year's Fall Classic, a 103.5 mph fastball from the Milwaukee Brewers' fireballer to the Tampa Bay Rays' Yandy Díaz on Friday night. Aroldis Chapman of the Chicago Cubs set the mark for a Series pitcher at 103.2 mph in the ninth inning of Game 2 in 2016, an offering that resulted in a groundout to second by Cleveland's Coco Crisp. Misiorowski's first pitch, taken for a ball above the strike zone, was listed at 103.4 mph on the stadium video boards but clocked at 103.5 by MLB's Statcast system. Misiorowski's first 10 pitches to the Rays were fastballs, including two hit for singles. Omar’s Washington home was raided by federal immigration authorities Oct. 12 as part of a criminal investigation into her immigration status. items.t: Florida Rep. says constituent arrested after making threat on his life
items.x: Rep. Jared Moskowitz (D-Fla.) said Thursday afternoon a man in Florida’s 23rd District , which Moskowitz represents, was arrested after making death threats against the lawmaker. “A constituent of mine has just been arrested in Boca, just a few miles from my house, for threatening my life,” Moskowitz wrote on the social platform X . items.t: Novel mRNA cancer vaccine helps reduce chances of melanoma patients’ tumors returning
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — A first-of-its-kind cancer vaccine is significantly reducing the chances that melanoma patients’ tumors come back, according to results of a major study released Thursday by drugmakers Moderna and Merck. The vaccine was custom-brewed for each patient to match their tumor. Adding it to a standard post-surgery treatment reduced by 42% the risk of melanoma returning two years after surgery, according to the most advanced study to date of this new strategy for fighting cancer. “The field has been looking for a win, and I think this one is a big one,” said Dr. Hussein Tawbi of MD Anderson Cancer Center in Houston, one of the researchers in the international study. The vaccine, called intismeran, is made with the same Nobel Prize-winning mRNA technology that was behind COVID-19 vaccines. He called 911 around 5 p.m. that evening, and deputies initiated a search-and-rescue response and notified USFS Climbing Rangers and CHP air operations. items.t: How much have home prices increased in Missouri, Illinois over 5 years?
items.x: ST. LOUIS If you're looking to buy a home in Missouri or Illinois, chances are you'll pay quite a bit more than you would have five years ago. MoneyLion, a financial technology company, released a study earlier this week comparing home-buying costs in 2026 to 2021, or now compared to five years ago. The study analyzed average home values, mortgage costs and salaries needed to afford a "typical single-family home" in each state, based on Zillow data available in August 2026. Missouri In Missouri, the average home costs around $57,147 more than it did five years ago, a 26.7% increase . Based on those figures, an average home cost roughly $215,000 in 2021, but is now around $272,000. The study also found that five-year annual mortgage costs for a typical home increased around $9,985, and buyers would need to earn nearly $35,000 more in annual salary to afford such a home at today's prices.

items.t: Understanding CPO cars: What does certified pre-owned mean?
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) With new-car prices near record highs, certified pre-owned vehicles (CPOs) offer buyers an affordable alternative to buying new, along with additional inspections and warranty protection. What Does Certified Pre-Owned Mean? If you’re shopping for a car, you’ve likely come across CPO vehicles. But what does that mean exactly, and how do they differ from traditional used cars? A certified pre-owned car is a used vehicle that meets the age, mileage, and condition requirements of a manufacturer or dealer certification program. CPO cars undergo a multipoint inspection and generally include additional warranty coverage, though the coverage and certification standards vary by program. Many CPO vehicles also include benefits such as roadside assistance, access to a loaner vehicle, and trip interruption coverage. The Illinois Board of Higher Education reported 190,114 students enrolled across the state’s 12 public universities for the fall 2026 semester. That is an increase of 287 students from last year and marks the third consecutive year of overall enrollment growth. Undergraduate enrollment increased 1.8%, adding 2,464 students for a total of 136,795. Seven of the 12 public universities reported undergraduate enrollment gains. Southern Illinois University Edwardsville saw a 10.1% increase in undergraduate enrollment, the second-largest percentage increase statewide behind Chicago State University at 15.8%. items.t: What happens when Missouri hunters donate their deer
items.x: JEFFERSON CITY, Mo. — Missouri conservation officials are asking deer hunters to donate venison this season to help food banks and pantries across the state. Missouri’s Share the Harvest program allows hunters to donate whole, field-dressed deer at participating meat processors at no cost. The venison is processed and distributed through local food banks and food pantries. The program has provided more than 6 million pounds of venison since it began in 1992. In recent years, hunters have donated about 5,000 deer annually, providing roughly 250,000 pounds of venison each year. Organizers hope to increase donations to 6,500 deer during the 2026 season and 10,000 in 2027. This season, Share the Harvest is testing refrigerated drop-off coolers at select locations, eliminating required hunter donation fees and increasing reimbursements for participating processors. items.t: A novel mRNA cancer vaccine helps reduce the chances of melanoma patients’ tumors returning
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — A first-of-its-kind cancer vaccine is significantly reducing the chances that melanoma patients’ tumors come back, according to results of a major study released Thursday by drugmakers Moderna and Merck. The vaccine was custom-brewed for each patient to match their tumor. Adding it to a standard post-surgery treatment reduced by 42% the risk of melanoma returning two years after surgery, according to the most advanced study to date of this new strategy for fighting cancer. “The field has been looking for a win and I think this one is a big one,” said Dr. Hussein Tawbi of MD Anderson Cancer Center in Houston, one of the researchers in the international study. The vaccine, called intismeran, is made with the same Nobel Prize-winning mRNA technology that was behind COVID-19 vaccines. items.x: ST. LOUIS Raja, the first elephant ever born at the Saint Louis Zoo and a longtime St. Louis favorite, will leave the zoo this fall. The 33-year-old male Asian elephant will move to another Association of Zoos and Aquariums-accredited zoo under a new breeding recommendation from the Asian Elephant Species Survival Plan. The zoo said Raja's destination will be announced later. Raja was born at the Saint Louis Zoo on Dec. 27, 1992. He has since fathered three daughters at the zoo: Maliha, Jade and Priya. He is also the grandfather of Jet, who was born in November 2024. The zoo previously announced plans in 2023 to move Raja to the Columbus Zoo and Aquarium. items.t: Corn maze fire at Wright City pumpkin patch

Smoke began rising from the maze while the family farm was operating. Co-owner Dave Mikus is unsure whether someone discarded a lit cigarette or if the fire was set intentionally. items.t: Supreme Court rules NH can block voters from using student IDs
items.x: ( The Hill ) The Supreme Court on Thursday ruled New Hampshire’s top election official can fully stop voters from using their student IDs when showing up to the polls in the midterms — a request backed by the Republican National Committee (RNC). A lower judge ruled officials had improperly gone further than a new state law placing restrictions on student IDs to get a ballot. The judge said the state still needed to consider student IDs alongside other evidence when a voter lacks other ways to prove their identity. The Supreme Court chastised the judge for intervening too close to November’s contests. The high court has said such orders can cause voter confusion, known as the Purcell principle. The county’s Canopy Initiative encourages residents to get involved in local tree care efforts and help grow a thriving canopy across the county. Thursday’s celebration at James McDonnell County Park featured the replanting of dozens of trees to restore the landscape and included a ceremonial tree planting with County Executive Sam Page. Advocates also shared tips on tree care, from mulching to leaving fall leaves in place. “ Leave the Leaves is really a movement within our region's native plant advocacy,” Jean Ponzi, green resources manager at the Missouri Botanical Garden, said. “Leaves are habitat for insects that over winter under trees, especially around oaks. items.t: 6-year-old found safe after going missing for hours
items.x: JENNINGS, Mo. – A 6-year-old girl has been found safe after she went missing Thursday afternoon. According to Vera Clay, a St. Louis County Police Department spokeswoman, the child went missing around 5:30 p.m. at the playground in Koeneman Park in Jennings. Clay said the child was at the park with her mother. The mother lost sight of her child and called police after about 10 minutes. Officers from the Jennings precinct and responders from the Maryland Heights Fire Protection District and the North County Fire Protection District came to the park to help search for the child, Clay said. The child was located just after 9:05 p.m. in St. Louis City. It's unclear at the moment how the child got to the city. The county's Bureau of Crimes Against Persons is continuing its investigation.

items.t: Understanding CPO cars: What does certified pre-owned mean?
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) With new-car prices near record highs, certified pre-owned vehicles (CPOs) offer buyers an affordable alternative to buying new, along with additional inspections and warranty protection. What Does Certified Pre-Owned Mean? If you’re shopping for a car, you’ve likely come across CPO vehicles. But what does that mean exactly, and how do they differ from traditional used cars? A certified pre-owned car is a used vehicle that meets the age, mileage, and condition requirements of a manufacturer or dealer certification program. CPO cars undergo a multipoint inspection and generally include additional warranty coverage, though the coverage and certification standards vary by program. Many CPO vehicles also include benefits such as roadside assistance, access to a loaner vehicle, and trip interruption coverage. Her body has since been transported to the medical examiner for an autopsy, according to the post. The attorney general’s office did not detail the circumstances surrounding the teen’s injuries. But Mexico’s El Universal reported that the teen fell from what appeared to be a pendulum-type ride that was set up temporarily for the festival. items.t: Metrolink to suspend part of OC Line due to forecasted high surf
items.x: Metrolink is suspending service on part of its Orange County Line in anticipation of high surf along the coast next week. Beginning Monday, Oct. 26, the OC Line will not operate between the Laguna Niguel-Mission Viejo and Oceanside stations, Metrolink announced on its website . "This is due to forecasted high tides," Metrolink officials said. No alternate transportation will be provided between the stations during the service suspension. Officials said the closure will reduce the risk of passengers experiencing extensive delays and unexpected service disruptions caused by changing tides. The tracks along the coast have been damaged several times in recent years by strong waves and landslides. items.t: 3 L.A. Metro D Line stations temporarily close just months after opening
items.x: Three Los Angeles Metro D Line subway stations that opened just five months ago are shutting down for 10 days, disrupting service along Wilshire Boulevard as crews complete electrical infrastructure repairs. The Wilshire/La Brea, Wilshire/Fairfax and Wilshire/La Cienega stations closed at 2 a.m. Friday, Oct. 23, and are scheduled to reopen at 4 a.m. Monday, Nov. 2. The shutdown will allow crews to install permanent electrical equipment at the Wilshire/La Brea station and complete additional work intended to improve the subway system's reliability, according to Metro. The three stations opened May 8 as part of the long-awaited D Line extension, which pushed subway service farther west beneath Wilshire Boulevard after decades of planning, political battles and construction delays. items.t: Apple’s $2,000 foldable iPhone hits stores. Is it worth it?
items.x: At $2,000, the price of the iPhone Duo might make you do a double take. And so will the two screens. Apple’s first foldable iPhone combines a phone and a mini tablet in one. I’ve been using it for a week, and when I first started, I was frustrated. Just about everything I knew about using an iPhone was different. But slowly, I started to appreciate the advantages and understand the trade-offs of this unique design. There’s a smaller, wider screen on the outside and a mini tablet-sized screen on the inside. Not every app is optimized for the Duo yet, so some things don’t look or work right. But that is improving every day as developers update their apps. Unlocking the phone also takes some getting used to. There’s no Face ID. Instead, you use a fingerprint sensor. Seeing notifications or going to the home screen takes a bit of extra effort. items.t: Toyota simplifies the 2027 Corolla Cross lineup
items.x: (TestMiles) The 2027 Corolla Cross returns with gas and hybrid powertrains, fewer hybrid grades, standard safety tech and pricing from $25,535. Toyota is taking a light-touch approach to the 2027 Corolla Cross. Rather than redesigning its smallest mainstream SUV again, the company is carrying over most of the equipment introduced for 2026 and making one notable change: the hybrid range is easier to understand. For 2027, the gas-powered Corolla Cross remains available in L, LE and XLE grades, with front-wheel drive or all-wheel drive depending on configuration. The hybrid lineup drops the previous S grade, leaving SE and XSE models, both with standard electronic all-wheel drive. Toyota says the new model year will begin reaching U.S. dealerships this fall. items.t: Trump ties big promises to GOP midterm election wins
items.x: President Trump’s growing list of promised “goodies” if Republicans retain control of Congress has become more niche the closer the country gets to the midterm elections. Trump and the GOP are hoping his big promises to voters will get them out to the polls on Election Day in less than two weeks. items.t: Crumbl shutters dozens of locations nationwide, including in California: reports
items.x: Crumbl, the bakery chain known for its rotating weekly menu and oversized cookies, has recently shuttered dozens of locations nationwide, including in California, according to multiple reports. At least 57 locations of the dessert chain have closed this year, according to an analysis of local reports and a location count on the company's website cited by Restaurant Business. Operators have warned of an insolvency crisis and say more closures could follow. At least 55 franchises are listed for sale on various broker websites, according to the report. In California, the closures span the state and include locations in Paso Robles, Pismo Beach, Hanford, Ladera Ranch, Mira Mesa, Cupertino, and Westlake Village. items.t: Scammers posing as California officials use fake police video calls to threaten victims
items.x: California health officials are warning residents about an elaborate phone scam in which callers impersonate government employees, threaten legal consequences and even pose as police officers on video calls to steal personal information. The California Department of Public Health issued the warning Thursday after receiving multiple reports of scammers posing as department employees and pressuring residents to disclose sensitive personal and financial information. According to the agency, the scheme often begins with a phone call claiming a prescription has been filled in the victim's name. The caller then demands that the person verify their identity to "clear their record," sometimes threatening legal action or the cancellation of prescriptions if they refuse. items.t: One-fifth of Americans cutting groceries to pay high electric bills, survey finds
items.x: Many Americans say they have to cut back on groceries in order to pay their electric bills, according to a new survey by Consumer Reports . The survey found that 20% of consumers, or one in five Americans, have cut back on grocery shopping or sought less expensive food to offset soaring costs. Twenty-five percent are opting to be cold this fall and winter rather than go hungry, and 75% said their household finances are simply being strained by higher prices and expenses. The national survey of 2,003 U.S. adults found that 81% of Americans who have lived in the same home for at least three years said their electricity bills increased during that time. More than a quarter reported increases of 20% to 49%. Many Americans also struggle with understanding their utility bills. items.x: Federal authorities charged 15 people, including six medical professionals, in a sweeping Los Angeles-area health care fraud crackdown involving $2 billion in alleged fraudulent claims, the Justice Department announced Thursday. Eight defendants were arrested Oct. 22 in connection with schemes involving sham addiction treatment centers, unnecessary surgical procedures, fraudulent hospice services and illegal kickbacks, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Central District of California. The cases include what prosecutors describe as the largest substance abuse treatment fraud scheme of its kind ever prosecuted by the Justice Department, involving more than $1.6 billion in claims submitted to private insurance companies. items.t: ‘Behemoth’ El Niño could be ‘off the charts,’ forecasters warn
items.x: (NEXSTAR) – Meteorologists are continuing to warn of the El Niño weather event expected to impact us throughout the winter, with a new climate outlook from the World Meteorological Organization suggesting it "could be unprecedented in strength." In an update Wednesday, the WMO said this year's El Niño weather pattern could be so strong, it could "literally [be] off the monitoring charts that we have used for the past four decades." A main focus of forecasting El Niño comes down to sea surface temperatures. In the Pacific, an "anomaly of 0.5 [degrees Celsius] above normal" can trigger an El Niño alert from the WMO, according to the United Nations. Between next month and January, WMO has forecast temperatures could rise 3.8 degrees Celsius above average. Thanksgiving weather outlooks released: What could it be like near you? items.t: Keep The Pie, Pass On The Drama 6 Tips For Setting Healthy Boundaries During The Holidays
items.x: Source: O2O Creative / Getty The holidays are supposed to be about love, laughter, good food and making memories. But let's be honest: sometimes, the most stressful part of Thanksgiving and Christmas isn't figuring out who's bringing the mac and cheese, it's the dread of figuring out how to survive being around everybody. Between family drama, unsolicited opinions about your love life, pressure to host a picture-perfect dinner and the expectation to show up everywhere, the holiday season can quickly turn from festive to exhausting. Add in the pressure to spend money, cook for a crowd and keep everybody happy, and suddenly, your holiday cheer is hanging by a thread. That's why learning how to set boundaries during the holidays is so important. Protecting your peace doesn't mean you don't love your family. It means understanding that your time, energy and emotional well-being matter, too.

items.t: How To Beat Seasonal Depression Like A Boss: Signs, Symptoms And Ways To Fight Back
items.x: PeopleImages Feeling sad, sluggish, or just not like yourself as the days get shorter, temperatures drop, and sunshine becomes harder to come by? Don’t worry, sis — you’re not alone. While the changing seasons can affect your mood and energy levels, those feelings may be more than just the winter blues. Seasonal affective disorder (SAD) is a type of depression associated with seasonal changes. It most commonly begins in the fall or winter and improves during the spring and summer. According to the Mayo Clinic , reduced sunlight can disrupt the body's internal clock and affect brain chemicals, including serotonin and melatonin, which help regulate mood and sleep. It’s estimated to affect 10 million Americans, or about 3% of the population, while another 10% may experience milder symptoms. items.x: Source: Boston Globe / Getty By 7:30 on summer mornings, while some vacationers are still deciding what to do with their day, swimmers are already in the water of Oak Bluffs, Massachusetts. Some have been coming for decades. Others are joining for the first time. Together, they exercise, socialize, and welcome another day at Inkwell Beach, a small stretch of Martha's Vineyard shoreline where Black Americans have gathered for generations. Known as the Polar Bears , the group began gathering in 1946, when nine Black summer workers started swimming before their shifts. Eight decades later, the ritual continues. The Martha's Vineyard Times documented the group's 80-year history in June 2026, tracing how an informal gathering of friends became a tradition built on movement, fellowship, and connection. items.t: Halloween candy sales are off to a slow start amid high chocolate prices and affordability concerns
items.x: Halloween candy sales are off to a slow start this year as U.S. consumers grapple with high living costs and eye-popping chocolate prices . Halloween candy sales fell 6.7% in the month ending Oct. 17 compared to the same period last year, according to NielsenIQ, a market research firm. Nielsen also noted an 11.7% decline in candy sales in mid-September, erasing the preseason gains that Halloween candy enjoyed the previous two years. Chris Costagli, a vice president and food thought leader at NielsenIQ, said high gas prices have worsened Americans’ concerns about affordability, and that's dampening demand for Halloween treats. As of Friday, the average price of a gallon of regular gasoline in the U.S. was $4.29, up nearly 40% from the prior year. “I think what you’re seeing now is a consumer that’s spending so much additional money on fuel and housing and clothing and food,” Costagli said

items.t: Understanding CPO cars: What does certified pre-owned mean?
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) With new-car prices near record highs, certified pre-owned vehicles (CPOs) offer buyers an affordable alternative to buying new, along with additional inspections and warranty protection. What Does Certified Pre-Owned Mean? If you’re shopping for a car, you’ve likely come across CPO vehicles. But what does that mean exactly, and how do they differ from traditional used cars? A certified pre-owned car is a used vehicle that meets the age, mileage, and condition requirements of a manufacturer or dealer certification program. CPO cars undergo a multipoint inspection and generally include additional warranty coverage, though the coverage and certification standards vary by program. Many CPO vehicles also include benefits such as roadside assistance, access to a loaner vehicle, and trip interruption coverage. Check out our helpful guide for more information on how to buy CPO cars

items.t: The science and politics behind the panic over ultraprocessed foods
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Ultraprocessed foods have a terrible reputation. Studies have linked them with multiple chronic diseases . Journalists and health influencers characterize them as poison . Some public health experts call for a global halt to producing and consuming them. But the debate around ultraprocessed foods is not nearly as settled as it may seem. As a researcher who studies social movements for healthy and sustainable food, I have been documenting the history of processed foods and examining debates around the science and politics of ultraprocessing . In basic terms, ultraprocessed foods are mass-produced, industrial formulations that use ingredients not typically found in a home kitchen, and that generally contain little to no intact whole foods. items.t: Early voting surges in battleground states as Democrats outpace GOP gains
items.x: Early voting is surging in several key battleground states, giving Democrats hope that their strength in midterm polling could translate into a turnout advantage in November. In North Carolina, more than 1.2 million early ballots have been accepted, a 37 percent increase from the same point leading up to the 2022 midterms, according to an analysis released Friday by Catawba College political scientist Michael Bitzer. That growth — which includes both in-person and mail-in ballots — has been driven by a 47 percent increase among registered Democrats and a 60 percent increase in participation among unaffiliated voters. Early voting among Republicans is up 2.6 percent. Similar patterns are emerging elsewhere, with high turnout especially pronounced in historically Republican-leaning states with competitive Senate races this cycle. items.t: Dayton residents evacuated after building deemed unsafe
items.x: DAYTON, Ohio ( WDTN ) – Residents were evacuated from a building on the corner of Troy and Kiefer streets after inspectors found it unsafe to live there on Thursday, Oct. 22. The city of Dayton and the Dayton Police Department executed an inspection warrant to evaluate documented structural, electrical, fire safety, and occupancy concerns. During the inspection, the city’s building official and nuisance abatement supervisor identified significant safety hazards, and the building was determined to be a nuisance. Occupants were given resources for temporary accommodations consistent with emergency vacate procedures. The city is currently determining the next steps for the property.

As is tradition, the holidays will begin with the Dayton Holiday Festival’s Grande Illumination tree lighting. items.t: About half concerned Republicans could try to overturn midterm results: Survey
items.x: ( The Hill ) A new poll released Friday suggests half of Americans are concerned Republicans may try to overturn the results of November’s midterm election. Fifty percent of respondents to the New York Times/Siena University survey said they were either "very" or "somewhat worried" the GOP may use “illegal means” to overturn the election, compared to 49 percent who are either "not too worried" or "not at all worried." A strong majority of Democrats — 86 percent — were among the share of likely voters who reported feeling worry about potential GOP election interference, and 52 percent independents felt the same. Even 10 percent of Republicans say they are worried their own party would overturn the results. items.t: A novel mRNA cancer vaccine helps reduce the chances of melanoma patients’ tumors returning
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — A first-of-its-kind cancer vaccine is significantly reducing the chances that melanoma patients’ tumors come back, according to results of a major study released Thursday by drugmakers Moderna and Merck. The vaccine was custom-brewed for each patient to match their tumor. Adding it to a standard post-surgery treatment reduced by 42% the risk of melanoma returning two years after surgery, according to the most advanced study to date of this new strategy for fighting cancer. “The field has been looking for a win and I think this one is a big one,” said Dr. Hussein Tawbi of MD Anderson Cancer Center in Houston, one of the researchers in the international study. The vaccine, called intismeran, is made with the same Nobel Prize-winning mRNA technology that was behind COVID-19 vaccines. Now, now, there's no need to get violent. Just have a conversation. According to Days of the Year , Slap Your Coworker Day is meant to be a day for coworkers to address their annoyances in a fun way. Some offices organize events to mark the occasion, playing games like "Slap Tennis" or sending "Slap-A-Grams." According to Days of the Year, the day began as a joke in the early 2000s. It became increasingly popular after being spread on message boards, emails and social media. The "Slap" part is purely humorous and not meant to be taken seriously. items.t: Dunbar blanks Meadowdale 27-0 to win first DPS title since 2023
items.x: DAYTON, Ohio (WDTN) For the first time since 2023 Dunbar secures the DPS title, with the Wolverines shutting out their rival and the two-time defending league champ Meadowdale 27-0 on Thursday night at Welcome Stadium. After leading 6-0 at halftime, the Wolverines exploded for 21 more points in the second half to complete the shutout. Junior quarterback Nazir White rushed for two touchdowns and threw for another, accounting for three of the Wolverine's four scores on the night. Dunbar completes a perfect conference schedule, going 5-0 in DPS play under head coach Darran Powell. The league title marks the Wolverine's fourth overall under the new DPS league format which started in 2021. With the win, Dunbar also clinches a playoff berth in the Div. 4 state tournament with their opponent for the first round of the postseason TBD.

items.t: Supreme Court rules NH can block voters from using student IDs
items.x: ( The Hill ) The Supreme Court on Thursday ruled New Hampshire’s top election official can fully stop voters from using their student IDs when showing up to the polls in the midterms — a request backed by the Republican National Committee (RNC). The Supreme Court chastised the judge for intervening too close to November’s contests. The high court has said such orders can cause voter confusion, known as the Purcell principle. items.t: Understanding CPO cars: What does certified pre-owned mean?
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) With new-car prices near record highs, certified pre-owned vehicles (CPOs) offer buyers an affordable alternative to buying new, along with additional inspections and warranty protection. What Does Certified Pre-Owned Mean? If you’re shopping for a car, you’ve likely come across CPO vehicles. But what does that mean exactly, and how do they differ from traditional used cars? A certified pre-owned car is a used vehicle that meets the age, mileage, and condition requirements of a manufacturer or dealer certification program. CPO cars undergo a multipoint inspection and generally include additional warranty coverage, though the coverage and certification standards vary by program. Many CPO vehicles also include benefits such as roadside assistance, access to a loaner vehicle, and trip interruption coverage. items.t: The science and politics behind the panic over ultraprocessed foods
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Ultraprocessed foods have a terrible reputation. Studies have linked them with multiple chronic diseases . Journalists and health influencers characterize them as poison . Some public health experts call for a global halt to producing and consuming them. But the debate around ultraprocessed foods is not nearly as settled as it may seem. As a researcher who studies social movements for healthy and sustainable food, I have been documenting the history of processed foods and examining debates around the science and politics of ultraprocessing . items.t: 2 found shot to death in moving car on I-57 overpass in south suburbs: police
items.x: BRADLEY, Ill. — Two people were found shot to death in a moving car in south suburban Bradley. Police said an officer was flagged down around 9 p.m. Thursday at East North Street and North Van Buren Avenue, over a stalled vehicle on East North Street atop the Interstate 57 overpass. Upon arrival, the officer located the vehicle, which was still in motion, with two gunshot victims inside. According to police, the passenger was pronounced dead on the scene. The driver was removed from the vehicle for life-saving measures and transported to an area hospital, where they were pronounced dead. Their names have not yet been released. Further information has not been provided. An investigation is underway.

items.t: A novel mRNA cancer vaccine helps reduce the chances of melanoma patients’ tumors returning
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — A first-of-its-kind cancer vaccine is significantly reducing the chances that melanoma patients’ tumors come back, according to results of a major study released Thursday by drugmakers Moderna and Merck. The vaccine was custom-brewed for each patient to match their tumor. Adding it to a standard post-surgery treatment reduced by 42% the risk of melanoma returning two years after surgery, according to the most advanced study to date of this new strategy for fighting cancer. “The field has been looking for a win and I think this one is a big one,” said Dr. Hussein Tawbi of MD Anderson Cancer Center in Houston, one of the researchers in the international study. The vaccine, called intismeran, is made with the same Nobel Prize-winning mRNA technology that was behind COVID-19 vaccines.
