items.t: Toyota simplifies the 2027 Corolla Cross lineup
items.x: (TestMiles) The 2027 Corolla Cross returns with gas and hybrid powertrains, fewer hybrid grades, standard safety tech and pricing from $25,535. Toyota is taking a light-touch approach to the 2027 Corolla Cross. Rather than redesigning its smallest mainstream SUV again, the company is carrying over most of the equipment introduced for 2026 and making one notable change: the hybrid range is easier to understand. For 2027, the gas-powered Corolla Cross remains available in L, LE and XLE grades, with front-wheel drive or all-wheel drive depending on configuration. items.t: Understanding CPO cars: What does certified pre-owned mean?
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) With new-car prices near record highs, certified pre-owned vehicles (CPOs) offer buyers an affordable alternative to buying new, along with additional inspections and warranty protection. What Does Certified Pre-Owned Mean? If you’re shopping for a car, you’ve likely come across CPO vehicles. But what does that mean exactly, and how do they differ from traditional used cars? A certified pre-owned car is a used vehicle that meets the age, mileage, and condition requirements of a manufacturer or dealer certification program. CPO cars undergo a multipoint inspection and generally include additional warranty coverage, though the coverage and certification standards vary by program. Many CPO vehicles also include benefits such as roadside assistance, access to a loaner vehicle, and trip interruption coverage. items.t: The science and politics behind the panic over ultraprocessed foods

items.t: Savannah Police patrol car involved in early morning crash
items.x: SAVANNAH, Ga. (WSAV) — A Savannah Police patrol car was involved in a crash early Friday morning in midtown Savannah. Just before 1 a.m., the patrol car was traveling west on 37th Street approaching Drayton St. A second vehicle, a Ford Escape, was traveling north on Drayton St. approaching 37th St. The patrol car struck the second vehicle on its passenger side. Georgia State Patrol (GSP) troopers were called to the scene. A GSP spokesperson told WSAV, "[The Savannah Patrol car] did have its emergency equipment activated, but it was unclear as to when it was activated." Chatham EMS CEO Chuck Kearns told WSAV three people were transported from the scene. WSAV reached out to Savannah Police officials for information and were told to contact the Georgia State Patrol as they do not comment on other organizations' investigations.

items.t: Breast cancer survivor from Pennsylvania signs Pink Jeep
items.x: SAVANNAH, Ga. (WASV) — As we continue to Paint the Town Pink, the Pink Jeep was rolling around Franklin Square when a breast cancer survivor and her husband were visiting from Pennsylvania. Dee Charles is six years cancer-free. Charles became emotional the moment she saw the Pink Jeep and asked to sign it. "In 2020, I had one of those feelings that said, Go get checked. And I did. And they found three small tumors. I was able to get away with just a lumpectomy, but I'm six years clean. Do not ever forget to check on a monthly basis, if not more, because you just don't know," said Charles. You can see more on Paint the Town Pink on the WSAV website .

items.t: Guyton City Council looking at special election for new mayor
items.x: GUYTON, Ga. (WSAV) — Guyton City Council held a Special Called Meeting on Thursday, where they discussed Mayor Andy Harville's recent resignation. Harville announced his resignation on Oct. 15. Guyton County Manager Bill Lindsey shared that Harville's resignation came unexpectedly and was due to health reasons. Lindsey said Harville would not go into detail about those health issues, but that council respects his privacy. Harville left with more than 14 months on his term; therefore, they must hold a special election, Lindsey said. The date for that special election will need to be announced by Nov. 29, Benjamin Perkins said. In the absence of the mayor, Mayor Pro Tem Micheal Johnsons assumes the duties and powers until the vacancy is filled.

items.x: SAVANNAH, Ga. (WSAV) — With less than two weeks until Election Day, U.S. Sen. Jon Ossoff says his race against Republican nominee and Congressman Mike Collins could come down to just a few thousand votes. Ossoff and U.S. Sen. items.t: Richmond Hill softball earns second straight elite 8 appearance
items.x: RICHMOND HILL, Ga. (WSAV) — Richmond Hill softball punched its ticket to second straight GHSA Class 7-A elite eight with a 4-2 win over Dacula on Thursday. The Wildcats split a double-header with Dacula Wednesday. They won game one 5-4 in extra innings, but lost game two 3-2 to send it to a decider. Richmond Hill led game three 4-0 before allowing a pair of runs in the seventh, but ended the game with a great defensive play to catch a Dacula baserunner stealing second base for the final out. The Wildcats move on to Columbus to face Buford in a double-elimination tournament.

items.t: Georgia residents worry of high prescription prices amid U.S. Customs and Border Protection rule
items.x: SAVANNAH, Ga. (WSAV) — A new U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) rule could make it harder for some Americans to get prescription medication from Canada. The change targets personal prescriptions shipped across the border, a source some patients turn to for lower prices. The rule was set to take effect on Oct. 22, 2026. However, it was delayed to Jan. 20, 2027. George Kircher a Claxton resident who gets his medication from a Canadian pharmacy, saving him more than $1,000 every three months. Now, he worries those savings could disappear. "In Canada, when I order my medication, I can order it for $144 for a three-month supply," Kircher said. "In the US, if I were to pay cash for the same supply, same drug, it would cost me $1,345." That price difference is why Kircher orders his generic brand Eliquis from Canada. State transportation officials announced the selection after opening bids from two competing teams in September. items.t: CCPD shares reminder after report of sweepstakes scam
items.x: CHATHAM COUNTY, Ga. (WSAV) — An elderly person in Chatham County was told they won millions in a sweepstakes, with one important condition to collect, which led to a reminder from officials. The person was convinced to send $500 to collect their multi-million-dollar prize from a Reader's Digest scam, a Chatham County Police Department spokesperson said. To prevent similar scams, officials offered the following reminder: "Any time you are required to send money in order to make more money (or claim a prize), you are almost certainly dealing with a scam. Remember, if you're lucky enough to win, it shouldn't cost you a fee." Immediately reporting scams you encounter to law enforcement is vital to protecting yourself and others.

items.t: Man accused of 2022 Gateway Apartments murder indicted
items.x: CHATHAM COUNTY, Ga. (WSAV) — The man arrested nearly four years after a shooting that killed 40-year-old Marvin Swan was indicted for murder charges Wednesday by a grand jury in Chatham County. Forty-two-year-old Julian Bryant was arrested on July 17 in connection to the Dec. 11, 2022, shooting at the Waters at Gateway Apartments. Bryant was indicted for one count of malice murder, two counts of felony murder, aggravated assault, possession of a firearm during the commission of a felony, possession of a firearm by a convicted felon and possession of a firearm by a convicted felon during a crime. Bryant allegedly shot Swan using a 9mm firearm, court records said. Savannah Police Department officers responded to the scene around 10:30 p.m. on Dec. 11, 2022, and found Swan outside the apartment with gunshot wounds. Swan later died from his injuries.

items.t: Madagascar's rare wild pepper prized by chefs faces growing threat from commercial demand
items.x: Voatsiperifery pepper, a unique wild spice native to Madagascar and highly popular for chefs worldwide, now faces a challenging future because of its popularity and the ongoing destruction of its forest habitat. This pepper, with a characteristic woody tail, a remnant of its stem, has a delicate, aromatic flavor and grows on vines that reach into the treetops of Madagascar's natural forests. Unfortunately, these forests have diminished by 27 percent from 1990 to 2025, as reported by the UN Food and Agriculture Organization . This happens because gatherers often cut down the vines and, in many instances, the trees that support them, to harvest the prized peppercorns without climbing. items.t: Veteran producer brings inspiring true story ‘Being Heumann’ to SCAD Savannah Film Festival
items.x: SAVANNAH, Ga. (WSAV) — For veteran Hollywood producer David Permut , great stories often begin with discovery. After more than 40 films and a career that has spanned projects ranging from "Face/Off" to the Oscar-nominated “Hacksaw Ridge,” his latest passion project, " Being Heumann ," grew from a film festival screening that introduced him to a pivotal figure in disability rights history. “Being Heumann” tells the story of disability rights activist Judy Heumann and the landmark 1977 San Francisco sit-in that compelled the federal government to enforce accessibility protections for Americans with disabilities. Permut is bringing "Being Heumann" to the SCAD Savannah Film Festival for its southeast premiere, where audiences will have the opportunity to watch the movie and sit in on a Q&A session with him following the screening. items.t: Interim Chief Cary Hill named Chief of Police for Richmond Hill
items.x: RICHMOND HILL, Ga. (WSAV) The City of Richmond Hill announced Tuesday that Cary Hill has been named Chief of Police for the Richmond Hill Police Department (RHPD). Chief Hill has been the Interim Chief since December of 2025. Richmond Hill leadership suspended the external search for a new chief in May so they could evaluate Hill for the permanent role. Chief Hill has more than 30 years of law enforcement experience. Over15 years of that experience is at the command level. Chief Hill began his career in law enforcement with the Savannah Police Department in 1992. During his time there, he climbed to the rank of Captain and commanded several precincts and Special Operations. He joined RHPD in 2024 as Major over Patrol, Criminal Investigations, and Police Administration.

items.t: Effingham Co. Sheriff’s Office to assist in Georgia sex offender compliance check
items.x: EFFINGHAM COUNTY, Ga. (WSAV) — The Effingham County Sheriff's Office will participate in Georgia's annual "Operation Watchful Eye" initiative, checking the residence and compliance of registered sex offenders. The statewide initiative will begin on Oct. 26 through Nov. 2 as coordinated by the Georgia Sheriffs' Association and the GSA Sex Offender Registry Task Force, a spokesperson for the ECSO said Wednesday. This is the 11th year that the ECSO has participated in Operation Watchful Eye, aiming to enforce the registration requirements of sex offenders in the county and arrest those who are non-compliant.

items.t: Not just gas and groceries: Childcare costs weigh on voters before midterm elections
items.x: Like so many Americans, Jenny Escolastico has watched wearily as the cost of living has risen, straining her household budget. But as a mother of two children under 5, she faces added pressure that could shape how she votes in November : childcare costs. Escolastico’s household outside Allentown, Pennsylvania, is relying solely on her husband’s income. She’s staying home with her children, at least in part because she simply can’t afford to work . "What I would be spending on childcare would be more than what I would be making if I were working full time,” said Escolastico, an Air Force veteran who later worked in human resources. “Childcare is another rent, another car note.” Even though her son now attends state-funded prekindergarten , returning to work would still mean finding him after-school care, plus full-time childcare for her daughter. items.t: Pedestrian struck, in critical condition after collision on I-516
items.x: CHATHAM COUNTY, Ga. (WSAV) — The Georgia State Patrol (GSP) is investigating an incident that occurred early Wednesday morning on I-516 in Garden City. At 3:29 a.m., GSP troopers responded to I-516 eastbound near mile marker 07 following reports of a vehicle vs. pedestrian crash. An investigation was conducted and it was revealed that the pedestrian walked south across the roadway when they were struck by a vehicle. After being struck, the pedestrian landed in another lane of the road, where they were then run over by a second vehicle. The individual was transported to a hospital and remains in critical condition. The section of I-516 eastbound near mile marker 07 was shut down for several hours and has since reopened. The images above are courtesy of Jonathan Dean . This is an ongoing story. Stay with WSAV for all updates as new information is made available.

items.t: Liberty County 2 wins away from first region title since 2021
items.x: HINESVILLE, Ga. (WSAV) — After a remarkable mid-season turnaround, the Liberty County football team has a chance to win its first region title since 2021. The Panthers started the season 1-3 in non-region play. However, since then, they have won four straight and sit alone at the top of the Region 3-AAAA standings. Head coach Tony Glazer attributes a lot of the success to his 25 seniors. He also said Liberty County is winning the final quarter, which is something they had to learn. "That's the difference between ok teams and good teams," Glazer said. "Good teams find a way to win the fourth quarter. I think having this group right here, they understand what that means. But they also understand winning the fourth quarter starts in the offseason, starts in the weight room, starts on the practice field." Liberty County plays West Laurens for Senior Night at 7:30 p.m. Friday in Hinesville.

Atlanta Bureau Chief Archith Seshadri sat down one-on-one with Luckovich to discuss what inspires his work, his advice for aspiring cartoonists and how he sees the future of editorial cartooning. Turning the news into art Luckovich began working at The Atlanta Journal-Constitution in 1989. items.t: Georgia surpasses 1 million in-person early votes cast
items.x: GEORGIA (WSAV) — More than one million in-person early votes have been counted in the state of Georgia as of Tuesday, marking a sizable increase from the same point in the last midterm election cycle. Georgia Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger said, “We continue to break records each day of early voting. This is evidence that Georgians trust our election process. To find early voting locations and hours in your county, visit the Secretary of State’s My Voter Page at https://mvp.sos.ga.gov. Election Day is Nov. 3.

The lawsuit , filed Thursday in federal court by ArchCity Defenders, targets the City of University City and five police officers, alleging they unlawfully searched private property and unlawfully towed cars over alleged municipal ordinance violations. In an update Wednesday, the WMO said this year's El Niño weather pattern could be so strong, it could "literally [be] off the monitoring charts that we have used for the past four decades." A main focus of forecasting El Niño comes down to sea surface temperatures. In the Pacific, an "anomaly of 0.5 [degrees Celsius] above normal" can trigger an El Niño alert from the WMO, according to the United Nations. Few pediatricians have treated a newborn with congenital measles, presenting a clinical challenge for physicians. items.t: Legal Lens: Understanding Workplace Harassment
items.x: Sponsored – Attorney Andrea McNairy of Brown & Crouppen Law Firm explains that under Missouri law, workplace harassment is illegal when it is based on a protected characteristic and meets legal requirements. Sexual harassment may include unwanted advances, inappropriate touching, explicit comments, or a hostile work environment. Employers may be held responsible depending on the circumstances, and retaliation against employees who report harassment is prohibited. Employees should document incidents, save relevant messages, and report harassment to a supervisor or HR in writing. Strict filing deadlines apply: generally 180 days under Missouri law and up to 300 days under federal law. Consulting a Missouri employment attorney can help clarify your rights and options. items.t: NSA warns organizations to patch security flaws identified by AI
items.x: ( The Hill ) The National Security Agency (NSA) warned organizations Wednesday to immediately patch a pair of security flaws or take their systems offline, after artificial intelligence discovered vulnerabilities in a key programming language. "Effective Immediately, all organizations using PHP for their systems are advised to be prepared for an update addressing two critical vulnerabilities," NSA Cyber wrote in a post on the social platform X. "These vulnerabilities often provide a direct path to the server's file system or database," the agency continued. "If an immediate update is not feasible, it is recommended that organizations take the system offline until it can be fully mitigated." PHP is a programming language frequently used in web development and is often referred to as the "backbone of the web." items.x: CAHOKIA HEIGHTS, Ill. A man accused of setting two Cahokia Heights spas on fire, which killed one woman , told investigators he started the fires after a sexual encounter left him upset, according to a federal criminal complaint. A massive fire destroyed Fuji Super Spa on S. 88th St. around 3 a.m. Monday. A woman’s remains were found inside the business the following day. On Wednesday, federal prosecutors with the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Illinois charged Quentin Hanks with one count of arson in connection with the fires. Investigators believe the crime began at another spa just down the street, where another fire broke out at One Spa around the same time, according to the criminal complaint. The damage there was mostly in the waiting room. Prosecutors said witnesses helped investigators identify a suspicious man who had been at the spa shortly before the fire.

items.t: Halloween candy sales are off to a slow start amid high chocolate prices and affordability concerns
items.x: Halloween candy sales are off to a slow start this year as U.S. consumers grapple with high living costs and eye-popping chocolate prices . Halloween candy sales fell 6.7% in the month ending Oct. 17 compared to the same period last year, according to NielsenIQ, a market research firm. Nielsen also noted an 11.7% decline in candy sales in mid-September, erasing the preseason gains that Halloween candy enjoyed the previous two years. Chris Costagli, a vice president and food thought leader at NielsenIQ, said high gas prices have worsened Americans’ concerns about affordability, and that's dampening demand for Halloween treats. As of Friday, the average price of a gallon of regular gasoline in the U.S. was $4.29, up nearly 40% from the prior year. “I think what you’re seeing now is a consumer that’s spending so much additional money on fuel and housing and clothing and food,” Costagli said

items.t: Understanding CPO cars: What does certified pre-owned mean?
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) With new-car prices near record highs, certified pre-owned vehicles (CPOs) offer buyers an affordable alternative to buying new, along with additional inspections and warranty protection. What Does Certified Pre-Owned Mean? If you’re shopping for a car, you’ve likely come across CPO vehicles. But what does that mean exactly, and how do they differ from traditional used cars? A certified pre-owned car is a used vehicle that meets the age, mileage, and condition requirements of a manufacturer or dealer certification program. CPO cars undergo a multipoint inspection and generally include additional warranty coverage, though the coverage and certification standards vary by program. Many CPO vehicles also include benefits such as roadside assistance, access to a loaner vehicle, and trip interruption coverage. items.t: The science and politics behind the panic over ultraprocessed foods
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Ultraprocessed foods have a terrible reputation. Studies have linked them with multiple chronic diseases . Journalists and health influencers characterize them as poison . Some public health experts call for a global halt to producing and consuming them. But the debate around ultraprocessed foods is not nearly as settled as it may seem. As a researcher who studies social movements for healthy and sustainable food, I have been documenting the history of processed foods and examining debates around the science and politics of ultraprocessing . In basic terms, ultraprocessed foods are mass-produced, industrial formulations that use ingredients not typically found in a home kitchen, and that generally contain little to no intact whole foods. items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — A first-of-its-kind cancer vaccine is significantly reducing the chances that melanoma patients’ tumors come back, according to results of a major study released Thursday by drugmakers Moderna and Merck. The vaccine was custom-brewed for each patient to match their tumor. Adding it to a standard post-surgery treatment reduced by 42% the risk of melanoma returning two years after surgery, according to the most advanced study to date of this new strategy for fighting cancer. “The field has been looking for a win and I think this one is a big one,” said Dr. Hussein Tawbi of MD Anderson Cancer Center in Houston, one of the researchers in the international study. items.t: Health officials caution residents about rabies amid increased bat bites in Baldwin County
items.x: ALABAMA ( WRBL ) — Officials with the Alabama Department of Public Health (ADPH) reported that in the state and nationwide, there has been an increase in human exposure to rabid or potentially rabid animals. In Baldwin County specifically, several people were treated at local emergency rooms for bat bites. Officials said the patients were bitten at different residences in the county. However, none of the bats were submitted for rabies testing, and the patients are undergoing post-exposure treatment. Anyone bitten by a bat needs post-exposure treatment unless the bat tests negative for rabies. Rabies is a viral infection in mammals that is transmitted by bites, scratches, or other contact with infected saliva. items.t: Understanding CPO cars: What does certified pre-owned mean?
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) With new-car prices near record highs, certified pre-owned vehicles (CPOs) offer buyers an affordable alternative to buying new, along with additional inspections and warranty protection. What Does Certified Pre-Owned Mean? If you’re shopping for a car, you’ve likely come across CPO vehicles. But what does that mean exactly, and how do they differ from traditional used cars? A certified pre-owned car is a used vehicle that meets the age, mileage, and condition requirements of a manufacturer or dealer certification program. CPO cars undergo a multipoint inspection and generally include additional warranty coverage, though the coverage and certification standards vary by program. Many CPO vehicles also include benefits such as roadside assistance, access to a loaner vehicle, and trip interruption coverage. items.t: Toyota simplifies the 2027 Corolla Cross lineup

Toyota is taking a light-touch approach to the 2027 Corolla Cross. Rather than redesigning its smallest mainstream SUV again, the company is carrying over most of the equipment introduced for 2026 and making one notable change: the hybrid range is easier to understand. The hybrid lineup drops the previous S grade, leaving SE and XSE models, both with standard electronic all-wheel drive. Toyota says the new model year will begin reaching U.S. dealerships this fall. items.t: Two suspects arrested in Columbia Road shooting, one person wounded
items.x: COLUMBIA COUNTY, Ga. (WJBF) The Columbia County Sheriff's Office responded to a shooting Thursday night, around 11:15. The incident reportedly happened at 5109 Columbia Road. According to authorities, Jorge Luis Landaverde was in front of the residence with his girlfriend when a red sedan pulled in front of the home. An argument ensued and one of the vehicle occupants allegedly fired three rounds, one struck the victim in the left ankle The victim was transported to Wellstar Hospital in Grovetown for treatment. The girlfriend told deputies she believes she knows some of the people involved. Two suspects were arrested in this case. Charles Ortiz and Lynda Human have been charged with Aggravated Assault. The investigation is ongoing and the victim did not appear to sustain life threatening injuries.

items.t: Georgia residents worry of high prescription prices amid U.S. Customs and Border Protection rule
items.x: SAVANNAH, Ga. (WSAV) — A new U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) rule could make it harder for some Americans to get prescription medication from Canada. The change targets personal prescriptions shipped across the border, a source some patients turn to for lower prices. The rule was set to take effect on Oct. 22, 2026. However, it was delayed to Jan. 20, 2027. George Kircher a Claxton resident who gets his medication from a Canadian pharmacy, saving him more than $1,000 every three months. Now, he worries those savings could disappear. "In Canada, when I order my medication, I can order it for $144 for a three-month supply," Kircher said. "In the US, if I were to pay cash for the same supply, same drug, it would cost me $1,345." That price difference is why Kircher orders his generic brand Eliquis from Canada. items.t: Georgia early voting tops 1.3 million: What voting patterns reveal about the electorate
items.x: ATLANTA (WJBF) – More than 1.3 million Georgians have already cast their ballots early, raising questions about who is voting, what motivates them and whether voting patterns could offer clues about the 2026 midterm elections. Political experts say the timing of a vote does not necessarily reveal how someone will vote. While Democrats have traditionally been more likely to vote early and Republicans more likely to vote on Election Day, turnout can depend on a range of factors, from work schedules and transportation to weather and other day-to-day circumstances. Ultimately, experts say, mobilizing voters and getting supporters to the polls will be critical as candidates compete for control of key races. Henry McMaster’s office announced early Wednesday morning that Westinghouse Electric Company will invest about $1 billion to expand its Columbia Fuel Fabrication Facility in Richland County and build a new facility to produce next-generation nuclear fuel. As Democrats put affordability front and center in their campaigns, there's one issue some candidates are focused on: personalized prices. Personalized pricing, which is also called surveillance pricing, is when companies use your personal data to determine how much you pay for their products or services. items.t: 79-year-old dead after stabbing identified, suspect arrested
items.x: AUGUSTA, Ga. (WJBF) – The Richmond County Coroner's Office responded to Wellstar MCG in reference to a homicide on Wednesday. According to the coroner's office, the incident took place when an "adult male was involved in an altercation with another adult male at the residence when he became unresponsive." When deputies arrived to the residence at Woodhaven Court at 3:03 p.m. on Oct. 21, they located 79-year-old Donese Bentley of Augusta, unresponsive with injuries sustained in a stabbing incident. Bentley was pronounced dead at 3:36 p.m. at the hospital. An autopsy has been scheduled. The suspect, 33-year-old Joshua Oglesby of Augusta, was detained at the scene. He was transported to the Criminal Investigation Division and then subsequently committed to the Charles B. Webster Detention Center. Oglesby is charged with Murder. This is a developing story.

items.t: Omega block pattern brings fantastic fall weather!
items.x: Wednesday evening update: This autumn weather is apple-solutely flawless! The reason? We're under an omega block. On the upper-level maps it looks just like the Greek letter omega (a strong ridge of high pressure parked over the central U.S., with troughs on both sides). That high acts like a traffic jam for the jet stream, forcing weather systems to go around us instead of through. The result is prolonged sunshine, dry air, and conditions that don't want to move. We're looking at highs in the mid to upper 70s on Thursday. By the weekend we cool a notch (highs in the lower 70s) with a breezy northeast wind that will make it feel a bit cooler. Overnight lows will hang in the low to mid 40s most nights. Perfect weather to head outside and do some fall activities! items.t: ‘Molotov cocktail’ was thrown at an ICE building in Atlanta and the FBI is investigating
items.x: ATLANTA (AP) — The FBI offered $20,000 on Wednesday for information leading to the arrest of an unidentified male who investigators say threw a “Molotov cocktail-style device” at a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement building in downtown Atlanta the night before. The device caused minor damage, the FBI said in a statement, which didn't specify whether the building itself was hit. The bureau said the “attempted arson” happened at around 8:15 p.m. Tuesday, and that agents were “reviewing evidence and following leads.” No arrests had been made. The multi-story brick building surrounded by a metal fence contains offices for ICE, as well as an immigration court.

items.t: Federal grant helps preserve historic Mother Trinity CME
items.x: AUGUSTA, Ga (WJBF)- A historic church in Augusta is one step closer to preservation thanks to a $750,000 federal grant. Mother Trinity CME Church is believed to be the first established Christian Methodist Episcopal (CME) Church in the country. It's not in the best shape right now, but soon that will change. "So one of the pillars of our charter is historic preservation. So it's very important to us," said Russ Gambill, Vice Chairman of the Augusta Canal Authority. Mother Trinity CME began in 1840, when about 125 enslaved people got permission to break off from St. John United Methodist Church to form their own church, something that didn't happen often. Over the decades the building evolved. "Before this building was built, and this building has been through several renovations in the past. items.t: Fatal vehicle crash, fire reported on Silver Bluff Road Wednesday
items.x: AIKEN, S.C. (WJBF) – The Aiken County Coroner's Office confirmed it responded to a deadly single-vehicle crash on the 3300 block of Silver Bluff Road on Wednesday. According to the coroner's office, the driver of a 2023 Subaru was traveling east on Silver Bluff Road when the vehicle exited the road to the right, went down an embankment and struck a tree before bursting into flames. The driver was not immediately identified due to thermal injuries and was pronounced deceased on scene at 10:55 am. An autopsy will be held in Newberry to assist in positive identification, and to determine the cause and manner of death. The coroner's office and the South Carolina Highway Patrol are continuing to investigate.

items.t: Understanding CPO cars: What does certified pre-owned mean?
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) With new-car prices near record highs, certified pre-owned vehicles (CPOs) offer buyers an affordable alternative to buying new, along with additional inspections and warranty protection. What Does Certified Pre-Owned Mean? If you’re shopping for a car, you’ve likely come across CPO vehicles. But what does that mean exactly, and how do they differ from traditional used cars? A certified pre-owned car is a used vehicle that meets the age, mileage, and condition requirements of a manufacturer or dealer certification program. CPO cars undergo a multipoint inspection and generally include additional warranty coverage, though the coverage and certification standards vary by program. Many CPO vehicles also include benefits such as roadside assistance, access to a loaner vehicle, and trip interruption coverage. items.t: The science and politics behind the panic over ultraprocessed foods
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Ultraprocessed foods have a terrible reputation. Studies have linked them with multiple chronic diseases . Journalists and health influencers characterize them as poison . Some public health experts call for a global halt to producing and consuming them. But the debate around ultraprocessed foods is not nearly as settled as it may seem. As a researcher who studies social movements for healthy and sustainable food, I have been documenting the history of processed foods and examining debates around the science and politics of ultraprocessing . items.t: Toyota simplifies the 2027 Corolla Cross lineup
items.x: (TestMiles) The 2027 Corolla Cross returns with gas and hybrid powertrains, fewer hybrid grades, standard safety tech and pricing from $25,535. Toyota is taking a light-touch approach to the 2027 Corolla Cross. Rather than redesigning its smallest mainstream SUV again, the company is carrying over most of the equipment introduced for 2026 and making one notable change: the hybrid range is easier to understand. For 2027, the gas-powered Corolla Cross remains available in L, LE and XLE grades, with front-wheel drive or all-wheel drive depending on configuration. The hybrid lineup drops the previous S grade, leaving SE and XSE models, both with standard electronic all-wheel drive. Toyota says the new model year will begin reaching U.S. dealerships this fall. items.t: Falling brick hits child in Queens: NYPD
items.x: MASPETH, Queens (PIX11) A 6-year-old girl is recovering after being hit by a falling brick in Maspeth on Thursday evening, according to the NYPD. The incident happened around 7:37 p.m. Discover more local reporting on our homepage Department of Buildings inspectors responded to 59-01 Garage Maspeth Avenue. They discovered that part of a brick veneer had detached from the side of a garage building and had fallen onto the sidewalk below. A violation was issued to the property owner for failing to maintain the garage building. Police say the child was taken to a local hospital in stable condition. What Does Certified Pre-Owned Mean? If you’re shopping for a car, you’ve likely come across CPO vehicles. But what does that mean exactly, and how do they differ from traditional used cars? A certified pre-owned car is a used vehicle that meets the age, mileage, and condition requirements of a manufacturer or dealer certification program. CPO cars undergo a multipoint inspection and generally include additional warranty coverage, though the coverage and certification standards vary by program. Many CPO vehicles also include benefits such as roadside assistance, access to a loaner vehicle, and trip interruption coverage. items.t: North Carolina mail-in ballot restrictions to remain through midterms, judge rules
items.x: ( The Hill ) A federal judge ruled Monday that North Carolina is permitted to keep its strict mail-in ballot rules in place for November’s election, which were changed just before ballots were mailed in September. In the ruling, Judge Thomas D. Shroeder wrote that it was too close to the election to change the rules again, and that plaintiffs waited too long to file their motion. “The Supreme Court has repeatedly admonished lower courts that they ‘should ordinarily not alter the election rules on the eve of an election,’” Shroeder wrote. “Here, ‘[t]he election is not merely upcoming; it has already started.’” North Carolina’s state board of elections updated the state’s rules to disqualify ballots where the signature does not match the name on the voter’s application. The new procedures also direct county election officials not to count votes if the inner envelope is not properly sealed.

items.t: Understanding CPO cars: What does certified pre-owned mean?
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) With new-car prices near record highs, certified pre-owned vehicles (CPOs) offer buyers an affordable alternative to buying new, along with additional inspections and warranty protection. What Does Certified Pre-Owned Mean? If you’re shopping for a car, you’ve likely come across CPO vehicles. But what does that mean exactly, and how do they differ from traditional used cars? A certified pre-owned car is a used vehicle that meets the age, mileage, and condition requirements of a manufacturer or dealer certification program. CPO cars undergo a multipoint inspection and generally include additional warranty coverage, though the coverage and certification standards vary by program. Many CPO vehicles also include benefits such as roadside assistance, access to a loaner vehicle, and trip interruption coverage. items.t: The science and politics behind the panic over ultraprocessed foods

items.t: A novel mRNA cancer vaccine helps reduce the chances of melanoma patients’ tumors returning
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — A first-of-its-kind cancer vaccine is significantly reducing the chances that melanoma patients’ tumors come back, according to results of a major study released Thursday by drugmakers Moderna and Merck. The vaccine was custom-brewed for each patient to match their tumor. Adding it to a standard post-surgery treatment reduced by 42% the risk of melanoma returning two years after surgery, according to the most advanced study to date of this new strategy for fighting cancer. “The field has been looking for a win, and I think this one is a big one,” said Dr. Hussein Tawbi of MD Anderson Cancer Center in Houston, one of the researchers in the international study. The vaccine, called intismeran, is made with the same Nobel Prize-winning mRNA technology that was behind COVID-19 vaccines. Last week, a 59-33 win over North Central kept them in 1st place in Region 4-1A. Quarterback Jaylen Morris played a big part in the victory with 320 yards (rushing & passing) and he accounted for 6 touchdowns. Lamar is now 8-1 on the season with their biggest match of the year looming. They'll travel to 2nd ranked Central on Friday and that will decide who will win the Region and earn home field advantage in the playoffs.

items.t: Blitz Grand Strand player of the week – Yaquarious Floyd
items.x: AYNOR, SC (WBTW) The Aynor Blue Jackets picked up a much needed region win last Friday over Lakewood, 43-18. Freshman running back Yaquarious Floyd had one of the best games in his career, totaling 229 yards (rushing & returns) and 3 scores to help aid in the Region 6-3A victory. Head Coach Jason Allen told News13 he has the potential to become one of the best players in program history when its all said and done. Floyd is also a stand out wrestler in the winter time. Aynor is off this week, they will face Loris to close out the regular season next Friday, October 30th.

items.t: Frank plants more lettuce in the News13 garden
items.x: While gardens are still going strong with warm season plants, it is just a matter of time before we get a killing freeze, and the growing season will end. In the WBTW garden, the cucumbers, peppers and tomatoes will not last much longer, and then I will have empty space in the garden… something I really don’t like! This time of year, it is difficult to start seeds in the ground. Soil temperatures are cool, and that slows down germination. Plus, once we start to get frost and freezing temperatures, young seedlings have a hard time surviving, even winter hardy plants. To get around this, we will start some seeds inside. They will sprout faster in the warmth and will be protected against any cold snaps. Once these seedlings are a few weeks old, they will be hardy enough to survive cold nights. items.t: Tom Skerritt, Emmy-winning actor with roles in ‘Top Gun’ and ‘Alien,’ dies
items.x: NEW YORK (AP) — Tom Skerritt, the Emmy-winning actor who embodied a solid, wry authority figure, whether as a flight instructor in “Top Gun,” a tough-but-fair sheriff on TV's “Picket Fences,” or the doomed captain of “Alien,” has died. He was 93. Skerritt died Wednesday of natural causes, his family said in a statement. “While the world knew Tom through his remarkable acting career, we knew him for his humor, curiosity, wisdom, generosity and the love he brought into our lives. He cared deeply about imagination, creativity, storytelling, service, veterans, the natural world and helping others find and share their own voices,” the statement said. Skerritt was twice nominated for an Emmy — both for “Picket Fences,” winning outstanding lead actor in a drama series in 1993. items.t: Americans spent $110B on the lottery in 2024, analysis finds
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — Americans spent $110.4 billion on lottery tickets in 2024, according to an analysis of U.S. Census Bureau data. That's up from the $109 billion spent in 2023 and $103.3 billion in 2022. According to the analysis by LendingTree, the average American spent $323 on lottery tickets in 2024. Per-capita spending fell in 28 states, rose in 16, and stayed the same in California. Massachusetts residents spent more than $900 Massachusetts again led the nation by a wide margin, with residents spending an average of $904 per person in 2024, down slightly from $915 in 2023 but still 43.5% higher than any other state. Spending was second-highest in Virginia at $630 per person and third-highest in Rhode Island at $567. North Dakota residents spent the least, at $51 per person. Wyoming, Montana, New Mexico and Oklahoma were the only other states where spending fell under $100 per person

items.t: Conway couple wins $50K on $2 scratch-off ticket
items.x: CONWAY, S.C. (WBTW) A Conway couple turned a $2 scratch-off ticket into $50,000, South Carolina lottery officials said Thursday. The wife picked out the Jumbo Bucks ticket after filling up her car at the Sunhouse on Highway 905 in Conway, lottery officials said. She scratched the ticket first, uncovering the barcode and scanning it with her phone. "Then I handed the ticket to my husband," she told lottery officials. Her husband scratched the rest of the ticket before screaming and jumping up and down. "I was amazed," the wife said. "My husband said we both got a part of it." The couple plans to use the winnings on a vacation. The odds of winning $50,000 playing Jumbo Bucks are 1 in 600,000. Seven more top prizes remain in the game. items.x: (NEXSTAR) – Meteorologists are continuing to warn of the El Niño weather event expected to impact us throughout the winter, with a new climate outlook from the World Meteorological Organization suggesting it "could be unprecedented in strength." In an update Wednesday, the WMO said this year's El Niño weather pattern could be so strong, it could "literally [be] off the monitoring charts that we have used for the past four decades." A main focus of forecasting El Niño comes down to sea surface temperatures. In the Pacific, an "anomaly of 0.5 [degrees Celsius] above normal" can trigger an El Niño alert from the WMO, according to the United Nations. items.t: Think You Know Martha's Vineyard? The African American Heritage Trail Tells The Black History Most Visitors Never See
items.x: Source: Thomas Barwick / Getty Every family has somebody who knows the stories behind the stories. They remember whose ambition began the family's legacy, who owned the house where everyone gathered, and who made a way when there wasn't one. On Martha's Vineyard, the African American Heritage Trail has spent nearly three decades making sure the island's Black history is remembered with that same care. Martha's Vineyard's reputation as a beloved summer destination for Black families is well earned. Its history also includes the people who established businesses, created gathering places, built institutions, and challenged discrimination so that future generations could live, work, rest, and return. items.t: Metastatic Breast Cancer Awareness Day: Understanding Stage 4 And The Fight For More Time
items.x: Source: kali9 / Getty October 13 is Metastatic Breast Cancer Awareness Day, a day dedicated to raising awareness about Stage 4 breast cancer, amplifying the voices of those living with the disease, and calling for more research, better treatments, and increased funding. Because when it comes to breast cancer, awareness should go beyond the pink ribbons. It should also include the realities of living with cancer that has spread. According to Breastcancer.org , more than 2 million women worldwide are diagnosed with breast cancer each year. Behind every statistic is a person, a family, and a future suddenly filled with questions. A cancer diagnosis can feel like an incredibly heavy weight to carry, but understanding the disease, recognizing the warning signs, and knowing what treatment options are available can help people feel more informed and empowered as they navigate their next steps.

items.t: Durant scores 22, Sheppard hits five 3-pointers to lead Rockets to a win in Atlanta’s home opener
items.x: ATLANTA (AP) — Kevin Durant scored 22 points and both Reed Sheppard and Tari Eason had 19 points as the Houston Rockets beat the Atlanta Hawks 121-114. The Hawks nearly pulled off a comeback by cutting Houston’s 20-point lead down to five in the closing moments, but Durant knocked down two three throws with 18.9 seconds remaining to push the lead back to three possessions. items.t: Understanding CPO cars: What does certified pre-owned mean?
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) With new-car prices near record highs, certified pre-owned vehicles (CPOs) offer buyers an affordable alternative to buying new, along with additional inspections and warranty protection. What Does Certified Pre-Owned Mean? If you’re shopping for a car, you’ve likely come across CPO vehicles. But what does that mean exactly, and how do they differ from traditional used cars? A certified pre-owned car is a used vehicle that meets the age, mileage, and condition requirements of a manufacturer or dealer certification program. CPO cars undergo a multipoint inspection and generally include additional warranty coverage, though the coverage and certification standards vary by program. Many CPO vehicles also include benefits such as roadside assistance, access to a loaner vehicle, and trip interruption coverage. items.x: Early voting is surging in several key battleground states, giving Democrats hope that their strength in midterm polling could translate into a turnout advantage in November. In North Carolina, more than 1.2 million early ballots have been accepted, a 37 percent increase from the same point leading up to the 2022 midterms, according to an analysis released Friday by Catawba College political scientist Michael Bitzer. items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — A first-of-its-kind cancer vaccine is significantly reducing the chances that melanoma patients’ tumors come back, according to results of a major study released Thursday by drugmakers Moderna and Merck. The vaccine was custom-brewed for each patient to match their tumor. Adding it to a standard post-surgery treatment reduced by 42% the risk of melanoma returning two years after surgery, according to the most advanced study to date of this new strategy for fighting cancer. “The field has been looking for a win and I think this one is a big one,” said Dr. Hussein Tawbi of MD Anderson Cancer Center in Houston, one of the researchers in the international study. (WKRN) — From shrinking ponds to dry pastures, this year’s drought is taking a toll on Middle Tennessee cattle farmers, forcing them to spend more money to keep their animals healthy while preparing for an uncertain winter. At Robert Elliott and Sons, a family cattle farm in Adams, owner William Elliott said this year’s weather has brought some unusual challenges. His family purchased the land in 1807, and his father started the cattle operation in 1935. Now, more than 90 years later, Elliott is still raising cattle on the property and adapting to whatever Mother Nature brings. “I’ve never seen a year that had two dry spells in it,” Elliott said. Across the farm, the effects of the drought are easy to see. Maiz de la Vida in the Pie Town neighborhood of Nashville received Bib Gourmand distinction, one of three new restaurants in the state to earn the award that honors high-quality, moderately priced dining experiences for the first time. items.t: Toyota simplifies the 2027 Corolla Cross lineup
items.x: (TestMiles) The 2027 Corolla Cross returns with gas and hybrid powertrains, fewer hybrid grades, standard safety tech and pricing from $25,535. Toyota is taking a light-touch approach to the 2027 Corolla Cross. Rather than redesigning its smallest mainstream SUV again, the company is carrying over most of the equipment introduced for 2026 and making one notable change: the hybrid range is easier to understand. For 2027, the gas-powered Corolla Cross remains available in L, LE and XLE grades, with front-wheel drive or all-wheel drive depending on configuration. The hybrid lineup drops the previous S grade, leaving SE and XSE models, both with standard electronic all-wheel drive. Toyota says the new model year will begin reaching U.S. dealerships this fall. items.t: Proposed Kentucky nuclear campus would be the largest in the country
items.x: LEWIS COUNTY, Ky. (WOWK) A nuclear plant has been proposed in Lewis County, Kentucky, and, if built, it would be the largest nuclear power campus in the United States. The project, by The Nuclear Company, is called Prosperity One. The campus, as proposed, could accommodate up to six Westinghouse AP1000 reactors and generate about 6.6 gigawatts of electricity. The potential site sits along the Ohio River. He told News 2's sister station, WOWK, that he sees the proposal as a job opportunity for the county's future. items.t: Supreme Court won’t revive Trump administration’s transgender inmate policy
items.x: ( The Hill ) The Supreme Court refused the Trump administration’s bid to stop providing transgender inmates hormone treatments and certain surgeries on Wednesday , declining to lift a lower judge’s block over the dissents of two conservative justices. The Bureau of Prisons policy would taper treatments for inmates currently receiving them, and officials would also need to stop providing social accommodations, like hair-removal devices. Solicitor General D. John Sauer asserted the changes are needed to maintain “institutional security” in federal prisons. It’s a rare loss for the Trump administration, which has emerged victorious more than two dozen times when asking the high court for emergency relief after a judge blocked an aspect of President Donald Trump’s agenda. items.t: ‘Behemoth’ El Niño could be ‘off the charts,’ forecasters warn
items.x: (NEXSTAR) – Meteorologists are continuing to warn of the El Niño weather event expected to impact us throughout the winter, with a new climate outlook from the World Meteorological Organization suggesting it "could be unprecedented in strength." In an update Wednesday, Oct. 21, the WMO said this year's El Niño weather pattern could be so strong, it could "literally [be] off the monitoring charts that we have used for the past four decades." A main focus of forecasting El Niño comes down to sea surface temperatures. In the Pacific, an "anomaly of 0.5 [degrees Celsius] above normal" can trigger an El Niño alert from the WMO, according to the United Nations. Between next month and January, WMO has forecast temperatures could rise 3.8 degrees Celsius above average. items.t: Pennsylvania warns of congenital measles amid ‘increase of measles cases during pregnancy’
items.x: ( The Hill ) — The Pennsylvania Department of Health issued a warning to doctors Monday about an increase in measles cases during pregnancy, along with rising concern about congenital measles, a disease rarely seen in the U.S. The alert said congenital measles — meaning measles infection in a newborn contracted from the mother — was identified “for the first time in decades.” There are more than 1,200 measles cases in Pennsylvania, and the health department has confirmed five deaths, though a sixth death was reported earlier this month in Franklin County. Few pediatricians have treated a newborn with congenital measles, presenting a clinical challenge for physicians. 6th measles-associated death reported in Pennsylvania In response to rising cases, the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) added a “frequently asked questions” page about congenital measles to its website in September. items.x: NASHVILLE, Tenn. (WKRN) — The Federal Emergency Management Agency has approved $64 million in funding for Tennessee and Kentucky for disaster recovery and resilience projects in both states. According to FEMA, Tennessee will receive more than $15 million for 27 separate projects, including $5.5 million for Middle Tennessee Electric Membership Corporation for utility repairs and $2 million for Metro Nashville-Davidson County for debris removal operations, as well as the repair of roads bridges and buildings. The state was approved for more than $13.4 million through FEMA's Public Assistance program, which provides federal reimbursement to communities after a disaster for debris removal, emergency protective measures to reduce or eliminate disaster impacts, and to repair or rebuild damaged critical infrastructure. items.t: Tom Skerritt, Emmy-winning actor with roles in ‘Top Gun’ and ‘Alien,’ dies
items.x: NEW YORK (AP) — Tom Skerritt, the Emmy-winning actor who embodied a solid, wry authority figure, whether as a flight instructor in “Top Gun,” a tough-but-fair sheriff on TV's “Picket Fences” or the doomed captain of “Alien,” has died. He was 93. Skerritt died Wednesday of natural causes, his family said in a statement. “While the world knew Tom through his remarkable acting career, we knew him for his humor, curiosity, wisdom, generosity and the love he brought into our lives. He cared deeply about imagination, creativity, storytelling, service, veterans, the natural world and helping others find and share their own voices,” the statement said. Skerritt was twice nominated for an Emmy — both for “Picket Fences,” winning outstanding lead actor in a drama series in 1993. items.x: [WATCH: In the video player above, learn which words Americans have the hardest time spelling. ] ( WJW ) – Say what? items.t: Understanding CPO cars: What does certified pre-owned mean?
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) With new-car prices near record highs, certified pre-owned vehicles (CPOs) offer buyers an affordable alternative to buying new, along with additional inspections and warranty protection. What Does Certified Pre-Owned Mean? If you’re shopping for a car, you’ve likely come across CPO vehicles. But what does that mean exactly, and how do they differ from traditional used cars? A certified pre-owned car is a used vehicle that meets the age, mileage, and condition requirements of a manufacturer or dealer certification program. CPO cars undergo a multipoint inspection and generally include additional warranty coverage, though the coverage and certification standards vary by program. Many CPO vehicles also include benefits such as roadside assistance, access to a loaner vehicle, and trip interruption coverage. items.t: The science and politics behind the panic over ultraprocessed foods

items.x: WASHINGTON, D.C. (NEXSTAR) A stalled effort to block companies from using AI to set prices is gaining new attention on the campaign trail. As Democrats put affordability front and center in their campaigns, there's one issue some candidates are focused on: personalized prices. Personalized pricing, which is also called surveillance pricing, is when companies use your personal data to determine how much you pay for their products or services. That means you could pay more than someone else for the same item. "The number of people who come up to me and say, Gosh, Mark, I saw your ad, and that's crazy,'" said Sen. Mark Warner (D-Virginia), who is running for reelection this year. Warner has proposed a federal ban on surveillance pricing. "This is the kind of part where technology gets creepy," Warner said. items.x: CLEVELAND (WJW) – A 24-year-old Brian Branch has been sentenced to 25 27 years in prison after pleading guilty to firing at police during a pursuit that injured five officers . Prosecutors said it started May 23rd, when officers responded to a shooting on Fleet Avenue in Cleveland . 2 suspects indicted in Cleveland AutoZone shooting Police said Branch was spotted circling the area, then opened fire on officers before fleeing. He fired again during a pursuit that ended in Shaker Heights , where he crashed into another vehicle and a building before running on foot. He was arrested, and a gun was recovered from his vehicle. Five officers were injured, including three hurt in crashes. A police K-9 was also in one of the cruisers but was not hurt. In court on Wednesday, the judge agreed to the recommended sentence, which prosecutors said was supported by the officers injured in the shooting.

items.x: Video above: Pope delivers thanks to faithful from Vatican window one day after return from hospital on Oct. 18, 2026. VATICAN CITY (AP) — Pope Leo XIV needs no further treatment for lung cancer after follow-up tests confirmed the disease was localized, the Vatican said in a statement Wednesday. Leo, 71, had the lower lobe of his right lung removed last week in the first major health event of his 17-month pontificate. The surgery confirmed he had adenocarcinoma , the most common type of lung cancer. He left the hospital on Saturday, four days after surgery and well ahead of the week-long hospital stay the Vatican had initially anticipated. items.x: (TestMiles) Honda’s reach stretches from everyday equipment to business jets, with endurance racing revealing the challenges behind dependable power. Ask someone to name the world’s biggest engine manufacturer, and the answers might include Toyota, an aircraft-engine company or a name associated with very expensive sports cars. Honda probably would not be everyone’s first guess. Yet Honda describes itself as the world’s largest engine manufacturer, a claim that makes more sense once the counting extends beyond cars. Motorcycles, generators, pumps, lawn equipment and marine outboards all belong in the picture. So does aviation, through the GE Honda partnership behind the HF120 turbofan. items.t: Florida puts 77-year-old man to death for a deputy’s killing
items.x: STARKE, Fla. (AP) — Florida carried out its 18th execution of the year on Tuesday under Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis ’ aggressive use of the death penalty in his final term. William Reaves, 77, was pronounced dead at 6:12 p.m. following a three-drug injection at Florida State Prison near Starke. He was convicted of first-degree murder in the September 1986 shooting death of Indian River County sheriff's deputy Richard Raczkoski. The death chamber curtain went up promptly at the 6 p.m. execution time with Reaves already strapped to a gurney with an IV in his arm. Asked if he had any last words, he replied ”No, I do not.” The injection began immediately after that. About 30 seconds later, Reaves took several big breaths and then stopped moving. items.t: Understanding CPO cars: What does certified pre-owned mean?
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) With new-car prices near record highs, certified pre-owned vehicles (CPOs) offer buyers an affordable alternative to buying new, along with additional inspections and warranty protection. What Does Certified Pre-Owned Mean? If you’re shopping for a car, you’ve likely come across CPO vehicles. But what does that mean exactly, and how do they differ from traditional used cars? A certified pre-owned car is a used vehicle that meets the age, mileage, and condition requirements of a manufacturer or dealer certification program. CPO cars undergo a multipoint inspection and generally include additional warranty coverage, though the coverage and certification standards vary by program. Many CPO vehicles also include benefits such as roadside assistance, access to a loaner vehicle, and trip interruption coverage. items.t: The science and politics behind the panic over ultraprocessed foods
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Ultraprocessed foods have a terrible reputation. Studies have linked them with multiple chronic diseases . Journalists and health influencers characterize them as poison . Some public health experts call for a global halt to producing and consuming them. Josephine is currently moving to the northeast at 17 mph with sustained winds of 65 mph. What is a subtropical storm? Unlike a traditional tropical storm, which gets its energy primarily from warm ocean water, a subtropical storm has characteristics of both tropical and non-tropical weather systems. On Monday, the state rested its case after calling its final witness, North Carolina State Bureau of Investigation special agent Justin Heinrich. Heinrich is the lead investigator who became involved in the case about a year after the crime happened in 2013. Court took a one-day break Tuesday and was back Wednesday as the defense was expected to begin calling up their witnesses. However, in a surprise move, the attorneys said they would not call anyone to the stand — including Salguero Olivares himself — and would rest their case without presenting any evidence. The amount of money reported as lost increased every year from 2021 through 2025. It rose from about $95 million in 2021 to just over $342 million in 2025. items.t: Coastal low moves away, more cool air coming
items.x: A week after record heat hit central North Carolina, cool weather persists with another shot of chilly air expected this weekend. Fall-like weather will continue through the week with no chance for rain in the foreseeable future. This is great for the fair, but bad news for our persistent drought. Meanwhile, a developing Nor’easter off the East Coast is helping keep a long stretch of cool, dry weather to central North Carolina. While coastal areas will deal with gusty winds and rough surf conditions, central North Carolina remains on the drier side of the system. High pressure to the west and low pressure offshore will maintain a northerly to northeasterly breeze throughout much of the week. There will be a small drop in temperatures Friday and this weekend, with highs in the upper 60s, but mostly sunny skies and dry weather will continue. The downside is the continued lack of rainfall.

The study from LendingTree found Raleigh has 29.1 accidents per 1,000 drivers, which is 11.2 more than the national average of 17.9 accidents per drivers. items.t: Understanding CPO cars: What does certified pre-owned mean?
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) With new-car prices near record highs, certified pre-owned vehicles (CPOs) offer buyers an affordable alternative to buying new, along with additional inspections and warranty protection. What Does Certified Pre-Owned Mean? If you’re shopping for a car, you’ve likely come across CPO vehicles. But what does that mean exactly, and how do they differ from traditional used cars? A certified pre-owned car is a used vehicle that meets the age, mileage, and condition requirements of a manufacturer or dealer certification program. CPO cars undergo a multipoint inspection and generally include additional warranty coverage, though the coverage and certification standards vary by program. Many CPO vehicles also include benefits such as roadside assistance, access to a loaner vehicle, and trip interruption coverage. items.t: The science and politics behind the panic over ultraprocessed foods

items.t: Halloween costume swaps: Reducing the night’s spooky environmental impact
items.x: LOS ANGELES (AP) — Braddock Sandoval perused tables with wigs, a Darth Vader mask, a black tutu and other items and garments on an unusually sizzling day in Los Angeles. He found a Hawaiian flower necklace and a shark costume and tried them on. The chemistry professor at Occidental College heard about a campus swap where he could pick out a free Halloween costume with the goal of keeping it from being thrown away. Curious and in need of one, he swung by to see what he could find. “I think there’s too much cheap plastic waste in this world. So the idea that people are recycling costumes is fantastic, both for budgets, like me, but also just for the planet,” Sandoval said with a laugh. He planned to attend a Halloween dance party dressed as a great white shark eating a tourist — a costume inspired by the freebies he found at the swap. Every Halloween, costumes get their big moment. items.t: A novel mRNA cancer vaccine helps reduce the chances of melanoma patients’ tumors returning
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — A first-of-its-kind cancer vaccine is significantly reducing the chances that melanoma patients’ tumors come back, according to results of a major study released Thursday by drugmakers Moderna and Merck. The vaccine was custom-brewed for each patient to match their tumor. Adding it to a standard post-surgery treatment reduced by 42% the risk of melanoma returning two years after surgery, according to the most advanced study to date of this new strategy for fighting cancer. “The field has been looking for a win and I think this one is a big one,” said Dr. Hussein Tawbi of MD Anderson Cancer Center in Houston, one of the researchers in the international study. The vaccine, called intismeran, is made with the same Nobel Prize-winning mRNA technology that was behind COVID-19 vaccines. items.t: Crumbl shutters dozens of locations nationwide: Reports
items.x: (KTLA) Crumbl, the bakery chain known for its rotating weekly menu and oversized cookies, has recently shuttered dozens of locations nationwide, according to multiple reports. At least 57 locations of the dessert chain have closed this year, according to an analysis of local reports and a location count on the company's website cited by Restaurant Business. Operators have warned of an insolvency crisis and say more closures could follow. At least 55 franchises are listed for sale on various broker websites, according to the report. In California, the closures span the state and include locations in Paso Robles, Pismo Beach, Hanford, Ladera Ranch, Mira Mesa, Cupertino, and Westlake Village. Shuttered stores have also been reported in Alabama, Florida, and Kentucky, according to SFGATE. Nexstar's KTLA reached out to Crumbl about the reports but did not receive a response before publication

Her body has since been transported to the medical examiner for an autopsy, according to the post. The attorney general’s office did not detail the circumstances surrounding the teen’s injuries. But Mexico’s El Universal reported that the teen fell from what appeared to be a pendulum-type ride that was set up temporarily for the festival. items.t: Biscuit Belly to open two Richmond-area locations

items.t: Richmond Redevelopment and Housing Authority labeled ‘troubled’ by federal government
items.x: RICHMOND, Va. (WRIC) — The Richmond Redevelopment and Housing Authority (RRHA) has been designated "troubled" by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). RRHA received an overall score of 58 out of 100 after a review of fiscal year 2024, according to the interim report from the Public Housing Assessment System (PHAS) from HUD dated Friday, Sept. 25. Under federal law, "troubled" means the agency has failed to meet federal performance and operational standards. HUD grades housing authorities using the PHAS, which evaluates performance across four primary categories: financial stability and management, physical condition of properties, management practices and occupancy rates and capital fund utilization. items.t: Man to spend 17 years in prison after Richmond Fire lieutenant shot, killed on Thanksgiving night in 2019
items.x: HOPEWELL, Va. (WRIC) — A Hopewell man will spend 17 years in prison nearly seven years after a lieutenant with the Richmond Fire Department was shot and killed on Thanksgiving night in 2019. Officers with the Hopewell Police Department responded to the 1000 block of Sunnyside Avenue around 11:40 p.m. on Nov. 28, 2019 — Thanksgiving night — for reports of a shooting . When officers arrived, they found 33-year-old Ashley Berry of Chesterfield County, a mother of three and a veteran of the Richmond Fire Department since 2011, with serious gunshot wounds. She was taken to a local hospital, where she later died the following day. Her uncle, William Berry, told 8News that she died while shielding her 5-year-old son from gunfire. items.t: Over $730K in illegal drugs seized across Virginia in one week: VSP
items.x: RICHMOND, Va. (WRIC) Over $730,000 worth of illegal drugs were recovered last week by Virginia State Police (VSP) as part of its crime suppression operations. According to an Oct. 23 report, VSP recovered over 98 pounds of illegal drugs with the help of local and federal agencies throughout Virginia between Oct. 14 and Oct. 20. This included 14.1 ounces of cocaine, 88 pounds of marijuana, 6.1 pounds of THC consumables, 3.1 pounds of methamphetamine, and 4 ounces of fentanyl. Combined, these drugs could have been sold for an estimated $733,227, VSP said. A VSP spokesperson said that typically, the drugs recovered by state police are safely incinerated to destroy them while avoiding fume inhalation by the public. items.t: Lost caiman found, wrangled from creek by Oklahoma deputies
items.x: NORMAN, Okla. (KFOR) – A caiman that had been on the loose in Cleveland County, Oklahoma, for months has finally been captured. His brush with freedom finally came to a screeching halt Tuesday night. Cleveland County deputies found the caiman in a creek bed near the Sunnylane Estates in Norman. They say it took neighbors about a month to be able to locate and spot the caiman, and then took deputies a few weeks to be able to wrangle it and get it back to the owners. "Trying to come out with ten fingers. That was my main goal," said Deputy Ben McKinney of the Cleveland County Sheriff's Office. "It's the creek bed, we're walking up and down it and I see a pair of eyes looking at me. I was like, that sure looks like it," McKinney recalled of finding the caiman. items.t: Friday is the deadline to register for Virginia midterm elections
items.x: RICHMOND, Va. (WRIC) Friday is the last day to register to vote ahead of the Virginia midterm elections on Nov. 3. According to the Virginia Public Access Project , 929,891 votes have been cast in Virginia as of Thursday, Oct. 22. Four years ago, 12 days out from election day, roughly 480,000 Virginians had voted. Officials said it's because voting in Virginia is easy to access. "You don't have to have a reason to request a ballot anymore," said Stephanie Iles, the Norfolk Director of Elections and General Registrar. "We can automatically send you a ballot if you get on our permanent absentee list. Coming out to vote early, we have 45 days of early voting before every election." Virginians vote for the U.S. Senate, House of Representatives, proposed constitutional amendments and referendums like the 1 for Schools sales tax in certain areas. items.x: (TestMiles) The 2027 Corolla Cross returns with gas and hybrid powertrains, fewer hybrid grades, standard safety tech and pricing from $25,535. Toyota is taking a light-touch approach to the 2027 Corolla Cross. Rather than redesigning its smallest mainstream SUV again, the company is carrying over most of the equipment introduced for 2026 and making one notable change: the hybrid range is easier to understand. For 2027, the gas-powered Corolla Cross remains available in L, LE and XLE grades, with front-wheel drive or all-wheel drive depending on configuration. The hybrid lineup drops the previous S grade, leaving SE and XSE models, both with standard electronic all-wheel drive. Toyota says the new model year will begin reaching U.S. dealerships this fall. items.t: Americans spent $110B on the lottery in 2024, analysis finds
items.x: (NewsNation) — Americans spent $110.4 billion on lottery tickets in 2024, according to an analysis of U.S. Census Bureau data. That's up from the $109 billion spent in 2023 and $103.3 billion in 2022. According to the analysis by LendingTree, the average American spent $323 on lottery tickets in 2024. Per-capita spending fell in 28 states, rose in 16, and stayed the same in California. Massachusetts residents spent more than $900 Massachusetts again led the nation by a wide margin, with residents spending an average of $904 per person in 2024, down slightly from $915 in 2023 but still 43.5% higher than any other state. Spending was second-highest in Virginia at $630 per person and third-highest in Rhode Island at $567. North Dakota residents spent the least, at $51 per person. Wyoming, Montana, New Mexico and Oklahoma were the only other states where spending fell under $100 per person.

items.x: (NEXSTAR) – Meteorologists are continuing to warn of the El Niño weather event expected to impact us throughout the winter, with a new climate outlook from the World Meteorological Organization suggesting it "could be unprecedented in strength." In an update Wednesday, the WMO said this year's El Niño weather pattern could be so strong, it could "literally [be] off the monitoring charts that we have used for the past four decades." A main focus of forecasting El Niño comes down to sea surface temperatures. In the Pacific, an "anomaly of 0.5 [degrees Celsius] above normal" can trigger an El Niño alert from the WMO, according to the United Nations. Between next month and January, WMO has forecast temperatures could rise 3.8 degrees Celsius above average. items.t: 16-year-old boy last seen in Northumberland found safe
items.x: NORTHUMBERLAND COUNTY, Va. (WRIC) A missing 16-year-old boy who was last seen in Northumberland County was found safe, state police say. Just before 11 p.m. on Wednesday, Oct. 21, Virginia State Police issued a CODI Alert for 16-year-old Cayden James Dawson, who was last seen at about 7:36 p.m. along Fruit Plain Road in the Callao area. His disappearance was believed to pose a credible threat to his health and safety. The morning of Thursday, Oct. 22, the Northumberland County Sheriff's Office took to Facebook to share that Dawson was safely located in Essex County's Tappahannock area.

items.x: HANOVER COUNTY, Va. (WRIC) — With Virginia’s retail marijuana market launching next summer, local governments are planning the framework for how cannabis businesses will operate in their communities. As Democrats put affordability front and center in their campaigns, there's one issue some candidates are focused on: personalized prices. Personalized pricing, which is also called surveillance pricing, is when companies use your personal data to determine how much you pay for their products or services. items.x: HONOLULU (KHON) An increase in costs is easily visible to consumers during their grocery shopping. For Hawaii residents, one item that continues to see sticker shock is the skyrocketing price of eggs. On average, it's now $10.06 to buy a dozen eggs in Honolulu, the Department of Agriculture and Biosecurity, or DAB, announced on Tuesday. According to statistics from DAB's Market Analysis and News Branch, the price of a dozen eggs spiked more than 11 percent in the past year, officials said. The report found that eggs from the U.S. continent increased slightly more than 1 percent, from $7.78 a dozen to $7.87. But local organic eggs saw the highest jump, with the average price for a dozen up by 22 percent from the first quarter of 2026 to the second quarter. items.x: ( The Hill ) – A judge in New Mexico ordered the technology giant Meta to pay $25 billion after a jury found the company liable for misleading users about its privacy and content policies. items.t: Supreme Court won’t revive Trump administration’s transgender inmate policy
items.x: (The Hill) The Supreme Court refused the Trump administration’s bid to stop providing transgender inmates hormone treatments and certain surgeries on Wednesday , declining to lift a lower judge’s block over the dissents of two conservative justices. The Bureau of Prisons (BOP) policy would taper treatments for inmates currently receiving them, and officials would also need to stop providing social accommodations, like hair-removal devices. Solicitor General D. John Sauer asserted the changes are needed to maintain “institutional security” in federal prisons. It’s a rare loss for the Trump administration, which has emerged victorious more than two dozen times when asking the high court for emergency relief after a judge blocked an aspect of President Donald Trump’s agenda. Justices Clarence Thomas and Samuel Alito, both members of the court's 6-3 conservative majority, publicly dissented.

Starting on Tuesday, Oct. 20, there will be daily intermittent lane closures on the Dumbarton Road bridge over the CSX railroad, which is located between Staples Mill and Byrdhill roads. (WJBF) – The Aiken County Coroner’s Office has identified a man whose body was found in a North Augusta field over the weekend, but investigators are still working to determine how he died. The man was identified as 51-year-old John L. Meyers III of Hephzibah, Georgia, according to Aiken County Coroner Darryl Ables. Workers discovered Meyers’ body shortly after noon Sunday, October 18, in a field in the 100 block of Philpot Lane. The Aiken County Coroner’s Office was notified at approximately 12:15 p.m. Ables told NewsChannel 6 the body was in stages of decomposition when it was discovered, making identification an early priority in the investigation. “One of the most paramount things we need to do is identify who is this person,” Ables said. The coroner confirmed that Meyers has since been identified and his family has been contacted. A forensic autopsy is scheduled

items.t: Georgia surpasses 1 million in-person early votes cast
items.x: GEORGIA (WSAV) — More than one million in-person early votes have been counted in the state of Georgia as of Tuesday, marking a sizable increase from the same point in the last midterm election cycle. Georgia Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger said, “We continue to break records each day of early voting. This is evidence that Georgians trust our election process. The strong turnout reflects the work our 159 county election officials do to make our elections free, fair, and fast.” Before noon Tuesday, 1,007,015 in-person early votes had been cast, which is a 12% increase from the same point in 2022. The overall turnout is 1,055,931, as 48,916 absentee ballots have been accepted. Early voting in Georgia continues through Oct. 30. To find early voting locations and hours in your county, visit the Secretary of State’s My Voter Page at https://mvp.sos.ga.gov. Election Day is Nov. 3.
