items.x: AUGUSTA, Ga. (WJBF) Eric Kennedy is a husband and father of three. He's been in recovery from drugs and alcohol for 16 years. Eric says what recovery has taught him is pretty simple: keep showing up, do the next right thing, and keep it practical. The founder of Recovery Vow , Eric's newest book, Loving Them Without Losing Us , teaches parents how to love their child without losing themselves, their marriage, or the rest of their family in the process. After starting Recovery Vow, Eric says he quickly realized addiction affects the entire family. Spouses need support, but so do parents of adolescent and adult children who are trying to understand the difference between helping and enabling while also protecting their marriage and the health of their family. items.t: Atlanta Falcons add Andy Dalton to quarterback room
items.x: ATLANTA, GA (WJBF)- The 2-4 Falcons added veteran quarterback Andy Dalton and released Cooper Rush. The 38-year-old has 16 years of NFL experience under his belt. He's thrown for over 39,000 yards and 254 touchdowns during his NFL career and has been on multiple teams, including the Cowboys, Bears, Bengals, Saints, and Panthers, and most recently on the Eagles. The 2-4 Falcons are back at home this week taking on the San Francisco 49ers. "I think Ian is always looking at ways to add to the roster. Andy was available, simple as that. I think the world of Cooper Rush, really like the person, so disappointed for him in that regard, but excited about the opportunity to add Andy." The Falcons host the undefeated San Francisco 49ers on Sunday at 1 p.m.

items.t: McCormick County family reflects on land lost through eminent domain as data center vote approaches
items.x: MCCORMICK COUNTY, S.C. (WJBF) – A McCormick County family is reflecting on its history of losing land through eminent domain as county leaders prepare to vote on rezoning requests for proposed data center development. For Kennetta Robertson, the steps of her family’s former home are more than just a piece of history. They’re a reminder of the generations who came before her and the land they once owned. In 1899, her great-grandparents, James and Francis Robertson, purchased nearly 400 acres of land in McCormick County for $2,000. But in the 1940s, the family says that land was taken through eminent domain for what would eventually become Strom Thurmond Lake. Today, the front steps are all that remain of the family’s former home. items.t: GBI Regional Office in Thomson named after Special Agent Bob Kirk
items.x: THOMSON, Ga. (WJBF) – The Georgia Bureau of Investigation's Regional Office in Thomson has a new name. The 11,000 square-foot building on Washington Road now bears the name of Special Agent Bob Kirk. Kirk was killed in the line of duty in August of 1988. He was only days away from celebrating two years with the agency. Every year since his death, the Bob Kirk General Investigations Award is presented to an agent with great work ethic who makes a difference in the field and community. items.t: Integrated Warning Team Meeting in Aiken
items.x: AIKEN, S.C. (WJBF)- The WJBF weather team participated in the Integrated Warning Team workshop hosted by the National Weather Service and the Aiken County Department of Emergency Management. This was a great opportunity to connect with key community partners and discuss ways to strengthen preparedness and response efforts for high-impact weather events. Chief Meteorologist Jenna Petracci participated in a panel discussion about Hurricane Helene and the team learned about upcoming improvements from the National Hurricane Center. They also talked about the potential impacts of a super El Niño, the current drought situation, and much more. The weather team looks forward to visiting the NWS office in Columbia in two weeks!

items.t: GDOT announces road projects in Jefferson and Emanuel counties
items.x: GEORGIA (WJBF) – The Georgia Department of Transportation recently awarded new contracts for projects in both Jefferson and Emanuel counties. In Jefferson County , Reeves Construction Company has been awarded a $1.08 million project to make safety enhancements on Zebina Road, between Middle Ground Road and Washington Street. The project will add new striping, signage, and raised pavement markers to the route. The shoulder will also be widened by two feet. A completion date of August 31, 2027 is expected. In Emanuel County, Reeves Construction Company was awarded a $5.28 million project to resurface about 14 miles of State Route 192, between US 80/State Route 26 and State Route 56. Additionally, the entirety of State Route 23 Spur (5th Avenue in Twin City) will be resurfaced as part of this contract. The same completion date of August 31, 2027 has also been given for the project.

items.t: Controlled burn at Mistletoe State Park may bring in smoke around McDuffie County, Columbia County line
items.x: (WJBF) According to Columbia County Fire Rescue and Mistletoe State Park, a 640-acre controlled burn at Mistletoe State Park Monday, October 19 th , means residents along the McDuffie County/Columbia County line could be seeing and smelling smoke in the area . According to Mistletoe State Park , a large portion of the controlled burn is being done by drone . According to Mistletoe State Park, the controlled burn “will clear the way for our Longleaf Pine restoration project, as well as removing fuel loads, and enhancing the health of our forest.” As of Tuesday, October 20th, crews say the burns are complete, but that residents may continue to see smoke for the next several weeks as the areas continue to smolder.

items.t: Perfect Fall Weather on Repeat
items.x: Your Monday Evening Update: It was another below average day across the CSRA with highs in the upper 60s to low 70s. High pressure dominates our skies with little to no cloud cover as winds from the north bring us drier air and cooler temperatures. Tomorrow, highs warm a few degrees to the mid 70s with sunny skies continuing. Dry air will allow our overnight low temperatures to cool off faster and longer bringing us lows in the low-40s. This weather pattern will continue through the week. If you’ve been waiting for a stretch to tackle yardwork, take an evening walk, or enjoy some time outside, this forecast is for you! The long-range outlook keeps the pleasant weather going into the weekend, with sunshine and highs in the middle 70s around Augusta. There’s still time for details to change, but we aren’t seeing a strong signal for meaningful rain locally.

items.t: Gelato recalled from Lidl stores in 9 states over listeria concern
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — German-owned supermarket chain Lidl is recalling one lot of gelato from all of its U.S. locations because of a potential listeria contamination, federal regulators announced over the weekend. items.t: How to get an accurate car value using a VIN
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s price tag at the dealership is not the same thing as its worth in the real world. A vehicle’s true market value — what it's worth in today's market based on comparable vehicles, mileage, condition, and other factors — is a more useful figure. That figure often diverges sharply from MSRP or any initial asking price. Yet true market value is only one possible price. A dealer’s trade-in offer, the private-party price you might get on your own, the retail figure a dealer will seek after reconditioning, and the payout an insurer calculates for a total-loss claim can all be different, because each scenario carries distinct costs and risks. items.t: Halloween candy sales are off to a slow start amid high chocolate prices and affordability concerns
items.x: Halloween candy sales are off to a slow start this year as U.S. consumers grapple with high living costs and eye-popping chocolate prices . Halloween candy sales fell 6.7% in the month ending Oct. 17 compared to the same period last year, according to NielsenIQ, a market research firm. Nielsen also noted an 11.7% decline in candy sales in mid-September, erasing the preseason gains that Halloween candy enjoyed the previous two years. Chris Costagli, a vice president and food thought leader at NielsenIQ, said high gas prices have worsened Americans’ concerns about affordability, and that's dampening demand for Halloween treats. items.t: Understanding CPO cars: What does certified pre-owned mean?
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) With new-car prices near record highs, certified pre-owned vehicles (CPOs) offer buyers an affordable alternative to buying new, along with additional inspections and warranty protection. What Does Certified Pre-Owned Mean? If you’re shopping for a car, you’ve likely come across CPO vehicles. But what does that mean exactly, and how do they differ from traditional used cars? A certified pre-owned car is a used vehicle that meets the age, mileage, and condition requirements of a manufacturer or dealer certification program. CPO cars undergo a multipoint inspection and generally include additional warranty coverage, though the coverage and certification standards vary by program. Many CPO vehicles also include benefits such as roadside assistance, access to a loaner vehicle, and trip interruption coverage. items.t: Early voting surges in battleground states as Democrats outpace GOP gains
items.x: Early voting is surging in several key battleground states, giving Democrats hope that their strength in midterm polling could translate into a turnout advantage in November. In North Carolina, more than 1.2 million early ballots have been accepted, a 37 percent increase from the same point leading up to the 2022 midterms, according to an analysis released Friday by Catawba College political scientist Michael Bitzer. That growth — which includes both in-person and mail-in ballots — has been driven by a 47 percent increase among registered Democrats and a 60 percent increase in participation among unaffiliated voters. Early voting among Republicans is up 2.6 percent. Similar patterns are emerging elsewhere, with high turnout especially pronounced in historically Republican-leaning states with competitive Senate races this cycle. A novel mRNA cancer vaccine helps reduce the chances of melanoma patients’ tumors returning
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — A first-of-its-kind cancer vaccine is significantly reducing the chances that melanoma patients’ tumors come back, according to results of a major study released Thursday by drugmakers Moderna and Merck. The vaccine was custom-brewed for each patient to match their tumor. Adding it to a standard post-surgery treatment reduced by 42% the risk of melanoma returning two years after surgery, according to the most advanced study to date of this new strategy for fighting cancer. “The field has been looking for a win and I think this one is a big one,” said Dr. Hussein Tawbi of MD Anderson Cancer Center in Houston, one of the researchers in the international study. The vaccine, called intismeran, is made with the same Nobel Prize-winning mRNA technology that was behind COVID-19 vaccines. items.x: Halloween candy sales are off to a slow start this year as U.S. consumers grapple with high living costs and eye-popping chocolate prices . Halloween candy sales fell 6.7% in the month ending Oct. 17 compared to the same period last year, according to NielsenIQ, a market research firm. Nielsen also noted an 11.7% decline in candy sales in mid-September, erasing the preseason gains that Halloween candy enjoyed the previous two years. Chris Costagli, a vice president and food thought leader at NielsenIQ, said high gas prices have worsened Americans’ concerns about affordability, and that's dampening demand for Halloween treats. items.t: Understanding CPO cars: What does certified pre-owned mean?
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) With new-car prices near record highs, certified pre-owned vehicles (CPOs) offer buyers an affordable alternative to buying new, along with additional inspections and warranty protection. What Does Certified Pre-Owned Mean? If you’re shopping for a car, you’ve likely come across CPO vehicles. But what does that mean exactly, and how do they differ from traditional used cars? A certified pre-owned car is a used vehicle that meets the age, mileage, and condition requirements of a manufacturer or dealer certification program. CPO cars undergo a multipoint inspection and generally include additional warranty coverage, though the coverage and certification standards vary by program. Many CPO vehicles also include benefits such as roadside assistance, access to a loaner vehicle, and trip interruption coverage. items.t: The science and politics behind the panic over ultraprocessed foods
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Ultraprocessed foods have a terrible reputation. Studies have linked them with multiple chronic diseases . Journalists and health influencers characterize them as poison . Some public health experts call for a global halt to producing and consuming them. But the debate around ultraprocessed foods is not nearly as settled as it may seem. As a researcher who studies social movements for healthy and sustainable food, I have been documenting the history of processed foods and examining debates around the science and politics of ultraprocessing . In basic terms, ultraprocessed foods are mass-produced, industrial formulations that use ingredients not typically found in a home kitchen, and that generally contain little to no intact whole foods. items.x: Early voting is surging in several key battleground states, giving Democrats hope that their strength in midterm polling could translate into a turnout advantage in November. In North Carolina, more than 1.2 million early ballots have been accepted, a 37 percent increase from the same point leading up to the 2022 midterms, according to an analysis released Friday by Catawba College political scientist Michael Bitzer. That growth — which includes both in-person and mail-in ballots — has been driven by a 47 percent increase among registered Democrats and a 60 percent increase in participation among unaffiliated voters. Early voting among Republicans is up 2.6 percent. Similar patterns are emerging elsewhere, with high turnout especially pronounced in historically Republican-leaning states with competitive Senate races this cycle. items.t: Veteran says Camp Lejeune victims aren’t pawns to win elections
items.x: CAMP LEJEUNE, N.C. ( WNCN ) — A Marine veteran who helped fight for a law to compensate victims of contaminated water at Camp Lejeune is still waiting for his own settlement more than four years later. Now, he's speaking out after President Donald Trump suggested those payments depend on Republicans winning the November election. "Trying to use veterans and their family members as a pawn to help win an election, I think it's wrong," said Brian Amburgey. Amburgey was stationed at Camp Lejeune in 1984, where he said he began experiencing health problems within a week of arriving. But it wasn't until nearly 30 years later, in 2013, that he received a letter from the Navy warning that he may have been exposed to contaminated water. Amburgey said he's struggled with lung and liver problems for decades. His health deteriorated to the point that he had to give up his construction work in 2022.

items.t: Missing teen identified nearly 50 years after remains found in Wilson County
items.x: RALEIGH, N.C. ( WNCN ) — Cindy Blizzard, a 15-year-old from Monkton, Maryland, disappeared in 1977. On December 29 of that year, skeletal remains were discovered in a wooded area near a tire manufacturing plant in Wilson, North Carolina. After nearly 49 years, investigators identified the remains as Cindy’s in September 2026 using advanced DNA testing and genetic genealogy. Her death is being investigated as a homicide, but no suspect has been publicly identified, and the case remains unsolved. Anyone with information about the case is asked to contact the SBI Cold Case Tip Lane at 919-582-8477 or coldcases@ncsbi.gov or the Wilson County Sheriff's Office at 252-237-2118.

items.t: NC early voting surges during first week, but will it mean higher overall turnout?
items.x: RALEIGH, N.C. ( WNCN ) More than 1.1 million North Carolinians have already cast their ballots in the midterm election, but whether that early surge will translate into higher overall voter turnout remains to be seen. After one week of early voting, turnout surged 37 percent compared to the 2022 midterm election, according to data from the North Carolina Board of Elections. Wake County is seeing an even bigger surge of more than 70 percent compared to 2022. "We are blowing the totals out of the water as far as voter turnout," said Olivia McCall, director of elections for the Wake County Board of Elections. items.t: No drought improvement for central NC

( WNCN ) —Researchers at North Carolina State University have completed a genomic survey of North Carolina black bears, identifying significant differences in genetic health between mountain and coastal populations. The findings provide wildlife management and law enforcement with new tools to monitor population resilience and track illegal poaching. Led by postdoctoral researcher Isabella Livingston and genomics professor Matthew Breen at NC State's College of Veterinary Medicine, the study analyzed DNA from 76 black bears across two state management units. The researchers found that coastal bears show lower genetic diversity and higher levels of inbreeding compared to mountain bears, despite the coastal region having a larger overall bear population. items.t: North Carolina mail-in ballot restrictions to remain through midterms, judge rules
items.x: ( The Hill ) A federal judge ruled Monday that North Carolina is permitted to keep its strict mail-in ballot rules in place for November’s election, which were changed just before ballots were mailed in September. In the ruling, Judge Thomas D. Shroeder wrote that it was too close to the election to change the rules again, and that plaintiffs waited too long to file their motion. “The Supreme Court has repeatedly admonished lower courts that they ‘should ordinarily not alter the election rules on the eve of an election,’” Shroeder wrote. “Here, ‘[t]he election is not merely upcoming; it has already started.’” North Carolina’s state board of elections updated the state’s rules to disqualify ballots where the signature does not match the name on the voter’s application. The new procedures also direct county election officials not to count votes if the inner envelope is not properly sealed.

items.t: High pressure brings a comfortable stretch of fall weather
items.x: COLUMBUS, Ga. ( WRBL ) — High pressure building eastward across the central United States will bring calmer winds and a gradual warmup across the region through the end of the workweek. Afternoon temperatures will climb to near 80 degrees Wednesday through Friday, with plenty of opportunity for a comfortable stretch of fall weather. Mornings, however, will remain cooler than average, creating a noticeable difference between the start and end of each day. By the weekend, high pressure will begin to weaken slightly, allowing temperatures to ease back into the mid-70s. While the change will be modest, it will bring a return to cooler afternoons after Thursday and Friday’s warmer readings. Overall, expect a quiet weather pattern with lighter winds, cool mornings and mild afternoons through the weekend.

items.t: Georgia surpasses 1 million in-person early votes cast
items.x: GEORGIA (WSAV) — More than one million in-person early votes have been counted in the state of Georgia as of Tuesday, marking a sizable increase from the same point in the last midterm election cycle. Georgia Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger said, “We continue to break records each day of early voting. This is evidence that Georgians trust our election process. The strong turnout reflects the work our 159 county election officials do to make our elections free, fair, and fast.” Before noon Tuesday, 1,007,015 in-person early votes had been cast, which is a 12% increase from the same point in 2022. The overall turnout is 1,055,931, as 48,916 absentee ballots have been accepted. Early voting in Georgia continues through Oct. 30. To find early voting locations and hours in your county, visit the Secretary of State’s My Voter Page at https://mvp.sos.ga.gov. Election Day is Nov. 3.

At least eight Columbus women are part of a much larger group of others from across the country who arrived in Paris, France on Friday, October 16. Yolanda Johnson tells WRBL News 3 all was calm when they arrived in the City of Lights. "When we arrived in Paris, it was beautiful, the streets were clear, clean, we didn't see anything that resembled what we eventually ran into," said Yolanda Johnson of Columbus. Johnson says that all changed just before sunset on Saturday when their bus encountered the protests. The tour bus was blocked by barricades because of the violence on the streets. items.t: Who is headlining the Super Bowl halftime show? Prediction markets lean heavily toward one artist
items.x: (NEXSTAR) – The NFL and Roc Nation have yet to officially announce next year’s Super Bowl halftime performer, but users across two of the biggest prediction markets seem to think they have a pretty good idea. As of Tuesday morning, the odds posted at Kalshi and Polymarket leaned heavily toward Jay-Z as the headliner of Super Bowl LXI in Feb. 2027. Jay-Z is also the founder of Roc Nation, the entertainment company that has chosen the act for, and co-produced, the Super Bowl Halftime Show since 2020. Jay-Z had a hefty lead over other potential performers, too. At Kalshi, the market viewed Jay-Z as having about a 91% chance of headlining, and the odds were even greater on Polymarket. items.t: HHS issues new recommendations for ‘gas station opioid’ products
items.x: (NEXSTAR) The federal government is cracking down on synthetic kratom-linked concentrates, also known as "gas station opioids," as the largely unregulated over-the-counter products have been sparking public health concerns. Assistant Secretary for Health Admiral Brian Christine says compounds 7-OH and MGPL are being highly concentrated and sold as if they are natural plant kratom. "With these illicit products, they really increase the concentration of these substances. And at these increased concentrations, they can have potent opioid-like effects, even more potent than morphine, believe it or not. They can depress respiration, and they can lead to death," he said. "They can be highly addictive, highly dangerous." What is kratom, the herbal product with a complicated reputation? items.t: Economy, housing and education top concerns for Georgia voters ahead of Election Day
items.x: ATLANTA (WJBF) — With Election Day just two weeks away, Georgia voters are weighing the issues that matter most to them as campaigns ramp up rallies, advertising and outreach across the state. The economy, affordable housing, healthcare and public safety are among the concerns shaping voters’ decisions, while others say education and equal rights are their top priorities. Georgia has approximately 7.5 million registered voters. More than 800,000 ballots were cast during the first week of early voting, representing about 11 percent of registered voters, according to state data. For David Bell of Alpharetta, economic concerns, crime and public safety are among the most important issues in the election. items.t: Christina Applegate says she was misdiagnosed with MS: ‘I haven’t gotten better’

In a two-part episode return to her podcast, "MeSsy," Applegate, 54, shared that her doctor "came into my room and she said, Congratulations, you don't have MS.'" She had taken time away from "MeSsy," which she co-hosts with Jamie Lynn Sigler of "The Sopranos," to process the news. "I was like, not happy at all," Applegate recounted in the episodes, released Tuesday. "Everybody else was happy." While it has always been on the cover – and will remain there – it will now follow you through the pages of the book. items.t: Virginia daycare temporarily shut down after 2-year-old allegedly put director’s loaded gun in mouth
items.x: RICHMOND, Va. ( WRIC ) The state of Virginia has temporarily shut down a Richmond daycare after a 2-year-old child found and put its director's gun in their mouth . Thrive Learning Center East, LLC — a daycare and preschool for kids as young as 6 weeks old — has not been operating since Oct. 1 while the Virginia Department of Education (VDOE) investigates the incident. According to the Virginia Department of Social Services (DSS), the incident took place on Friday, Sept. 25. On that day, an administrator brought a loaded gun to the facility in their fanny pack. While the Virginia DSS did not identify this administrator, the Richmond Police Department confirmed the arrest of 66-year-old Martha Evans in connection with the incident. items.t: Gimmick or giveback? Even some Trump supporters don’t expect to get $5,000 checks after midterms
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump is hoping that $5,000 checks can juice Republican turnout in November’s midterm elections — but even some of his devoted fans are doubting that government payouts would arrive. “I mean, I guess it’s good for some people. I really don’t care," said Jamie Alvarez, who attended Trump's recent Alaska rally in a red, white and blue outfit. "I don’t feel like your vote should be bought. I feel like you should vote for who you feel is going to do the best job.” Joseph Eatherton was attending that same rally and said he was “not sure if it's necessary." When asked whether Trump could deliver on the promised money, he said, “I don’t know, and I hate being an armchair quarterback." This marked another move by Trump to rename the state after he shared a map on Truth Social last month showing a large “X” over “Mexico” in the state’s name, with the word “America” labeled below it. items.t: Trump blasts federal judge as legal battle over D.C. golf course heats up
items.x: (NEXSTAR) – President Donald Trump has unveiled plans to transform East Potomac Golf Links, a public course located two miles from the White House, into a world-class championship golf venue. The announcement comes as the project faces an active legal battle in federal court over site preparation activities. The dispute intensified after crews cut down hundreds of trees at the property. A federal judge had previously ordered the administration to notify the court before taking any action on the course. Attorney Greg Werkheiser said the administration is sidestepping federal historic preservation rules that require public input before proceeding with work at the site. Werkheiser noted that officials provided minimal advance notice to the court prior to crew activity. “They only let the court know at 4:55 on a Friday,” Werkheiser said. items.t: Sunshine dominates before another shot of cooler air arrives late week
items.x: Columbus, Ga. (WRBL) -Cool mornings will continue across the region, with afternoon temperatures climbing closer to seasonal averages. Sunshine will dominate the forecast through much of the week, but changes are on the way. High pressure building in from the north late week will usher in another round of cooler-than-average temperatures, bringing a fresh taste of fall to the Chattahoochee Valley.

items.t: Columbus man sentenced to life without parole for murder he committed at 16
items.x: COLUMBUS, Ga. ( WRBL ) — More than a month after a Muscogee County jury convicted Mayel Porter of killing 16-year-old Joshua Huff, Superior Court Judge Maureen Gottfried handed down the sentence Monday. Only 16 years old at the time of 2022 murder, Porter will spend the rest of his life in a Georgia prison. “I feel for the families and friends on both sides," Gottfried said. "I truly believe that these young men were not raised to do these type of things. I believe that they were raised in homes that have values and a sense of right and wrong, and that this happened despite that.” That is how Gottfried summed up the murder of Joshua Huff on Cross Tie Court in 2022. She spoke those words just before she sentenced Mayel Porter to life in prison without the possibility of parole. Porter was the only of the three co-defendants found guilty of murder. items.t: Subaru brings back a cheaper WRX, but buyers must do the full math
items.x: (TestMiles) Subaru has made its performance sedan easier to afford again. The 2026 WRX starts at $32,495 before delivery, bringing back a base version and reducing prices elsewhere in the lineup without reducing the standard engine's 271 horsepower. For Americans who want something more interesting than basic transportation but still need four doors, that is a useful development. It also illustrates why an advertised starting price should be the beginning of a buying calculation rather than its conclusion. Add Subaru's listed $1,195 destination charge and the entry WRX becomes $33,690 before taxes, registration, accessories or dealer adjustments. Delivery charges vary in some states. An automatic transmission requires a substantially more expensive version. Premium gasoline and appropriate winter tires belong in the household budget, too. items.x: ( The Hill ) Facebook's parent company, Meta, on Sunday apologized for suspending the "No Kings" Instagram account, saying the suspension was caused by a high increase in traffic by bots. Meta spokesperson Andy Stone wrote in a statement that the company's engineering team found that the "spike that triggered the incorrect enforcement was primarily in the account’s reading' behavior" attributed to the rapid use of the Anthropic model Claude. "These abrupt, high-volume, sequential requests in a short period resembled automated bot traffic rather than an ordinary human browsing our systems," he said. "This activity caused our automated protections to incorrectly take the No Kings Instagram account offline It unfortunately took additional time for us to straighten out the situation with admin access to the IG account." It was sold in 16-ounce clear plastic containers, with a best-by date of March 26, 2028, a universal product code of 4 0564897 22458 and a lot number of 085261. Nearly 1.6M pounds of meat, poultry products recalled nationwide: FSIS The recalled gelato was distributed between July 19 and Oct. 15 to Lidl stores in Delaware, Georgia, Maryland, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Virginia and Washington, D.C., the FDA said. items.x: NASHVILLE, Tenn. ( WKRN ) — Country Music Hall of Fame member John Anderson has passed away, his family announced. He was 71 years old. "It is with the heaviest of hearts that we share the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and best friend," Anderson's loved ones wrote. "To the world, he was a gifted country music singer whose voice and songs touched countless lives. To us, he was so much more. He was the heart of our family, the one who made us laugh, loved us fiercely, and made every ordinary moment feel special. We are completely heartbroken. His music will live on, but for us, his greatest legacy will always be the love he gave his family and the memories we will carry with us forever. items.t: Your next Airbnb stay may come with fewer chores. Here’s why
items.x: ( KTLA ) Your next Airbnb stay could come with fewer chores. Beginning next month, Airbnb hosts will face limits on the tasks they can ask guests to complete before checkout. “House rules help guests understand what hosts expect, but we've heard from our community that they can be confusing, onerous, and hard to manage,” the company said in a statement. “So we've redesigned them to make them easier to discover and clearer to set, alongside a new policy that keeps requests reasonable, with no surprises.” According to Airbnb: Hosts can now choose from seven standard house rules and add reasonable requests, all in one place. items.t: Gas, groceries, electricity: Where prices stand as midterms approach
items.x: ( The Hill ) September’s uptick in inflation dealt Americans with higher prices just before the midterm elections , as Democrats seek to wrestle back control of Congress from the GOP by highlighting affordability concerns. Annual inflation was 3.7 percent last month, according to the consumer price index (CPI). On a monthly basis, the cost of energy, gas and electricity rose. Democrats have campaigned on lowering the cost of living, honing in on President Trump’s tariffs and the Iran war as the causes of price hikes. Trump and Republicans, meanwhile, have accused the opposition of falling victim to “communists” within the party, as multiple left-wing candidates have won primaries this year. items.t: Screwworm spreads to US wildlife in Texas, USDA says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — The first spread of the New World screwworm in U.S. wildlife has been detected in Texas, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture . The USDA's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service said Tuesday the screwworm was found in an elk. According to the federal agency, the elk was reported after it was harvested by a hunter on a game ranch. "This detection highlights the critical role hunters, landowners, outdoor enthusiasts, and wildlife professionals play in helping detect and stop the spread of NWS," the USDA said in a news release. Federal and state officials said they are expanding surveillance in the area and urging hunters, landowners, and outdoor enthusiasts to watch for signs of infestation and report suspicious cases quickly to help prevent further spread. items.t: More absentee ballots are being spoiled in North Carolina. Here’s what voters need to know
items.x: RALEIGH, N.C. ( WNCN ) — More absentee ballots are being rejected in North Carolina compared to the last midterm election, but state election officials can't say how many are connected to stricter mail-in voting rules that a federal judge allowed to remain in place this week. Preliminary data from the NC State Board of Elections shows 3.1% of absentee ballots have been spoiled so far this election cycle, a half-point increase from 2.6% in 2022. "So, a slight increase, but we do want to stress to all absentee voters the importance of closely following the instructions that come with the ballot to ensure that they comply with the law," said Jason Tyson, director of external affairs for the NC State Board of Elections Under the new guidance, absentee ballots must be spoiled if the inner envelope isn't sealed. On Monday, the state rested its case after calling its final witness, North Carolina State Bureau of Investigation special agent Justin Heinrich. Heinrich is the lead investigator who became involved in the case about a year after the crime happened in 2013. Court took a one-day break Tuesday and was back Wednesday as the defense was expected to begin calling up their witnesses. items.t: North Carolina mail-in ballot restrictions to remain through midterms, judge rules
items.x: ( The Hill ) A federal judge ruled Monday that North Carolina is permitted to keep its strict mail-in ballot rules in place for November’s election, which were changed just before ballots were mailed in September. In the ruling, Judge Thomas D. Shroeder wrote that it was too close to the election to change the rules again, and that plaintiffs waited too long to file their motion. “The Supreme Court has repeatedly admonished lower courts that they ‘should ordinarily not alter the election rules on the eve of an election,’” Shroeder wrote. “Here, ‘[t]he election is not merely upcoming; it has already started.’” North Carolina’s state board of elections updated the state’s rules to disqualify ballots where the signature does not match the name on the voter’s application. The new procedures also direct county election officials not to count votes if the inner envelope is not properly sealed.

items.t: Florence Motor Speedway to stop operations after this season
items.x: FLORENCE COUNTY, S.C. (WBTW) — Florence Motor Speedway will cease operations for the 2027 racing season after six years under its current ownership. Owner Steve Zacharias announced the decision Tuesday, citing the financial strain of maintaining the venue. Zacharias took over the four-tenths-of-a-mile short track in 2020. The 40-year-old facility in Florence County faced rising upkeep expenses and an overall decline in racing activity, pushing the owners to a financial breaking point as expenses surpassed incoming revenue. Zacharias said his family's involvement with the track began when another regional venue closed. “When we lost Myrtle Beach Speedway, I called my family and asked them what they wanted to do,” he said. “My kids, you know, I got three kids, and they were, at that time, six years younger. items.x: ( The Hill ) – A third of Americans think that the government should try a second time to put 50-year-old Christa Pike to death after she survived Tennessee’s attempt to execute her by lethal injection last month. A four-day Reuters/Ipsos poll found 33 percent of American adults said a second attempt should be made to execute inmates who survive the first time, while 39 percent supported life in prison instead. She was taken to a Nashville area hospital in an ambulance, where she received medical care and regained consciousness five days after. items.t: Former NC State football head coach Chuck Amato dies at 80
items.x: RALEIGH, N.C. ( WNCN ) — Chuck Amato, a former player and head coach of the North Carolina State Wolfpack football team, has died, the university said Monday. Amato, 80, had been battling throat cancer that caused him to lose his voice, according to university officials. "Chuck Amato was a one-of-a-kind coach and a one-of-a-kind person," the university said in a statement. "We mourn his loss and celebrate his life." Amato played for the Wolfpack as a linebacker from 1965 to 1967 before holding assistant coaching roles with the program from 1971 to 1979. Following 18 years as an assistant for the Florida State Seminoles, he returned to NC State as head coach, a position he held from 2000 to 2006. items.t: Americans spent $110B on the lottery in 2024, analysis finds
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — Americans spent $110.4 billion on lottery tickets in 2024, according to an analysis of U.S. Census Bureau data. That's up from the $109 billion spent in 2023 and $103.3 billion in 2022. According to the analysis by LendingTree, the average American spent $323 on lottery tickets in 2024. Per-capita spending fell in 28 states, rose in 16, and stayed the same in California. Massachusetts residents spent more than $900 Massachusetts again led the nation by a wide margin, with residents spending an average of $904 per person in 2024, down slightly from $915 in 2023 but still 43.5% higher than any other state. Spending was second-highest in Virginia at $630 per person and third-highest in Rhode Island at $567. North Dakota residents spent the least, at $51 per person. The companies are the two largest private health insurance companies for older adults in the U.S. and are ending plans in specific areas where they are making less money, a shift that comes as Medicare enrollment season starts . Medicare Advantage plans being discontinued The plans being discontinued are primarily Preferred Provider Organizations, which offer more flexible provider networks. items.t: Pennsylvania warns of congenital measles amid ‘increase of measles cases during pregnancy’
items.x: ( The Hill ) – The Pennsylvania health department issued a warning to doctors Monday about an increase in measles cases during pregnancy, along with rising concern about congenital measles, a disease rarely seen in the U.S. The department’s alert said congenital measles— meaning measles infection in a newborn contracted from the mother — was identified “for the first time in decades.” There are more than 1,200 measles cases in Pennsylvania, and the health department has confirmed five deaths, though a sixth death was reported earlier this month in Franklin County. Few pediatricians have treated a newborn with congenital measles, presenting a clinical challenge for physicians. That's right, Costco is planning its first-ever warehouse in Rhode Island. "To the world, he was a gifted country music singer whose voice and songs touched countless lives. To us, he was so much more. He was the heart of our family, the one who made us laugh, loved us fiercely, and made every ordinary moment feel special. We are completely heartbroken. His music will live on, but for us, his greatest legacy will always be the love he gave his family and the memories we will carry with us forever. items.t: HVAC issue ignites fire at business on Marketplace Drive in Hampton
items.x: HAMPTON, Va. (WAVY) Crews in Hampton responded to a business fire Thursday morning. According to officials, firefighters were called to that fire, in the 100 block of Marketplace Drive, just before 8 a.m. Photos provided by fire officials show this incident appeared to have occurred at Cracker Barrel. Officials say a 911 caller noted seeing heavy smoke in the area of the bathroom. When crews arrived on scene within minutes and were able to isolate the issue to a burned HVAC belt on the roof of the building. Occupants safely evacuated the building prior to firefighters arrival. No injuries were reported.

items.t: Skunk caught in Suffolk tests positive for rabies
items.x: SUFFOLK, Va. (WAVY) A skunk that was picked up in the 1700 block of White Marsh Road has tested positive for rabies, according to the Suffolk Department of Health. Rabies is caused by a virus that attacks the nervous system and is lethal if proper medical care is not given following exposure. The virus is most commonly transmitted through an animal bite, but it can also spread if saliva from a rabid animal enters open wounds, the mouth, eyes or nose. All mammals, including humans, can contract rabies, with symptoms appearing anywhere from a few days to several months after exposure. Angela Tillery, health director for the Western Tidewater Health District, strongly recommends Suffolk residents protect their families and their pets from rabies by following the following protocols. items.t: Inmate dies in Hampton Community Corrections Center
items.x: HAMPTON, Va. (WAVY) Officials with the Hampton Community Corrections Center announced an inmate died in the facility Wednesday morning. In a press release, officials say the female inmate was found unresponsive inside a restrictive housing cell around 6:30 p.m. Medical personnel immediately began life-saving measures until EMS arrived on scene. The inmate, identified as 68-year-old Karla Smith, was pronounced deceased. There are no signs of foul play, officials say. The incident remains under investigation by the Hampton Police Division and the Hampton Sheriff’s Office.

items.x: NORFOLK, Va. (WAVY) Early voting numbers are high throughout the Commonwealth as more than 870,000 Virginians have already cast a ballot. According to the Virginia Public Access Project , early voting is set to outpace the numbers from 2022. Then, 976,558 Virginians chose to vote early. A majority of early voters are choosing to do so via in-person, making up 627,545 of the votes as of Oct. 21. Congressional Districts one and four are about to surpass the 2022 total early votes. In Hampton Roads, Gloucester County has already totaled more early votes than in 2022, with 4,649 ballots cast. James City County is another locality that has surpassed the 2022 mark, with nearly 18,000 early votes totaled this year. District 1 has a U.S. House seat up for grabs. items.t: Gas, groceries, electricity: Where prices stand as midterms approach
items.x: ( The Hill ) September’s uptick in inflation dealt Americans with higher prices just before the midterm elections , as Democrats seek to wrestle back control of Congress from the GOP by highlighting affordability concerns. Annual inflation was 3.7% last month, according to the consumer price index , or CPI. On a monthly basis, the cost of energy, gas and electricity rose. The cost of food held steady from August to September, and was up 2.5% year-over-year. Democrats have campaigned on lowering the cost of living, honing in on President Trump’s tariffs and the Iran war as the causes of price hikes. Trump and Republicans, meanwhile, have accused the opposition of falling victim to “communists” within the party, as multiple left-wing candidates have won primaries this year. items.t: ‘Behemoth’ El Niño could be ‘off the charts,’ forecasters warn
items.x: (NEXSTAR) – Meteorologists are continuing to warn of the El Niño weather event expected to impact us throughout the winter, with a new climate outlook from the World Meteorological Organization suggesting it "could be unprecedented in strength." In an update Wednesday, the WMO said this year's El Niño weather pattern could be so strong, it could "literally [be] off the monitoring charts that we have used for the past four decades." A main focus of forecasting El Niño comes down to sea surface temperatures. In the Pacific, an "anomaly of 0.5 [degrees Celsius] above normal" can trigger an El Niño alert from the WMO, according to the United Nations. Between next month and January, WMO has forecast temperatures could rise 3.8 degrees Celsius above average. items.t: Surveillance pricing comes into focus in some midterm campaigns
items.x: WASHINGTON, D.C. (NEXSTAR) A stalled effort to block companies from using AI to set prices is gaining new attention on the campaign trail. As Democrats put affordability front and center in their campaigns, there's one issue some candidates are focused on: personalized prices. Personalized pricing, which is also called surveillance pricing, is when companies use your personal data to determine how much you pay for their products or services. That means you could pay more than someone else for the same item. "The number of people who come up to me and say, Gosh, Mark, I saw your ad, and that's crazy,'" said Sen. Mark Warner (D-Virginia), who is running for reelection this year. Warner has proposed a federal ban on surveillance pricing. "This is the kind of part where technology gets creepy," Warner said. items.t: Pope Leo won’t need further treatment for lung cancer, doctors say
items.x: Video above: Pope delivers thanks to faithful from Vatican window one day after return from hospital on Oct. 18, 2026. VATICAN CITY (AP) — Pope Leo XIV needs no further treatment for lung cancer after follow-up tests confirmed the disease was localized, the Vatican said in a statement Wednesday. Leo, 71, had the lower lobe of his right lung removed last week in the first major health event of his 17-month pontificate. The surgery confirmed he had adenocarcinoma , the most common type of lung cancer. He left the hospital on Saturday, four days after surgery and well ahead of the week-long hospital stay the Vatican had initially anticipated. items.x: Like so many Americans, Jenny Escolastico has watched wearily as the cost of living has risen, straining her household budget. But as a mother of two children under 5, she faces added pressure that could shape how she votes in November : childcare costs. Escolastico’s household outside Allentown, Pennsylvania, is relying solely on her husband’s income. She’s staying home with her children, at least in part because she simply can’t afford to work . President Trump on Tuesday signed H.R. 6380 , redesignating Chiricahua National Monument as the Chiricahua National Park. Chiricahua is located about two hours east of Tucson in the southeast corner of Arizona, not far from Saguaro National Park, within the historical territory of the Chiricahua Apache tribes. Officials say the rare breakthrough infection is the first case to be reported in DuPage County so far this year. items.t: Supreme Court won’t revive Trump administration’s transgender inmate policy
items.x: ( The Hill ) The Supreme Court refused the Trump administration’s bid to stop providing transgender inmates hormone treatments and certain surgeries on Wednesday , declining to lift a lower judge’s block over the dissents of two conservative justices. The Bureau of Prisons (BOP) policy would taper treatments for inmates currently receiving them, and officials would also need to stop providing social accommodations, like hair-removal devices. Solicitor General D. John Sauer asserted the changes are needed to maintain “institutional security” in federal prisons. It’s a rare loss for the Trump administration, which has emerged victorious more than two dozen times when asking the high court for emergency relief after a judge blocked an aspect of President Donald Trump’s agenda. items.t: Tow truck carrying forklift crashes into Hubbard’s Cave on Kennedy Expressway, spilling battery acid: ISP
items.x: CHICAGO — A major accident on the Kennedy Expressway caused extensive delays Wednesday morning. The accident, involving a tow truck hauling a forklift, happened around 8 a.m. on the southbound Kennedy and Hubbard Street. According to Illinois State Police, a preliminary investigation indicates the forklift fell of the tow truck and hit Hubbard's Cave. As a result, battery acid leaked onto the roadway. ISP says this was not a hazmat situation and no injuries were reported. The middle and right lanes were closed for cleanup causing major delays in the area. This is an ongoing incident and there is no further information available at this time.

items.t: Jokic has triple-double, Murray scores 42 points in Nuggets’ OT victory over Pelicans
items.x: DENVER (AP) — Nikola Jokic scored eight of his 35 points in overtime and finished with 15 rebounds and 10 assists, and the short-handed Denver Nuggets rallied from down 23 to beat the New Orleans Pelicans 141-135 on Saturday night. Jokic had his 199th career triple-double in the regular season, second to Russell Westbrook, who retired with 209. items.t: Understanding CPO cars: What does certified pre-owned mean?
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) With new-car prices near record highs, certified pre-owned vehicles (CPOs) offer buyers an affordable alternative to buying new, along with additional inspections and warranty protection. What Does Certified Pre-Owned Mean? If you’re shopping for a car, you’ve likely come across CPO vehicles. But what does that mean exactly, and how do they differ from traditional used cars? A certified pre-owned car is a used vehicle that meets the age, mileage, and condition requirements of a manufacturer or dealer certification program. CPO cars undergo a multipoint inspection and generally include additional warranty coverage, though the coverage and certification standards vary by program. Many CPO vehicles also include benefits such as roadside assistance, access to a loaner vehicle, and trip interruption coverage. items.t: The science and politics behind the panic over ultraprocessed foods
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Ultraprocessed foods have a terrible reputation. Studies have linked them with multiple chronic diseases . Journalists and health influencers characterize them as poison . Some public health experts call for a global halt to producing and consuming them. But the debate around ultraprocessed foods is not nearly as settled as it may seem. As a researcher who studies social movements for healthy and sustainable food, I have been documenting the history of processed foods and examining debates around the science and politics of ultraprocessing . items.t: About half concerned Republicans could try to overturn midterm results: Survey
items.x: ( The Hill ) A new poll released Friday suggests half of Americans are concerned Republicans may try to overturn the results of November’s midterm election. Fifty percent of respondents to the New York Times/Siena University survey said they were either "very" or "somewhat worried" the GOP may use “illegal means” to overturn the election, compared to 49 percent who are either "not too worried" or "not at all worried." A strong majority of Democrats — 86 percent — were among the share of likely voters who reported feeling worry about potential GOP election interference, and 52 percent independents felt the same. Even 10 percent of Republicans say they are worried their own party would overturn the results. items.x: ( The Hill ) The Cook Political Report is shifting a closely watched gubernatorial contest toward Democrats after a controversial campaign ad shook up the race. The nonpartisan election forecaster moved the governor’s race in Ohio from “toss up” to “lean Democrat,” now favoring Amy Acton (D) to beat Vivek Ramaswamy (R) in the Buckeye State. The race was the source of national attention after Ramaswamy debuted an ad with Acton’s estranged mother, who claims Acton is a “liar” and encourages voters not to elect her as Ohio governor. Acton was removed from her mother’s custody at age 12. Her campaign said that she was sexually abused by her stepfather, who her mother remained with until his death. items.t: Texas man dies in Cameron Parish motorcycle crash
items.x: CAMERON, La. ( KLFY ) A 55-year-old Texas man was killed on Wednesday around 7 p.m. in Cameron Parish, officials said. Troopers with Louisiana State Police Troop D responded to a two-vehicle crash on Louisiana Highway 27 near LA 384. The preliminary investigation revealed that a 2018 Ford F-150 towing a grain hopper was stopped on Louisiana Highway 27, preparing to make a left turn onto Louisiana Highway 384. At the same time a 2019 Harley Davidson was traveling south approaching the rear of the Ford. For reasons still under investigation, the Harley Davidson failed to stop and rear-ended the grain hopper, officials said. The motorcyclist died at the scene. He was wearing a DOT-approved helmet at the time of the crash. Impairment is not suspected. Routine toxicology samples were obtained and submitted for analysis. items.t: A novel mRNA cancer vaccine helps reduce the chances of melanoma patients’ tumors returning
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — A first-of-its-kind cancer vaccine is significantly reducing the chances that melanoma patients’ tumors come back, according to results of a major study released Thursday by drugmakers Moderna and Merck. The vaccine was custom-brewed for each patient to match their tumor. Adding it to a standard post-surgery treatment reduced by 42% the risk of melanoma returning two years after surgery, according to the most advanced study to date of this new strategy for fighting cancer. “The field has been looking for a win and I think this one is a big one,” said Dr. Hussein Tawbi of MD Anderson Cancer Center in Houston, one of the researchers in the international study. The vaccine, called intismeran, is made with the same Nobel Prize-winning mRNA technology that was behind COVID-19 vaccines. items.t: Americans spent $110B on the lottery in 2024, analysis finds
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — Americans spent $110.4 billion on lottery tickets in 2024, according to an analysis of U.S. Census Bureau data. That's up from the $109 billion spent in 2023 and $103.3 billion in 2022. According to the analysis by LendingTree, the average American spent $323 on lottery tickets in 2024. Per-capita spending fell in 28 states, rose in 16, and stayed the same in California. Massachusetts residents spent more than $900 Massachusetts again led the nation by a wide margin, with residents spending an average of $904 per person in 2024, down slightly from $915 in 2023 but still 43.5% higher than any other state. Spending was second-highest in Virginia at $630 per person and third-highest in Rhode Island at $567. North Dakota residents spent the least, at $51 per person. Wyoming, Montana, New Mexico and Oklahoma were the only other states where spending fell under $100 per person

items.t: US Treasury proposes a rule to crack down on high-tech investments in China, other adversaries
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — The U.S. Treasury Department proposed a rule Thursday to crack down on American high-tech investments such as supercomputing and artificial intelligence in China, Russia, North Korea and other “countries of concern." The U.S. government has been working for years to deny China and other adversaries investments that could help them boost their military power. That program began in 2023 when then-President Joe Biden signed an executive order putting restrictions on outbound U.S. investments in sectors such as semiconductors, quantum computing and artificial intelligence going into China. Treasury later established the Outbound Investment Security Program. In December 2025, Congress passed a law that codified and expanded the program to target more technologies and more foreign countries, including Cuba, Iran, North Korea and Russia. items.t: Execution staff warned IV site might have ‘blown’ during Christa Pike’s execution attempt
items.x: Tennessee execution team members failed multiple times to establish working IV lines in Christa Pike’s arms before her attempted execution and warned that some of her veins may have ruptured, or “blown,” before she was injected with the lethal drug, her attorney wrote in a court document filed Thursday. The IV team went through about 10 needles and tried several IV sites on both arms, attorney Randy Spivey wrote in the document, which provides the most detailed account of the execution attempt so far. They even struggled to push saline through the last IV site they established, Spivey wrote. Pike, 50, was hospitalized after surviving two doses of pentobarbital as the state tried to execute her on Sept. 30 for the 1995 stabbing death of classmate Colleen Slemmer. items.t: Almost all coral reef ecosystems face risk of collapse in 50 years, study warns
items.x: The world’s coral reef ecosystems almost all face a high risk of collapse in the next 50 years, mostly due to warming oceans and heat waves, according to a global assessment released Thursday. It's the latest dose of bad news for coral reefs, which are critical sources for seafood and tourism and often serve as buffers from coastal erosion and storms. Sometimes dubbed “rainforests of the sea,” they have some of the world’s richest biodiversity. They support a quarter of marine species as well as coastal communities and businesses. Some 96% of shallow-water reef systems are already critically endangered and could disappear by 2075, the International Union for Conservation of Nature announced on the sidelines of a U.N. biodiversity conference in Albania. items.t: WATCH: Kitten rescued from drainpipe using custom RC car
items.x: WEST VALLEY CITY, Utah ( ABC4 ) — Using a remote-controlled crawler, West Valley City's Public Works Department rescued a kitten stuck in a pipe. According to the West Valley City Government, members of their storm crew in their Public Works Department received reports of a kitten that was stuck inside of a drainpipe last week. They were able to use a pole camera to locate the cat. However, efforts to coax the kitten out of the pipe were unsuccessful. Crews then called in a custom remote-controlled camera that has a live camera and lights, which they call R2D2. Typically, they use R2D2 to inspect pipes. However, the city says, "it can add kitten' rescuer to its list of functions." R2D2 nudged the kitten out of the pipe and into the waiting arms of crew members, effectively saving it. West Valley City adds, "Thanks to Public Works for the rescue!"

items.t: Nearly $42M in SNAP benefit fraud uncovered in enforcement surge: DOJ
items.x: TAMPA, Fla. (WFLA)— During a Nationwide Enforcement Surge, the Middle District of Florida joined the DOJ Fraud Division and others to uncover nearly $42 million in SNAP benefit fraud. According to the DOJ, between Sept. 1, 2026, and Oct. 21, 2026, the Fraud Division, the MDFL, along with 12 other U.S. Attorneys' Offices, and the Utah Attorney General's Office conducted the first National USDA Benefits and Program Fraud Enforcement Surge. This operation resulted in actions against 40 defendants whose alleged or proven schemes caused almost $45 million in losses to the federal government. Almost $42 million of the amount was involved in fraud against SNAP benefits, which provide monthly food assistance to low-income families and individuals. According to the DOJ, the MDFL case involved fraud against a USDA crop-insurance program that is designed to help farmers recover from covered losses.

items.t: Social Security says it’s ‘corrected’ tens of millions of records. Here’s why
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — The Social Security Administration says it has "corrected" nearly 15% of active Social Security numbers since the start of the Trump administration as part of an ongoing effort to improve the accuracy and integrity of its database. The agency said Tuesday it has added 17 million death dates to records that previously had none and updated citizenship information in roughly 25 million records where it was missing. "This is the first time SSA has undertaken an effort of this scale, and I am proud of the work we have done to strengthen the foundation of identity data relied upon throughout government and the economy," SSA Commissioner Frank Bisignano said in a release. SSA said it is still correcting an additional 8 1/2 million records with "inaccurate citizenship status." The agency said it has also implemented "stronger internal controls" to prevent future data entry error

His family issued the following statement after he died in his sleep on Wednesday, Oct. 21: It is with the heaviest of hearts that we share the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and best friend. To the world, he was a gifted country music singer whose voice and songs touched countless lives. To us, he was so much more. He was the heart of our family, the one who made us laugh, loved us fiercely, and made every ordinary moment feel special. We are completely heartbroken. His music will live on, but for us, his greatest legacy will always be the love he gave his family and the memories we will carry with us forever. items.t: Keep The Pie, Pass On The Drama — 6 Tips For Setting Healthy Boundaries During The Holidays
items.x: Source: O2O Creative / Getty The holidays are supposed to be about love, laughter, good food and making memories. But let's be honest: sometimes, the most stressful part of Thanksgiving and Christmas isn't figuring out who's bringing the mac and cheese, it's the dread of figuring out how to survive being around everybody. Between family drama, unsolicited opinions about your love life, pressure to host a picture-perfect dinner and the expectation to show up everywhere, the holiday season can quickly turn from festive to exhausting. Add in the pressure to spend money, cook for a crowd and keep everybody happy, and suddenly, your holiday cheer is hanging by a thread. That's why learning how to set boundaries during the holidays is so important. Protecting your peace doesn't mean you don't love your family. It means understanding that your time, energy and emotional well-being matter, too.

items.t: Shirley Chisholm's Legacy Takes Center Stage Ahead of Midterms
items.x: Source: “If they don’t give you a seat at the table, bring a folding chair.” Few political declarations capture the spirit of Shirley Chisholm quite like that one. The pioneering Black congresswoman understood that waiting for the powerful to make room for you was no substitute for claiming your place—and that lesson remains strikingly relevant as Americans prepare for another consequential midterm election. Chisholm, who broke barriers in Congress and challenged the political establishment with an unprecedented presidential campaign, believed that meaningful change required people to reject limitations, organize and demand a voice in the decisions affecting their lives. “You don’t make progress by standing on the sidelines, whimpering and complaining. items.t: Why Was Malcolm X Holding A Gun? The Story Behind His Iconic Window Photo
items.x: Source: Bettmann / Getty Some photographs capture a moment. Others capture an entire chapter of history. In 1964, photographer Don Hogan Charles took an image of Malcolm X standing behind a curtained window in his Queens, New York, home, holding a rifle in his right hand. His eyes are fixed outward, his expression serious and alert, as if watching for a danger that could arrive at any moment. The photograph would become one of the most recognizable images of the legendary civil rights leader. But it also raises an important question: Why was Malcolm X, a man fighting for the freedom and dignity of Black Americans, holding a gun? To understand the image, you have to understand the threats surrounding his life at the time. Don Hogan Charles took the historic photo. items.t: Tennessee court dismisses challenge to Education Freedom Scholarship Program
items.x: NASHVILLE, Tenn. (WKRN) — Tennessee’s Education Freedom Scholarship Program will remain in place after a three-judge panel dismissed a lawsuit challenging its constitutionality. The lawsuit argued the program violates the state constitution by funding private education and undermines public school funding. A two-judge majority rejected both claims. It found the Tennessee Constitution does not prohibit funding private education and said a challenge to public school funding must target the laws that fund public schools, not the scholarship program. During the week of July 14, top U.S. Postal Service officials conducted an audit into three post office locations in Middle Tennessee: one on Church Street in Nashville , one in Lebanon , and one in Hendersonville . The audit team looked into six areas of deficiencies, such as delayed mail and package scanning. Deficiencies were identified in five categories at the Nashville location. On the morning of July 14, auditors found more than 5,100 delayed mail pieces in carrier cases. items.t: Not just gas and groceries: Childcare costs weigh on voters before midterm elections
items.x: Like so many Americans, Jenny Escolastico has watched wearily as the cost of living has risen, straining her household budget. But as a mother of two children under 5, she faces added pressure that could shape how she votes in November : childcare costs. Escolastico’s household outside Allentown, Pennsylvania, is relying solely on her husband’s income. She’s staying home with her children, at least in part because she simply can’t afford to work . "What I would be spending on childcare would be more than what I would be making if I were working full time,” said Escolastico, an Air Force veteran who later worked in human resources. “Childcare is another rent, another car note.” Even though her son now attends state-funded prekindergarten , returning to work would still mean finding him after-school care, plus full-time childcare for her daughter. items.x: ( KTLA ) The whereabouts of Amelia Earhart’s plane remain a mystery after a team of archaeologists and filmmakers failed to locate the pilot’s Model 10E Electra aircraft on a remote, uninhabited atoll in the Western Pacific earlier this month. The highly publicized voyage, known as the “Taraia Object” expedition, was envisioned after a plane-shaped object was spotted in a lagoon off Nikumaroro atoll using satellite imagery in 2020. A team from Purdue University planned the voyage in hopes of discovering Earhart’s plane and solving the 89-year-old mystery. Earhart and her navigator, Fred Noonan, vanished somewhere over the Pacific Ocean while she attempted to become the first woman to circumnavigate the globe in 1937. items.t: No bullhorns: City council lays out new rules for meetings
items.x: MEMPHIS, Tenn. — The City of Memphis announced new rules Monday for attending City Council meetings. Among those rules: No bullhorns or megaphones, no signs with sticks or poles, and only clear bags no larger than 6-by-8 inches are allowed. There are also new rules on where to sit and other items not allowed inside, such as large bags. "No threatening behavior or disruptive outbursts," the city said in a Facebook post. Justin Pearson files lawsuit after being banned from council meetings The rules were announced a few days after the chairwoman of the City Council banned Rep. Justin J. Pearson and several activists from two future council meetings after a chaotic meeting earlier this month. Pearson says a letter states he was banned for "disruptive behavior" in a meeting regarding a data center moratorium; he denies being disruptive and has filed suit against City Council.

items.x: A Roman Catholic priest celebrating an evening Mass in southwestern Ecuador has died after a crucifix fell on him during the livestreamed service. The Archdiocese of Guayaquil, a coastal city 164 miles southwest of the capital, Quito, identified the priest as Patricio Sánchez of Perpetuo Socorro Church. Footage of the service on Saturday night shows a heavy crucifix detaching from the wall above the altar and striking Sánchez on the head as he celebrated Mass. He did not appear to see it falling. Worshippers cried for help as the social media broadcast continued. Local authorities have not commented on the incident. Sánchez belonged to the Congregation of the Most Holy Redeemer, a Roman Catholic religious order founded in 1732 with a presence in 80 countries.

items.t: How to get an accurate car value using a VIN
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s price tag at the dealership is not the same thing as its worth in the real world. A vehicle’s true market value — what it's worth in today's market based on comparable vehicles, mileage, condition, and other factors — is a more useful figure. That figure often diverges sharply from MSRP or any initial asking price. Yet true market value is only one possible price. A dealer’s trade-in offer, the private-party price you might get on your own, the retail figure a dealer will seek after reconditioning, and the payout an insurer calculates for a total-loss claim can all be different, because each scenario carries distinct costs and risks. Keeping those contexts straight prevents apples-to-oranges comparisons and helps you avoid unrealistic expectations. What factors affect a used car’s value? The organization celebrated its sixth annual Day in the Parks event, with over 100 volunteers planting around 3,000 trees at Possum Creek MetroPark in Dayton. “Being able to help our grandkids, our kids, even ourselves—to be able to come enjoy it when we work, look forward to some of our retirement plans—it’s an excellent way to give back just out during the day,” said AES Safety Specialist Shawn Talley. “We couldn’t have asked for better weather.” Since the initiative began, AES has supported local parks by planting trees, repairing and painting bikeway fences, maintaining gardens, and more.

Questions about the video will likely shadow Ramaswamy, a biotech billionaire who previously ran for president but has never before held public office, in the final two weeks of the contest. Democrats said he was growing desperate at a moment when more than 676,000 people have already cast ballots in Ohio. items.t: More bright sunshine to check out those fall colors
items.x: DAYTON, Ohio (WDTN) — A huge area of high pressure centered over southern Canada will continue to be the dominant weather feature affecting the Miami Valley for at least the next week. That means lots of sunshine during the day and clear skies at night with seasonable to mild high temperatures in the upper 60s to lower 80s. TONIGHT: Clear, calm and seasonably cool. Low 44. THURSDAY: Sunny, pleasant and mild. High 71. THURSDAY NIGHT: Clear and continued seasonably cool. Low 45. FRIDAY: Sunny and still quite mild. High 70. The weekend will bring more of the same with lots of sunshine and highs in the lower 70s. In fact, the only change over the next week will be more cloud cover on Monday and especially Tuesday, but no rain is expected. Daily highs will continue to range from the mid 60s to the lower 70s.

items.t: Eggs cost more than $10 in Hawaii: Report
items.x: HONOLULU ( KHON ) An increase in costs is easily visible to consumers during their grocery shopping. For Hawaii residents, one item that continues to see sticker shock is the skyrocketing price of eggs. On average, it's now $10.06 to buy a dozen eggs in Honolulu, the Department of Agriculture and Biosecurity, or DAB, announced on Tuesday. According to statistics from DAB's Market Analysis and News Branch, the price of a dozen eggs spiked more than 11 percent in the past year, officials said. The report found that eggs from the U.S. continent increased slightly more than 1 percent, from $7.78 a dozen to $7.87. But local organic eggs saw the highest jump with the average price for a dozen up by 22 percent from the first quarter of 2026 to the second quarter. items.t: Pope Leo won’t need further treatment for lung cancer, doctors say
items.x: Video above: Pope delivers thanks to faithful from Vatican window one day after return from hospital on Oct. 18, 2026. VATICAN CITY (AP) — Pope Leo XIV needs no further treatment for lung cancer after follow-up tests confirmed the disease was localized, the Vatican said in a statement Wednesday. Leo, 71, had the lower lobe of his right lung removed last week in the first major health event of his 17-month pontificate. The surgery confirmed he had adenocarcinoma , the most common type of lung cancer. He left the hospital on Saturday, four days after surgery and well ahead of the week-long hospital stay the Vatican had initially anticipated. items.t: McDonald’s McRib returning to Ohio by end of October
items.x: There are few things to be sure of in life beyond death, taxes and Kilimanjaro rising like Olympus above the Serengeti. One of those others is happening soon: The McRib is coming back! The fan-favorite sandwich will be returning to Ohio McDonald's restaurants starting Oct. 26 for a limited time. The sandwich a seasoned boneless pork patty coated in BBQ sauce, onions and pickles has attracted an almost Buc-ee's-like fanbase since debuting in Kansas City in 1981. Fans have even created McRibLocator.com , a website tracking the appearance and disappearance of the sandwich across the United States. The sandwich will reportedly also be returning to McDonald's menus in Indiana, Michigan and Pennsylvania the same day.

"If an immediate update is not feasible, it is recommended that organizations take the system offline until it can be fully mitigated." items.t: Supreme Court won’t revive Trump administration’s transgender inmate policy
items.x: ( The Hill ) The Supreme Court refused the Trump administration’s bid to stop providing transgender inmates hormone treatments and certain surgeries on Wednesday , declining to lift a lower judge’s block over the dissents of two conservative justices. The Bureau of Prisons (BOP) policy would taper treatments for inmates currently receiving them, and officials would also need to stop providing social accommodations, like hair-removal devices. Solicitor General D. John Sauer asserted the changes are needed to maintain “institutional security” in federal prisons. It’s a rare loss for the Trump administration, which has emerged victorious more than two dozen times when asking the high court for emergency relief after a judge blocked an aspect of President Donald Trump’s agenda. That's up from the $109 billion spent in 2023 and $103.3 billion in 2022. According to the analysis by LendingTree, the average American spent $323 on lottery tickets in 2024. Per-capita spending fell in 28 states, rose in 16, and stayed the same in California. Massachusetts residents spent more than $900 Massachusetts again led the nation by a wide margin, with residents spending an average of $904 per person in 2024, down slightly from $915 in 2023 but still 43.5% higher than any other state. Spending was second-highest in Virginia at $630 per person and third-highest in Rhode Island at $567. North Dakota residents spent the least, at $51 per person. items.t: Halloween candy sales are off to a slow start amid high chocolate prices and affordability concerns
items.x: Halloween candy sales are off to a slow start this year as U.S. consumers grapple with high living costs and eye-popping chocolate prices . Halloween candy sales fell 6.7% in the month ending Oct. 17 compared to the same period last year, according to NielsenIQ, a market research firm. Nielsen also noted an 11.7% decline in candy sales in mid-September, erasing the preseason gains that Halloween candy enjoyed the previous two years. Chris Costagli, a vice president and food thought leader at NielsenIQ, said high gas prices have worsened Americans’ concerns about affordability, and that's dampening demand for Halloween treats. As of Friday, the average price of a gallon of regular gasoline in the U.S. was $4.29, up nearly 40% from the prior year. “I think what you’re seeing now is a consumer that’s spending so much additional money on fuel and housing and clothing and food,” Costagli said

items.t: Understanding CPO cars: What does certified pre-owned mean?
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) With new-car prices near record highs, certified pre-owned vehicles (CPOs) offer buyers an affordable alternative to buying new, along with additional inspections and warranty protection. What Does Certified Pre-Owned Mean? If you’re shopping for a car, you’ve likely come across CPO vehicles. But what does that mean exactly, and how do they differ from traditional used cars? A certified pre-owned car is a used vehicle that meets the age, mileage, and condition requirements of a manufacturer or dealer certification program. CPO cars undergo a multipoint inspection and generally include additional warranty coverage, though the coverage and certification standards vary by program. Many CPO vehicles also include benefits such as roadside assistance, access to a loaner vehicle, and trip interruption coverage. items.t: The science and politics behind the panic over ultraprocessed foods
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Ultraprocessed foods have a terrible reputation. Studies have linked them with multiple chronic diseases . Journalists and health influencers characterize them as poison . Some public health experts call for a global halt to producing and consuming them. But the debate around ultraprocessed foods is not nearly as settled as it may seem. As a researcher who studies social movements for healthy and sustainable food, I have been documenting the history of processed foods and examining debates around the science and politics of ultraprocessing . In basic terms, ultraprocessed foods are mass-produced, industrial formulations that use ingredients not typically found in a home kitchen, and that generally contain little to no intact whole foods.
