items.t: Early voting surges in battleground states as Democrats outpace GOP gains
items.x: Early voting is surging in several key battleground states, giving Democrats hope that their strength in midterm polling could translate into a turnout advantage in November. In North Carolina, more than 1.2 million early ballots have been accepted, a 37 percent increase from the same point leading up to the 2022 midterms, according to an analysis released Friday by Catawba College political scientist Michael Bitzer. That growth — which includes both in-person and mail-in ballots — has been driven by a 47 percent increase among registered Democrats and a 60 percent increase in participation among unaffiliated voters. Early voting among Republicans is up 2.6 percent. Similar patterns are emerging elsewhere, with high turnout especially pronounced in historically Republican-leaning states with competitive Senate races this cycle. items.t: About half concerned Republicans could try to overturn midterm results: Survey
items.x: ( The Hill ) A new poll released Friday suggests half of Americans are concerned Republicans may try to overturn the results of November’s midterm election. Fifty percent of respondents to the New York Times/Siena University survey said they were either "very" or "somewhat worried" the GOP may use “illegal means” to overturn the election, compared to 49 percent who are either "not too worried" or "not at all worried." A strong majority of Democrats — 86 percent — were among the share of likely voters who reported feeling worry about potential GOP election interference, and 52 percent independents felt the same. Even 10 percent of Republicans say they are worried their own party would overturn the results. items.t: A novel mRNA cancer vaccine helps reduce the chances of melanoma patients’ tumors returning
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — A first-of-its-kind cancer vaccine is significantly reducing the chances that melanoma patients’ tumors come back, according to results of a major study released Thursday by drugmakers Moderna and Merck. The vaccine was custom-brewed for each patient to match their tumor. Adding it to a standard post-surgery treatment reduced by 42% the risk of melanoma returning two years after surgery, according to the most advanced study to date of this new strategy for fighting cancer. “The field has been looking for a win and I think this one is a big one,” said Dr. Hussein Tawbi of MD Anderson Cancer Center in Houston, one of the researchers in the international study. The vaccine, called intismeran, is made with the same Nobel Prize-winning mRNA technology that was behind COVID-19 vaccines. items.x: PRINCE WILLIAM COUNTY, Va. ( DC News Now ) Officers arrested a Stafford man on Wednesday in connection with the vandalism of an Iwo Jima statue, according to the Prince William County Police Department. Police said crews responded Wednesday at 10:13 p.m. to reports of property destruction at the Iwo Jima statue, located at Richmond Highway and Fuller Road in Quantico. Kayleb Coker pleaded guilty to the following charges: attempted malicious wounding, use of a firearm in the commission of a felony, unlawfully shooting into an occupied vehicle, shooting from an occupied vehicle and shooting in a public place. items.t: Crumbl shutters dozens of locations nationwide: Reports
items.x: ( KTLA ) Crumbl, the bakery chain known for its rotating weekly menu and oversized cookies, has recently shuttered dozens of locations nationwide, according to multiple reports. At least 57 locations of the dessert chain have closed this year, according to an analysis of local reports and a location count on the company's website cited by Restaurant Business. In California, the closures span the state and include locations in Paso Robles, Pismo Beach, Hanford, Ladera Ranch, Mira Mesa, Cupertino, and Westlake Village. Shuttered stores have also been reported in Alabama, Florida, and Kentucky, according to SFGATE. items.t: VSP: 75-year-old woman fatally struck by vehicle in Smithfield Kroger parking lot
items.x: SMITHFIELD, Va. (WAVY) A 75-year-old woman died after being stuck by a vehicle Thursday afternoon in the parking lot of a Smithfield Kroger, according to Virginia State Police. On Oct. 22, state police responded to a pedestrian-involved crash in the parking lot of Kroger, located at 1282 Smithfield Plaza, at approximately 2 p.m. The pedestrian, identified as 75-year-old Janet Hope Edwards, of Smithfield, was struck by the vehicle and suffered fatal injuries. The operator of the vehicle, identified as a 70-year-old woman, did not sustain any injuries during the crash. The incident remains under investigation.

items.t: VBPD release composite image of unidentified 1976 homicide victim
items.x: VIRGINIA BEACH, Va. (WAVY) Virginia Beach police have predicted the physical appearance of a homicide victim whose body was discovered in the water near the Chesapeake Bay Bridge-Tunnel in May 1976. In partnership with Virginia-based DNA technology company Parabon NanoLabs, genetic material recovered from the crime scene was used to generate precise trait predictions regarding the victim's ancestry, eye color, hair color, skin tone, freckling and facial structure. Forensic artists produced a snapshot composite illustration depicting the possible appearance of the victim at age 25 with an average Body Mass Index of 22. Police said the baseline metrics were used because chronological age and weight cannot be determined solely through DNA. items.t: Toyota simplifies the 2027 Corolla Cross lineup
items.x: (TestMiles) The 2027 Corolla Cross returns with gas and hybrid powertrains, fewer hybrid grades, standard safety tech and pricing from $25,535. Toyota is taking a light-touch approach to the 2027 Corolla Cross. Rather than redesigning its smallest mainstream SUV again, the company is carrying over most of the equipment introduced for 2026 and making one notable change: the hybrid range is easier to understand. For 2027, the gas-powered Corolla Cross remains available in L, LE and XLE grades, with front-wheel drive or all-wheel drive depending on configuration. The hybrid lineup drops the previous S grade, leaving SE and XSE models, both with standard electronic all-wheel drive. Toyota says the new model year will begin reaching U.S. dealerships this fall. items.t: Firefighters contain forklift fire at the Lowe’s Distribution Center
items.x: SUFFOLK, Va. (WAVY) Suffolk Fire and Rescue responded to a fire at the Lowes Distribution Center on Enterprise Drive Thursday. According to officials, units were dispatched to the location at 11:47 a.m. following reports of a commercial structure fire. Upon arrival at 11:54 a.m., firefighters found smoke showing from a trailer docked at a bay door of the warehouse. After investigating, it was determined that a forklift was on fire inside the trailer. The fire was placed under control at 1:12 p.m. While the fire didn't extend into the building, the exterior wall sustained thermal damage. Courtesy: Suffolk Fire & Rescue All occupants evacuated prior to the arrival of fire personnel. No injuries have been reported. items.t: Halloween candy sales are off to a slow start amid high chocolate prices and affordability concerns
items.x: Halloween candy sales are off to a slow start this year as U.S. consumers grapple with high living costs and eye-popping chocolate prices . Halloween candy sales fell 6.7% in the month ending Oct. 17 compared to the same period last year, according to NielsenIQ, a market research firm. Nielsen also noted an 11.7% decline in candy sales in mid-September, erasing the preseason gains that Halloween candy enjoyed the previous two years. Chris Costagli, a vice president and food thought leader at NielsenIQ, said high gas prices have worsened Americans’ concerns about affordability, and that's dampening demand for Halloween treats. As of Friday, the average price of a gallon of regular gasoline in the U.S. was $4.29, up nearly 40% from the prior year. “I think what you’re seeing now is a consumer that’s spending so much additional money on fuel and housing and clothing and food,” Costagli said

items.t: Understanding CPO cars: What does certified pre-owned mean?
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) With new-car prices near record highs, certified pre-owned vehicles (CPOs) offer buyers an affordable alternative to buying new, along with additional inspections and warranty protection. What Does Certified Pre-Owned Mean? If you’re shopping for a car, you’ve likely come across CPO vehicles. But what does that mean exactly, and how do they differ from traditional used cars? A certified pre-owned car is a used vehicle that meets the age, mileage, and condition requirements of a manufacturer or dealer certification program. CPO cars undergo a multipoint inspection and generally include additional warranty coverage, though the coverage and certification standards vary by program. Many CPO vehicles also include benefits such as roadside assistance, access to a loaner vehicle, and trip interruption coverage. items.t: The science and politics behind the panic over ultraprocessed foods
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Ultraprocessed foods have a terrible reputation. Studies have linked them with multiple chronic diseases . Journalists and health influencers characterize them as poison . Some public health experts call for a global halt to producing and consuming them. But the debate around ultraprocessed foods is not nearly as settled as it may seem. As a researcher who studies social movements for healthy and sustainable food, I have been documenting the history of processed foods and examining debates around the science and politics of ultraprocessing . In basic terms, ultraprocessed foods are mass-produced, industrial formulations that use ingredients not typically found in a home kitchen, and that generally contain little to no intact whole foods. items.t: Early voting surges in battleground states as Democrats outpace GOP gains
items.x: Early voting is surging in several key battleground states, giving Democrats hope that their strength in midterm polling could translate into a turnout advantage in November. In North Carolina, more than 1.2 million early ballots have been accepted, a 37 percent increase from the same point leading up to the 2022 midterms, according to an analysis released Friday by Catawba College political scientist Michael Bitzer. That growth — which includes both in-person and mail-in ballots — has been driven by a 47 percent increase among registered Democrats and a 60 percent increase in participation among unaffiliated voters. Early voting among Republicans is up 2.6 percent. Similar patterns are emerging elsewhere, with high turnout especially pronounced in historically Republican-leaning states with competitive Senate races this cycle. items.t: New Reservoir police chief is a familiar face
items.x: JACKSON, Miss. ( WJTV ) Trevell Dixon returned to the Reservoir Police Department as police chief on October 21, 2026. Dixon previously spent 11 years with the department, serving as chief for four of those years. He left in June 2024 to become the police chief at the Jackson-Medgar Wiley Evers International Airport. Dixon said he's excited to be back and looks forward to reconnecting with the community. "It's great to be back home! You never know where God will lead you, so I just follow the path, and this is where He has put me," said Dixon. "I'm forever grateful to the Jackson Municipal Airport Authority for the opportunity to serve as chief during their progressive era and be a part of the great improvements! items.t: Mississippi DEI ban can go into full effect after Fifth Circuit reversal
items.x: JACKSON, Miss. (AP) Portions of a Mississippi ban on diversity, equity and inclusion practices in public schools can go into effect after the U.S. Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals vacated a lower court's ruling that blocked sections of the law from being enforced. The parts of the law in question prevent public schools from requiring diversity training and maintaining DEI-related programs, courses and offices. It also bans public schools from discussing a list of “divisive concepts” related to race, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity and national origin. Public schools that violate the law could lose state funding. The ban passed in April 2025 and is being challenged by a group of educators, students, parents and activists who say the law violates their First and Fourteenth Amendment rights. items.t: A novel mRNA cancer vaccine helps reduce the chances of melanoma patients’ tumors returning
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — A first-of-its-kind cancer vaccine is significantly reducing the chances that melanoma patients’ tumors come back, according to results of a major study released Thursday by drugmakers Moderna and Merck. The vaccine was custom-brewed for each patient to match their tumor. Adding it to a standard post-surgery treatment reduced by 42% the risk of melanoma returning two years after surgery, according to the most advanced study to date of this new strategy for fighting cancer. “The field has been looking for a win and I think this one is a big one,” said Dr. Hussein Tawbi of MD Anderson Cancer Center in Houston, one of the researchers in the international study. The vaccine, called intismeran, is made with the same Nobel Prize-winning mRNA technology that was behind COVID-19 vaccines. items.t: Trump approval hits record low in new survey
items.x: ( The Hill ) President Trump's approval rating hit a record low in a new survey, with just over two weeks until voters decide which party will control Congress next year. The Washington Post-ABC News-Ipsos poll, released Sunday , shows Trump sitting at 33 percent approval. The rating is 4 points lower than a previous poll conducted in July, 8 points lower than at this point last year and lower than at any other time during his first term. Roughly 66 percent of respondents said they disapprove of his job performance, including 52 percent who say they strongly disapprove, according to the survey. Democrats also received more support nationally from likely voters than their Republican counterparts, with 52 percent to 44 percent, respectively. items.x: KNOX COUNTY, Tenn. Per-capita spending fell in 28 states, rose in 16, and stayed the same in California. Massachusetts residents spent more than $900 Massachusetts again led the nation by a wide margin, with residents spending an average of $904 per person in 2024, down slightly from $915 in 2023 but still 43.5% higher than any other state. Spending was second-highest in Virginia at $630 per person and third-highest in Rhode Island at $567. North Dakota residents spent the least, at $51 per person. items.t: West Virginia sees pending house sales drop, market slows
items.x: WEST VIRGINIA (WOWK) Houses aren't flying off the market as fast as before across the United States, and the scene isn't much different in West Virginia. The drastic change of pace is something local real estate brokers have seen since 2021. items.t: Eggs cost more than $10 in Hawaii: Report
items.x: HONOLULU ( KHON ) An increase in costs is easily visible to consumers during their grocery shopping. For Hawaii residents, one item that continues to see sticker shock is the skyrocketing price of eggs. On average, it's now $10.06 to buy a dozen eggs in Honolulu, the Department of Agriculture and Biosecurity, or DAB, announced on Tuesday. According to statistics from DAB's Market Analysis and News Branch, the price of a dozen eggs spiked more than 11 percent in the past year, officials said. The report found that eggs from the U.S. continent increased slightly more than 1 percent, from $7.78 a dozen to $7.87. But local organic eggs saw the highest jump with the average price for a dozen up by 22 percent from the first quarter of 2026 to the second quarter. items.t: The science and politics behind the panic over ultraprocessed foods
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Ultraprocessed foods have a terrible reputation. Studies have linked them with multiple chronic diseases . Journalists and health influencers characterize them as poison . Some public health experts call for a global halt to producing and consuming them. But the debate around ultraprocessed foods is not nearly as settled as it may seem. items.t: Understanding CPO cars: What does certified pre-owned mean?
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) With new-car prices near record highs, certified pre-owned vehicles (CPOs) offer buyers an affordable alternative to buying new, along with additional inspections and warranty protection. What Does Certified Pre-Owned Mean? If you’re shopping for a car, you’ve likely come across CPO vehicles. But what does that mean exactly, and how do they differ from traditional used cars? A certified pre-owned car is a used vehicle that meets the age, mileage, and condition requirements of a manufacturer or dealer certification program. CPO cars undergo a multipoint inspection and generally include additional warranty coverage, though the coverage and certification standards vary by program. Many CPO vehicles also include benefits such as roadside assistance, access to a loaner vehicle, and trip interruption coverage. items.x: ( The Hill ) The Supreme Court on Thursday ruled New Hampshire’s top election official can fully stop voters from using their student IDs when showing up to the polls in the midterms — a request backed by the Republican National Committee (RNC). Founded in 1935 as the Norfolk Unit of Virginia Union University during the Great Depression, the comprehensive urban public institution is "committed to transforming students’ lives through exemplary teaching, research, and service" while fostering a "supportive academic and culturally diverse environment for all," per its official site .
